title: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
abstract: High energy density promised by solid-state batteries requires overcoming fundamental limitations in carrier transport. Although tortuous carrier pathways in high-loading cathodes are often viewed as the dominant bottleneck, we show that interfacial ion and electron transport is an even more critical lever for enhancing energy density in sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries. By enabling partial lithiation at the sulfur-sulfide interface and eliminating the electron-impeding oxidation layer at the sulfur-carbon interface, we achieve high-loading all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery cathodes with areal capacities near 15 mAh cm-2 and sulfur utilization above 90% with a moderate stack pressure of 15-25 MPa. These metrics correspond to projected pouch-cell-level energy densities surpassing 500 Wh kg-1. Fast cycling at 1C retains 82.1% capacity over 500 cycles with Coulombic efficiencies up to 99.9%, and stable cycling is also achieved with a lithium metal anode at 10 MPa instead of the more common Li-In alloy. This work highlights the power of interfacial control within composite cathodes, and demonstrates another approach for designing high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries for next-generation energy storage.

title: Nanostructures strengthen titanium alloys
abstract: Machine learning guides the design of an additively manufactured titanium alloy containing superfine features at the 10 nm scale through controlled martensitic transformation, which achieves an ultimate tensile strength of more than 1.7 GPa and 7.5% uniform elongation.

title: Concurrent atmospheric phenomena amplify precipitation extremes under anthropogenic climate change
abstract: Extreme precipitation events are increasing in many regions. Here the authors discuss how the increasing concurrence of atmospheric phenomena could contribute to these trends under anthropogenic warming.

title: Climate and glacier geometry dominate global glacier–lake interactions
abstract: The contribution of glacial lakes to glacier mass loss is unclear. This work maps global glacial lakes in 2000 and 2020 to quantify changes in number, volume and area, showing that they explain 11 ± 7% of lake-terminating glacier loss, with climate forcing and glacier geometry the dominant factors.

title: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways
abstract:
Abstract
                  Reaching the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a rapid transformation of global energy systems. Yet, energy supply and use exert multiple pressures on ecosystems, human health and natural resources, raising questions about the broader environmental consequences of alternative decarbonization pathways and the resources they require. Here we analyse 24 climate mitigation pathways from three integrated assessment models using a life-cycle perspective. This enables a system-wide comparison of environmental impacts and resource requirements of global final energy provision from 2020 to 2100. We find that deep decarbonization delivers substantial cobenefits for human health and ecosystem quality, but does not systematically reduce pressures on land, water or mineral resource extraction. For metals central to electrification, climate change mitigation ambition primarily reshapes the timing of extraction rather than cumulative volumes. Pathways achieving similar climate targets can impose markedly different environmental and resource pressures, shaping the feasibility and desirability of alternative transitions.

title: Improving compatibility in mixed-matrix membranes
abstract: Mixed-matrix membranes promise to combine the processability of polymers with the transport advantages of porous fillers, yet poor compatibility between the two limits their performance. New research shows that tailoring interfaces between polymers and covalent organic frameworks enables high filler loadings, producing improved membranes for carbon capture.

title: Antireflective bilayer metasurfaces with complete wavefront control
abstract: Antireflection coatings are widely used in optical systems to increase transmission and suppress unwanted reflections by matching the optical impedance across a uniform interface. Applying the same idea to metasurfaces is fundamentally more challenging because their wavefront control relies on arrays of geometrically distinct meta-atoms, presenting as a spatially varying optical impedance. Here we show that vertical integration can overcome this limitation by allowing bilayer meta-atoms to act simultaneously as phase shifters and impedance-matching stacks. By treating meta-atoms as multilayer thin films, we derive a design rule that links the effective refractive indices of two independently patterned layers and identifies antireflective bilayer libraries with full 0-2π transmission phase coverage. We demonstrate the approach with a free-standing TiO2/TiO2 metalens operating at 1,310 nm, which suppresses reflection below that of bare glass while maintaining diffraction-limited focusing. These results establish bilayer metasurfaces as a platform for jointly engineering optical impedance and wavefront response at the meta-atom level.

title: Four-dimensional X-ray nano-holotomography reveals multiscale chemomechanics in composite graphite–silicon battery electrodes
abstract: Linking electrode microstructure to electrochemical performance is essential for optimizing Li-ion batteries. However, this requires mechanistic four-dimensional observations at the ultimate spatiotemporal scales, which remain elusive. Here we demonstrate the use of interrupted-operando synchrotron X-ray nano-holotomography combined with digital volume correlation to track chemomechanical dynamics at both particle (local) and electrode (averaged) scales. Quantitative scale-bridging image analysis is applied to composite graphite-silicon electrodes during their electrochemical formation cycle. Our findings reveal that local ionic diffusion properties, graphite particle morphology and position in the electrode, distance to silicon clusters, surface contact with the liquid electrolyte solution, and mechanical deformations all directly affect local electrochemical activity and irreversibility, although these parameters are not equally important. In particular, we identify fast ionic diffusion channels that play a key role and counterbalance intrinsic depth-dependent reaction heterogeneities arising from ionic and electronic diffusion limitations. The various structural factors that determine the electrochemical performance of composite graphite-silicon electrodes in Li-ion batteries beyond ensemble properties are classified using a scale of influence, providing a practical framework for the optimization of materials and electrode manufacturing.

title: Tracking local chemomechanics in graphite–silicon composite electrodes
abstract: Operando 4D imaging reveals how local ionic pathways govern activity in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

title: Isolable crystalline oxoboranes
abstract: Oxoboranes, compounds featuring a central dicoordinate boron atom engaged in a B–O triple bond, have long been regarded as highly reactive and are typically observed only as transient species. Although attempts to synthesize them date back to the 1960s, their isolation in the condensed phase has proved challenging. Now, two independent studies describe the isolation of neutral and cationic oxoboranes derived from related diboracumulenes.

title: Plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots for crop disease management
abstract: Plant fungal pathogens in crops can lead to substantial economic losses and pose a severe threat to food security. To tackle wheat Fusarium head blight, a devastating disease infecting wheat crops, an effective antifungal strategy using plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots has been developed.

title: O6-type layered oxides for sustainable high-energy battery cathodes
abstract: Cobalt-free cathodes are vital for green energy but suffer from structural instability. Here the authors report a unique O6-type framework that stabilizes oxygen redox for exceptional cycling durability.

title: Assessing public preferences for reforming water subsidy eligibility rules in Delhi
abstract: Sinha and co-authors survey 728 residents of Delhi about water subsidy design options to understand which eligibility rules people consider most acceptable and fair. Although the study finds support for subsidies when water use remains below a threshold as well as an income-based subsidy, preferences differ sharply across population groups, making reform politically and practically challenging.

title: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations
abstract:
Abstract
                  Electrocyclizations are a fundamental class of pericyclic transformations that can proceed through thermal or photochemical pathways. Although thermal electrocyclizations have been implicated in numerous biosynthetic pathways, there are few examples of enzyme-mediated processes, and the structural requirements for efficient catalysis are poorly understood. Here we develop an artificial photoenzyme for 6π-electrocyclizations (PhotoElectroCyclase PEC1.3) by introducing ten mutations into a recently reported [2 + 2]-cyclase. PEC1.3 processes diverse acrylanilide substrates with exceptional yields, regiocontrol and stereocontrol. A 1.3-Å crystal structure shows the substrate ideally positioned for energy transfer from a genetically programmed benzophenone triplet sensitizer. Interestingly, hydrogen-bonding interactions that were critical to [2 + 2] cyclase activity were abandoned during evolution of PEC1.3. Instead, the enzyme employs a network of hydrophobic interactions to constrain the substrate into a reactive geometry for selective antarafacial electrocyclization, allowing PEC1.3 to retain activity at cryogenic temperatures where appreciable molecular motions are frozen out. This example of controlled reaction outcomes without polar substrate–enzyme contacts points towards selective conversions of substrates lacking functional handles.

title: Designing solar panels for realistic end-of-life scenarios
abstract: The rapid growth of photovoltaics is generating vast waste streams, a portion of which flows to regions where recycling is unregulated. Solar panel design criteria do not account for these end-of-life realities, creating global asymmetry in environmental burdens. This Comment proposes research directions beyond material substitution to address these design gaps.

title: Mapping safety zones as lithium-ion batteries degrade to improve safety
abstract:
Abstract
                  Battery safety is crucial for reliable system operation, yet current safety assessments remain largely based on fixed thresholds that do not evolve with battery degradation, leading to suboptimal operational decisions. Here we show that safety performance evolves as batteries degrade, requiring safety management to adapt throughout battery life. We introduce a physics-based framework that characterizes safety performance through evolving safety zones and boundaries linked to the initiation and severity of thermal runaway. Using a comprehensive model that integrates multiple degradation and failure mechanisms, we demonstrate how the safety landscape of a commercial 21700 cell shifts under different degradation conditions, potentially resulting in false negatives under existing management strategies. We further show that degradation pathways strongly affect safety characteristics, causing different safety outcomes despite similar capacity fade and exposing the limitations of capacity-based health assessments. Finally, we map possible degradation-to-failure pathways and highlight diagnostics and modeling needs for lifelong safety management.

title: Genetic control of active matter
Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Interfacial void formation during discharge limits the practical performance of lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here we show that introducing an egg-box topography at the Li/Li

                    PS
                    5

                    −2

                    at 60 °C without cell failure. Under these conditions, it does not completely eliminate void formation but suppresses void growth and associated voltage polarization. Consequently, it sustains discharge profiles derived from the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, representing realistic electric vehicle driving demands, whereas non-contoured interfaces fail rapidly. A full cell with a thin contoured solid electrolyte retains this advantage over its non-contoured counterpart. Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.

title: Depth-robust super-resolution nanofabrication for 3D mesoscopic photonic structures
abstract: Mesoscopic optical systems underpin photonic interconnects, on-chip metrology, quantum computing and miniature microscopy, but monolithic integration of these components is currently limited by fabrication methodologies that only offer limited depth control. At depth, the super-resolution performance of stimulated-emission-depletion direct laser writing is hindered by absorption, scattering and aberrations arising from refractive index mismatch that distort the depletion focus. Here we show that maintaining axial alignment between the excitation and depletion fields overcomes this limitation. We implement this principle through an axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion direct laser writing strategy that keeps the depletion zone aligned with the Gaussian excitation focus. Axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion produces isolated lines 56.2 nm wide and resolves gratings with a 150-nm period and a 110-nm linewidth at a 160 μm depth with a numerical aperture of 1.27, while maintaining a 167.3-nm linewidth at 1,400 μm, using a numerical aperture of 1.1. We use axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion to fabricate axially extended mesoscopic optical systems, including 4f systems, vortex phase plates, miniaturized objectives and microlens arrays.

title: Chiral cobalt-catalysed electrochemical enantioselective C–P coupling via phosphinoyl radicals
abstract: The stereocontrolled generation and utilization of phosphinoyl radicals for asymmetric synthesis remain a formidable challenge, stemming from their transient nature and stereochemical unpredictability. Here we show an electrocatalytic strategy that addresses this longstanding challenge via the merger of asymmetric Lewis acid catalysis with anodic oxidation to enable highly enantioselective C–P bond formation. Through a Lewis acid-coupled electron-transfer mechanism, the chiral cobalt catalyst directs radical generation while creating a confined chiral environment that governs stereoselective bond formation. This integrated platform enables intermolecular coupling under mild conditions, providing efficient access to a diverse array of P(V)-stereogenic compounds with excellent enantioselectivity (up to 99% enantiomeric excess) and enabling synthetic diversification. Mechanistic studies, including electrochemical analysis, radical-clock experiments and density functional theory calculations, corroborate the proposed pathway and elucidate the origin of stereocontrol. This work bridges electrochemistry, asymmetric catalysis and radical chemistry, expanding the synthetic toolkit for constructing phosphorus stereocentres.

title: Encoding information into an embroidery of topological defects in liquid crystals
abstract: A photopatterned alignment layer with a periodic lattice of vortices acts as a substrate for pinned defect lines in a liquid crystal. These topological defect lines can be rearranged by optical manipulation into a vast number of states that can store information.

title: Construction of benzochalcogenaboroles via single-atom editing of boracycles
abstract: Benzoxaborole is arguably the most important boron-based pharmacophore. Since Torssell's 1957 synthesis, hundreds of benzoxaborole derivatives have emerged, including US Food and Drug Administration-approved tavaborole and crisaborole. However, while peripheral modifications are well studied, synthetic challenges leave isoelectronic core modification less explored, despite its potential to enhance potency and reveal unexplored functions. Here we report a challenging ring expansion of benzoboretenes with elemental chalcogens, where benzoboretenes act as a 'diradical reservoir'. This synthetic protocol provides a versatile and modular platform for accessing three previously inaccessible classes of benzochalcogenaborole skeletons, in which the oxygen atom of the benzoxaborole core is formally replaced with Se, S or SO2. Preliminary biological evaluation reveals that this 'O-to-S' modification confers potent ferroptosis-inhibitory activity. Furthermore, its excellent functional group compatibility enables structure-activity optimization, leading to a 20-fold increase in cellular potency. This research not only expands the chemical space of boron-containing pharmacophores via single-atom ring expansion but also exemplifies how skeletal editing can unlock biological activities.

title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics1,2. Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively2, rare variation remains relatively unexplored1. Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency < 0.0001%) putative loss-of-function variants, implicated 17 genes with large effects on height ranging from -17cm (ACAN) to +11 cm (FBN1) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes (TET1, DTL and IGF2BP2) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects-often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes-and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization.

title: Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro
abstract: Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1-7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

title: Micelle-Driven MOF Degradation for Enhanced Cargo Release in Micromotors
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored as cargo-delivery platforms, yet efficient release of the encapsulated cargo remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that anionic surfactant micelles actively destabilize the HKUST-1 MOF framework through Cu2+ extraction, converting a typically undesired degradation process into a mechanism for enhanced cargo release. Complementary mechanistic studies reveal that this process depends on surfactant self-assembly and on the accessibility and coordination environment of the metal nodes. The resulting framework destabilization greatly enhances the release of different cargos from HKUST-1. This mechanistic concept is subsequently translated into tubular MOF-based micromotors by confining SDS within an agarose matrix inside the micromotor cavity. Local surfactant release generates a micelle-rich microenvironment that promotes MOF degradation and cargo release while limiting bulk surfactant exposure and reducing the cytotoxic effects associated with free surfactant under the tested conditions. The resulting platform integrates micelle-mediated MOF disassembly with spatially confined micromotor delivery, providing a strategy for localized and enhanced cargo release from MOF-based dynamic systems.

title: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP
abstract: Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

title: Dynamic Li+/Na+-Exchanging Interphase Stabilizes High-Voltage Ni-Rich Cathodes for 557 Wh kg–1 Lithium Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-voltage operation of Ni-rich layered cathodes LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) accelerates electrolyte decomposition at the surface and destabilizes the bulk lattice with oxygen loss. Conventional strategies for regulating the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) commonly suppress persistent parasitic reactions at Ni-rich cathode surfaces, but increase interfacial polarization and offer limited protection against structural degradation in the bulk. Here, a dynamic interphase is constructed by coating NCM811 with a Na+-based solid-electrolyte Na3Zr2Si2PO12 (NZSP). During cycling, Li+/Na+ exchange transforms the NZSP layer into a fast Li+ conducting interphase LixNa3–xZr2Si2PO12 (L-NZSP), while the Na+ ions are incorporated into the NCM811 lattice. The L-NZSP suppresses parasitic reactions at high charging voltages. Meanwhile, the incorporated Na+ ions provide pillar-like support for the layered framework, stabilizing the oxygen lattice and mitigating chemo-mechanical degradation. Consequently, the modified cathode retains 80% capacity after 511 cycles at 4.7 V and enables a 4 Ah pouch cell to deliver 557 Wh kg–1 with 80.5% retention over 118 cycles. This work demonstrates Li+/Na+-exchanging interphase as an effective strategy to couple interfacial protection with bulk lattice reinforcement for high-voltage Ni-rich cathodes in high-energy lithium batteries.

title: An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals
abstract: Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30-40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4-32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7-42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

title: Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker-ejection fraction-although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome.

title: Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids
abstract: Colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1. Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling2,3, establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm2 V-1 s-1 and submillimetre drift lengths-far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection.

title: Asymmetric Partial Hydrogenation of Quinazolines: Overcoming Catalyst Poisoning by a Robust yet Active Solo-Coordination-Vacant Ir(III) Pincer Catalyst
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catalytic asymmetric partial hydrogenation of quinazolines to afford enantioenriched 3,4-dihydroquinazolines, a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry, is a long-standing challenge likely due to product-induced catalyst deactivation. Here, we report a robust yet highly reactive solo-coordination-vacant Ir(III) pincer catalyst being capable of overcoming this poisoning challenge. This catalyst enables the asymmetric partial hydrogenation of a broad range of quinazolines, affording 3,4-dihydroquinazolines in high yields (up to 98%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). In a dedicated catalyst-loading study, the loading could be reduced to 0.001 mol % (10 ppm, TON = 38,000). Mechanistic investigations, including NMR spectroscopic detection of a key Ir–H intermediate and base-dependence studies, support a catalytic cycle proceeding through a well-defined Ir(III)-hydride species and suggest that an alkali-metal-assisted pathway is unlikely to be dominant.

title: Local Molecular Motions Encode Time-Resolved Infrared Spectra of Proteins
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy probes protein dynamics over time scales spanning more than 10 orders of magnitude, yet the molecular motions underlying the observed kinetic signatures have remained elusive. Here we combine transient infrared spectroscopy with nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to establish a direct connection between experimental relaxation times and local structural motions. Studying single-domain allosteric proteins, we find that inter-residue contact distances provide the structural representation that most faithfully reproduces the experimental dynamics. Correlation analysis identifies localized networks of coordinated contacts that mediate long-range coupling between secondary-structure elements. The characteristic time scales of these contact networks quantitatively match the experimentally observed relaxation processes, enabling each kinetic step to be assigned to a specific molecular motion. Applied to allosteric signal propagation in PDZ3 and photoinduced perturbation of the binding pocket of PDZ2 or a ligand binding to PDZ2, this framework provides an atomistic picture of hierarchical protein relaxation and establishes a general framework for connecting transient infrared spectroscopy with the molecular mechanisms of protein dynamics.

title: Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons
abstract: Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.

title: Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide
                    1–4
                    , yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

title: A continental dilemma: Is centralized or decentralized renewable hydrogen cheaper?
abstract: Hydrogen is a strong candidate on the path towards the decarbonization of the transportation, energy, and industry sectors. In addition to being a well-known element, hydrogen is mainly produced from fossil fuels, with the renewable production chain still requiring development. In this context, this work evaluates the technical and economic potential of hydrogen production using solar photovoltaic (PV) energy and electricity purchased from the Brazilian grid, and evaluates two layouts: (i) centralized production of solar PV energy and hydrogen at the same site and (ii) decentralized production of energy and hydrogen powered by the Brazilian interconnected grid (SIN). The use of PV energy is found to decrease the levelized cost of hydrogen ( L C O H ) when compressed, from 14.00 USD / kg to 13.24 USD / kg in the centralized case and to 9.11 USD / kg in the decentralized case. However, a system powered only by P V energy had a cost of 18.23 USD / kg ; this corroborates the fact that the highest verified cost is from the purchase of energy from the grid. From the analysis of the design parameters, increasing the electrolyzer power and the size of the PV field reduces the L C O H , due to the economies of scale of both pieces of equipment. The optimization shows that it is possible to reach an L C O H for compressed hydrogen of 9.89 USD / kg for the centralized system and values of 5.88 USD / kg for the decentralized system.

title: In Situ High-Pressure NMR Reveals Pressure-Defect Generation in Aluminum Acetylacetonate toward Integrated Optical Response
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive luminescent materials featuring real-time pressure-response with persistent memory effects hold considerable promise for advanced photonic computing. However, most pressure-memory behavior depends on triggered irreversible phase transitions, which hinders the integration of reversible optical sensing. Synergistic pressure treatment and defect generation serve as an effective approach that ensures the phase-transition-free structure while affording excellent photoluminescence (PL) performance. In this work, we employ pressure-defect generation strategy in aluminum acetylacetonate that effectively integrates short-term pressure response with long-term history memory. Notably, the PL wavelength acts as a digital readout across 476–486 nm, alongside an intensity-based analog signal below 4 GPa. Upon crossing this threshold, the response further embeds memory states dependent on pressure history. In situ high-pressure nuclear magnetic resonance (HP-NMR) measurements reveal, from both static and dynamic perspectives, the progressive deepening of pressure-induced local responses within the molecular framework, from ligand-associated modulation to Al–O coordination perturbation. This establishes a two-regime pressure-defect generation pathway: reversible structural distortion induces electronic-state defects, whereas partially trapped severe distortion may generate radical defects. Our work not only highlights the unique capability of local dynamic probing for the design of pressure-responsive materials, but also broadens the horizons of single-material multifunctional information-processing systems.

title: Cross-Linked Halide Networks for Lithium Superionic Conduction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) hold great promise for next-generation energy storage owing to their high safety and energy density, yet their performance critically depends on solid electrolytes (SEs) with high ionic conductivity and structural robustness. Mixed-anion chemistry, exemplified by the Cl/O system, has emerged as an effective approach for designing halide-based superionic conductors, where partial oxygen incorporation distorts the regular halide framework and enhances Li+ mobility. However, we herein show that uncontrolled oxygen incorporation is prone to generate nonbridging oxygens (NBOs), which can hinder Li+ migration via Coulombic interactions. To address this, we develop a polyanion-assisted cross-linking strategy that promotes more bridging-oxygen (BOs) coordination and less formation of NBOs. This yields a highly disordered, frustrated energy landscape conducive to efficient Li+ percolation and rapid ion migration. As an example, PO43– polyanion cross-linked ZrClx halide networks (ZrCl4-xLi3PO4) are developed and exhibit ionic conductivities up to 2.8 × 10–3 S cm–1 at 30 °C, competitive with state-of-the-art rare-metal halides, while maintaining >10–3 S cm–1 after humid exposure (5% RH, 12 h). ASSBs incorporating these electrolytes demonstrate stable cycling not only under elevated temperatures (55 °C) but also under high voltages (4.6 V). These findings identify NBO environments as potential transport inhibitors and establish inorganic cross-linking topochemistry as a structural design principle for robust, high-performance, halide solid electrolytes.

title: Localization of micron-scale lithium polysulfide-rich phases causes anode heterogeneity in lean-electrolyte lithium–sulfur batteries
abstract: Kim et al. reveal that concentrated lithium polysulfides form micron-scale, salt-anion-deficient phases in lean-electrolyte lithium–sulfur batteries, promoting heterogeneous interphase formation and uneven lithium deposition. Fragmenting these phases with a lithium iodide additive improves anode uniformity and cycling stability, establishing spatial electrolyte heterogeneity as a key consideration for practical batteries.

abstract: Direct electrolysis of seawater and chloride-rich brines is widely pursued as a route to hydrogen that bypasses desalination, with intense effort directed at catalysts and membranes that suppress chlorine chemistry....

title: Synergistic high negative pressure enables direct lithium crystallization from raw salt-lake brine
abstract: Solar-driven separation–crystallization pump achieves direct lithium crystallization from raw salt-lake brine by synergistic evaporation negative pressure and capillary negative pressure.

title: Molar-mass- and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules via iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition of α-substituted acrylates
abstract: Free-radical polymerization of simple vinyl monomers enables mass production of widely used polymers, but typically affords products that are poorly defined in molecular size and monomer sequence. Despite advances in precision polymerization, chain growth remains probabilistic, precluding molar-mass- and sequence-defined macromolecules. Here we report photoredox decarboxylative addition of bulky α-substituted acrylates, which enables quantitative addition of single building blocks without oligomerization. The α-acyl radical generated upon acrylate addition is irreversibly deactivated by rapid electron transfer within the photocatalytic cycle. A C(sp3)-centred radical is regenerated only after conversion of the terminal ester into a carboxylic acid and subsequent photoredox decarboxylation. Iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition yields vinyl macromolecules comprising residues identical to the repeat units of conventional vinyl polymers, without inseparable oligomeric impurities. Aperiodic vinyl-residue sequences can be assembled rapidly in continuous-flow reactors, offering a route towards fully automated synthesis of synthetic macromolecules and exploration of their sequence-dependent functions. A light-driven reaction scheme links a carboxylic acid to a vinyl compound through a decarboxylated radical intermediate. The resulting product retains the substituents from both starting materials. Iterative single-unit addition and deprotection yield mass-defined and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules. Below, examples of mass-defined and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules illustrate the products: the mass-defined example has a repeated phenyl-bearing unit, while the sequence-defined example contains phenyl, methoxy-substituted phenyl, and fluorine-substituted phenyl groups.

title: Metal-meets-acid: catalysis for lignin depolymerization
abstract: Lignin, the most abundant renewable aromatic biopolymer on Earth, represents a highly promising feedstock for sustainable chemicals and biofuels. However, the efficient catalytic depolymerization of lignin remains challenging due to its robust interunit linkages and the tendency of reactive intermediates to form irreversible condensates. Acid-metal bifunctional catalysis has emerged as an effective strategy to address these challenges, as the acid sites and metal sites promote bond cleavage while stabilizing intermediates to suppress recondensation. This review focuses on the cooperative mechanisms between acidic sites and metal catalysts during lignin valorization. We examine the specific catalytic functions of these dual active sites, discuss how their bifunctional catalysis enables efficient depolymerization, and summarize recent advances in catalyst design. In the end, we provide perspectives on tuning the spatial distribution and matching degree of dual active sites, offering potential directions for the future development of effective lignin conversion catalysts.

title: Climate warming amplifies metabolic imbalance across global lakes
abstract: Lake metabolism remains a critical yet poorly constrained component of the global carbon cycle. Here we integrate satellite observations, climate reanalysis data, free-water measurements derived metabolic estimates and machine-learning approaches to quantify lake metabolism across more than 4000 lakes from 2003 to 2024. We show that global lakes are overwhelmingly net heterotrophic, with ecosystem respiration (ER) exceeding gross primary production (GPP) in approximately 95% of lakes, generating a global metabolic imbalance equivalent to ∼2 Pg C yr−1. Temperature is the dominant control on metabolic variability, and warming stimulates ER more strongly than GPP across most climatic regions. Consequently, climate warming is projected to intensify both the annual mean and intra-annual variability of GPP and ER, leading to an 11% more negative annual net ecosystem production by the end of this century (−2.03 to − 2.26 Pg C yr−1). These findings highlight lake metabolism as an important component of carbon-climate feedbacks.

title: A Bowl-Shaped B,N-Tetraquinane Organic Super-Reductant
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing a stable molecular reductant with exceptionally strong reducing power remains highly challenging. In this work, we synthesized and characterized a bowl-shaped B–N tetraquinane in a single high-yield step. Cyclic voltammetry reveals a reduction potential of −3.2 V vs Fc/Fc+, a new record among organic reductants. This super-reductant enables [3 + 2] cycloadditions with ketones and imines, dearomatization of phthalazine, cleavage of strong C–Si bonds, direct reduction–borylation of fluorobenzene, deoxygenative coupling of nitrosobenzene, and ring-opening C–C coupling of aromatics into polyenes. Computational studies support its synthetic pathway, ring strain, high reactivity, and remarkably negative reduction potential. These findings demonstrate how three-dimensional topological strain can transform a boron-based dianion into a powerful reagent for reductive reactions and demanding bond activations.

title: Photoinduced Eosin Y Self-Disproportionation Enables Reactivity beyond Direct Excited-State Electron Transfer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photoredox catalysis is commonly governed by the redox properties of the initially excited photocatalyst, which can limit the activation of difficult-to-oxidize alkenes. Here, we identify photoinduced self-disproportionation of neutral eosin Y (EH2) as an alternative activation pathway. In fluorinated-alcohol media, specific hydrogen-bonding interactions stabilize a minor population of the visible-light-absorbing EH2_acid tautomer. Following excitation and intersystem crossing, triplet EH2 undergoes intermolecular hydrogen-atom transfer with ground-state EH2 to generate the complementary radicals EH• and EH3•. Time-resolved spectroscopy shows that the alkene substrate does not measurably intercept excited EH2 but instead reacts with the secondary radical EH•, thereby separating photon absorption from substrate activation. Fluorinated alcohols further couple this radical-pair chemistry to productive C–C bond formation, as illustrated by highly selective polyene cyclizations. These findings establish photocatalyst self-disproportionation as a distinct mechanistic pathway that generates secondary reactive species whose reactivity is not accessible via direct excited-state electron transfer.

title: A Cu-Modified Layered Thiostannate for Selective Pb Capture from Strongly Acidic Media
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Layered metal sulfide ion exchangers are powerful platforms for soft-metal capture, but their application in strongly acidic environments requires framework stability while preserving accessible ion-exchange pathways. Here, we introduce a new series of Cu-modified SnS2-derived layered chalcogenides, AMS-8 (A = Na, K, Rb, Cs), featuring labile interlayer alkali metal ions. NMS-8 (Na1.13Cu1.32Sn3.34S8·xH2O) demonstrates that Cu+ can be incorporated into the SnS2-derived AMS layered motif without disrupting the fundamental architecture. Upon acid exposure, NMS-8 undergoes Na+/H+ exchange and interlayer contraction, showing low Sn leaching in 6 M H2SO4 but substantial Sn dissolution in 6 M HCl after prolonged exposure, despite persistent powder X-ray diffraction reflections of the layered phase. NMS-8 can rapidly capture Pb2+ from water, achieving near-complete removal within 20 s under dilute conditions, a Sips-fitted capacity of 178.2 ± 12.4 mg g–1 (regression standard error), and high selectivity against common competing cations. Structural characterization supports preservation of the lamellar network and a proposed structural model featuring Cu+ displaced off-center within a distorted octahedral framework environment. In an acid mine drainage simulant, NMS-8 selectively removes Pb, Cd, and Cu under acidic multicomponent conditions while retaining its layered structure. Local structural characterization of NMS-8@Pb reveals a spatially heterogeneous Pb distribution within individual crystallites that is not appropriately described by a simple homogeneous interlayer exchange model and is consistent with local structural reorganization during Pb2+ uptake. These results highlight Cu-modified layered thiostannates as promising platforms for rapid, selective soft-metal capture, with substantial resistance to concentrated sulfuric acid and Pb retention dependent on the leaching medium.

title: Advances in Synthetic Methodologies for Isotopic Labeling of Organic Molecules
abstract: Abstract Radioactive and stable isotopes are essential tools in the discovery and development of new agrochemical and pharmaceutical molecules. Consequently, the body of research focused on developing novel synthetic methodologies for isotope incorporation into bioactive molecules continues to grow. Progress in this field has largely been driven by innovative catalytic methods, including late-stage functionalization (LSF) methods like hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE), carbon isotope exchange (CIE), molecular skeletal editing, biocatalysis, and other labeling approaches. These methods enable efficient and sustainable site-specific introduction of isotopes into bioactive molecules at late stages of synthesis. Given the broad applications across various scientific fields, this comprehensive, critical, and accessible review summarizing diverse isotope labeling methodologies will be of great benefit to researchers in academia as well as professionals in the pharmaceutical and agrochemical industries. This review focuses primarily on recent developments in catalytic methodologies for incorporating 2H, 3H, 11C, 13C, 14C, 15N, 18O, 18F, and 34S isotopes into organic molecules, along with a brief overview of well-established methods reported in this field.

title: Bioinspired Ångström-Scale Coupling of Reductive Centers in Covalent Organic Frameworks Drives Efficient Photocatalytic Oxygen Reduction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The photocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is crucial for solar-to-chemical energy conversion but faces challenges from weak oxygen adsorption and slow kinetics. Inspired by the spatially cooperative multimetal centers in natural enzymes, we develop a strategy of Å-scale spatial coupling of reductive centers in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Ortho-amino-functionalized COFs were constructed with catalytic pockets that position multiple acceptors within subnanometer proximity, creating coupled reductive centers for cooperative O2 adsorption and multielectron relay. The optimal framework, with a model-derived separation of approximately 3.3 Å between reductive centers, achieves a hydrogen peroxide production rate of 4.10 mmol g–1 h–1 in pure water under visible light without sacrificial agents, along with a high apparent quantum yield of 19.2% at 450 nm. Practical viability is confirmed through operation in diverse water sources and continuous-flow systems. Moreover, the enhanced ORR activity accelerates oxidative coupling of benzylamine derivatives, showing over 80% conversion for 12 analogues. Experimental and theoretical analyses indicate that the confined neighboring sites enhance O2 adsorption and activation, stabilize •OOH intermediates, and promote the two-electron reduction pathway. This work establishes convergent multicenter coupling as a foundational design principle, unlocking new avenues for the rational creation of high-performance photocatalysts in sustainable chemistry.

title: Excitonic electrically tunable metaatoms for visible light
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Phase-gradient metasurfaces shape optical wavefronts through arrays of optical nanoantennas acting as metaatoms. While dynamic tunability forms a major frontier in this area, direct electrical switching of metaatoms operating in the visible has remained challenging. Here, we present an exciton-based metaatom that is electrically tunable and operates in the visible. Its function originates from an excitonic absorption band of a dedoped conjugated polymer, which together with low background permittivity induces optical metallicity in the visible. This allows anisotropic nanostructures to exhibit polarization-dependent optical response through localized surface exciton-polariton resonances, rather than plasmons or dielectric Mie resonances. This function can be fully switched off through reversible doping by small bias potentials, which turns off the exciton-induced metallicity. Our study details the mechanism of these metaatoms and demonstrates their use in electrically tunable phase-gradient metasurfaces for visible light, including erasable and rewritable holograms. This work thereby establishes a class of electrically switchable exciton-based metaatoms and expands the design space of dynamic visible metaoptics.

title: Achieving high-yield and pilot-scale synthesis of nano graphene oxide via photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The high-yield synthesis of nanoscale graphene oxide is increasingly critical, yet widespread scalable implementation of top-down methods remains hindered by low efficiency. Here, we report a highly efficient, scaled-up approach coupling photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage to fragment micron-sized graphene oxide into nanoscale flakes. Irradiation induces nanoscale holes on the graphene oxide basal plane, causing rapid fragmentation upon hydrogen peroxide treatment. This yields nanoscale graphene oxide (20 to 60 nanometers) featuring an sp2-hybridized carbon core and carboxylic acid-rich edges. The material exhibits exceptional stability against thermal ripening, prolonged solar irradiation, and chemical reduction. Achieving an 85 ± 5 % conversion yield, the practical scalability of this process is demonstrated using a pilot-scale device with a projected annual capacity of 0.52 tons of powder. This work provides a route for the pilot-scale production of high-performance nanoscale graphene oxide materials.

title: Giant nonlinear optical responses in the visible via lattice-controlled cascade amplification of photon avalanche
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The photon avalanche effect exhibits a large optical nonlinear response, which is crucial for advancement in super-resolution imaging and optical sensing. However, photon avalanche systems with nonlinearity exceeding 100 remain confined to a single band in the near-infrared region, where standard detectors have low sensitivity. Here, we show that a cascade amplified photon avalanche strategy via lattice reconstruction to address these limitations. Introducing lutetium substitution into the host lattice enhances interionic energy exchange and cross-relaxation, activating multiple visible emission channels of holmium and erbium ions with amplified nonlinearities. A nonlinearity order of up to 560 is achieved in ~216 nm nanoparticles, while 43 nm nanoparticles retain a nonlinearity of 183 and enable super-resolution microscopy with 28 nm lateral resolution. We further demonstrate multi-color super-resolution microscopy and sub-cellular bioimaging. Benefiting from high detection efficiency and flexible wavelength selection, cascade amplified photon avalanche nanoprobes are promising for ultrasensitive sensing and super-resolution lithography beyond optical imaging.

title: Low-pressure operation of all-solid-state batteries enabled by an organic electrode
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: All-solid-state batteries offer enhanced safety and high energy density. However, their practical application is challenged by the need for high external pressures, often tens of MPa, to maintain intimate solid–solid contact and preserve ion/electron percolation pathways during cycling. In this work, we demonstrate that low-modulus, low-hardness, creep-compliant, low-strain organic active materials that readily deform in response to external pressures and microstructural changes enable stable cell operation under low stack pressures. Using bis-tetraaminobenzoquinone (TAQ) as a model compound, we show its low modulus (8.4–15.3 GPa), low hardness (0.33–0.76 GPa), and moderate creep compliance (m = 0.038–0.073), quantified by nanoindentation of both pristine and lithiated TAQ, enable adaptive deformability under low stack pressures. TAQ-based solid-state cells achieve stable cycling and promising rate performance at external pressures as low as 1 MPa, retaining 80.3% capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5C. Operando and post-mortem electron microscopy reveal that TAQ electrodes maintain high structural integrity at pressures as low as 0.2 MPa. These findings establish a materials design strategy centered on mechanically adaptive materials to enable solid-state battery operation under practically relevant pressure conditions.

title: Chip-scale narrow-linewidth optical parametric oscillators
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Continuous-wave-pumped optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) provide an exciting avenue to generate coherent radiation at wavelength regions that are difficult to reach by traditional semiconductor optical amplifiers. However, attaining ultra-narrow linewidth operation in OPOs requires pump lasers with exceptional purity to begin with. Here, we demonstrate an integrated Kerr nonlinear OPO featuring an integrated external cavity based on ultralow-loss silicon nitride that results in a continuous-wave signal with a 15-fold intrinsic linewidth reduction compared to the pump, down to 10 Hz. Our numerical analysis indicates that the intrinsic linewidth can be reduced below the Schawlow-Townes limit of a single-cavity OPO depending on the feedback length and strength of the external cavity. Utilizing an integrated erbium-doped waveguide amplifier, we further demonstrate sub-Hz intrinsic linewidth coherent oscillation. These results establish an effective pathway towards chip-scale ultra-coherent light sources with high power and broad wavelength tunability, opening new opportunities for high-precision optical sensing and detection.

title: Carbon-neutral algal bloom management via algal organic matter repurposing
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Algal organic matter (AOM) has been considered a typical pollutant in algal bloom waters, conventionally managed through flocculation-flotation processes with high carbon footprints. This study presents a paradigm shift by redefining AOM as a functional crosslinker and developing an AOM-induced self-driven flotation (A-SDF) strategy. The approach utilizes active groups in AOM (-COOH/-OH) coordinated with trace amounts of metal coagulants to construct multilevel gel flocs with Al2O3/FeO(OH) crystalline phases. Remarkably, these flocs not only capture algal cells but also activate dissolved oxygen (DO), inducing DO enrichment-interfacial gas nucleation behavior (DOE-IGNB) and leading to microbubbles (MBs) formation at the floc interface under mild turbulence. The process achieved efficient removal of algal cells (82–95%), turbidity (86–95%), and AOM (45–79%) within 2 min without external aeration. Compared with existing technologies, the carbon footprint, treatment time, and economic cost were reduced by 66.08–96.90%, 71.67–96.00%, and 50.55–97.67%, respectively, while residual metal concentrations remained well below drinking water standards. Density functional theory calculations confirmed strong DO adsorption by tetrahedral AlO4/FeO4 lattices as the molecular mechanism driving DOE-IGNB. By repurposing AOM as a resource and activating endogenous DO, this work provides a universal carbon-neutral pathway for sustainable algal bloom management worldwide.

title: Lithium coordination compound reduces nephrotoxicity and enhances therapeutic effects in Alzheimer’s disease female mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lithium holds therapeutic promise for Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet its clinical application is hindered by a narrow therapeutic range and nephrotoxicity. We rationally design a lithium coordination compound, BuLiPro, chelated with endogenous butyrate and proline. Single-crystal diffraction and mass-spectrometry confirm its crystal structure and solution-state coordination, while spectroscopic assays verify an identity distinct from free lithium. Compared with lithium carbonate, BuLiPro achieves improved plasma exposure, slower clearance, and 61.6%-higher brain lithium accumulation at 48 h in rats. It yields lower renal cytotoxicity and in vivo kidney injury, and inhibits glycogen synthase kinase-3β over three-fold more potently. In female AD model mice, BuLiPro attenuates tau and amyloid-β pathologies to a greater extent and rescues cognition. This coordination-based strategy enhances lithium’s central bioavailability and reduces systemic toxicity, offering a framework for the development of next-generation lithium therapeutics.

title: Restoring global forest canopy structure complexity for potential local warming mitigation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Forests are natural coolers of Earth’s land surface temperatures. However, the local biophysical cooling provided by forest is often constrained by trade-off between expanding forest areas and competing land uses, which has challenged both policymakers and scientists for decades. Restoring forest canopy structural complexity has long been viewed as a promising nature-based strategy to alleviate this constrain, yet its effectiveness and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood at the global scale. Using satellite-derived land surface temperature and LiDAR-based measurements of canopy structures, we show that increasing canopy structural complexity enhances local land surface cooling across most global forests (90.0%). The cooling potential of vertical canopy complexity consistently exceeds that of horizontal crown cover density, which has been long overlooked. By aligning canopy structure complexity of managed forests with that of nearby intact forests, we estimate a potential reduction of 0.25 ± 0.001 °C in local land surface temperature globally. Our findings provide insights into strengthening the climate regulation of existing forests through the ecological restoration of forest canopy structure complexity and suggest a space-efficient management strategy that complements, rather than substitutes for, forest conservation and afforestation.

title: Observationally-constrained CMIP6 projections of a snow-free Northern Hemisphere
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Northern Hemisphere snow cover retreat poses substantial climate risks, but large uncertainties in Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) hinder accurate projections of future evolution. We develop a monthly emergent constraint based on historical warming trends, which strongly correlate with ablation-season (May–October) snow cover loss. This constraint reduces inter-model variance by 17.0–58.4% under different emission scenarios and rectifies raw CMIP6 snow-loss biases. Constrained projections reveal that under the higher-emission scenario (SSP5-8.5), winter snow cover retreats in arid regions from the 2030 s, and Arctic summers become snow-free by the 2040 s. By mid-century, mid-latitude spring and autumn snow cover disappears, with arid and semi-arid regions approaching year-round snow-free conditions and humid regions losing 1–4 months of seasonal snow cover. Under the most sustainable scenario (SSP1-2.6) snow disappearance is delayed by 7.1–34 years relative to SSP5-8.5 across vulnerable regions and months. Overall, our constraint narrows projection uncertainty by 0.95–11.91 years, delaying projected disappearance by 0.01–2.65 years in transitional months while advancing it by 0.51–4.15 years in midsummer, providing refined month-specific baselines for climate risk assessments.

title: Basal mantle motion causes Pacific hotspot drift
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hotspot-based reference frames are foundational to plate reconstructions yet increasing evidence indicates that individual Pacific hotspots have migrated over time. How the overall motion of Pacific hotspots relates to the evolution of the underlying Pacific basal mantle structure (BMS), the inferred source of Pacific mantle plumes, remains elusive. Here we combine plate reference frame analysis with global mantle flow simulations to quantify the average motion of Pacific hotspots and compare it with the predicted motion of the Pacific BMS. Comparisons between Pacific fixed-hotspot reference frames and other absolute reference frames suggest an average southward migration of Pacific hotspots of ~5–10° from 80 Ma. Mantle flow models driven by plate reconstructions independently predict comparable southward average migration of Pacific plumes and the underlying Pacific BMS. In the models, the coupled BMS-plume migration is driven by greater subduction flux along the northern Pacific than along the southern Pacific between ~80-45 Ma, which generated persistent southward lower-mantle flow. Our results indicate that the average drift of Pacific hotspots is linked to the motion of the Pacific BMS, highlighting dynamic coupling between surface hotspot motion and basal mantle evolution.

title: Atomic-resolution insights into interactions of rifampicin and rifamycin derivatives with orphan CYP143 of M. tuberculosis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Analysis of drug-resistant strains of M. tuberculosis identified a Gly334Ala mutation in the orphan CYP143 gene, located within the ESX-5 secretion cluster. Guided by this clinical association, we tested the frontline antitubercular agent rifampicin as a CYP143 ligand. Atomic-resolution structures reveal a closed binding mode of rifampicin above the heme, which we also observed for other natural and synthetic rifamycins. The high quality of crystallographic data for both the wild type and mutant structures allowed us to track ligand-induced changes from the active site to the meander, the binding site for the redox partner. Consistent with this, the structure of a CYP143–ligand–redox partner complex confirms that these conformational changes are directly coupled to ligand binding. The structure of CYP143 with a selective inhibitor provides a template for rational drug design. Together, these results advance the understanding of rifampicin resistance/tolerance and the role of the orphan CYPome of M. tuberculosis.

title: An interaction module for mitochondrial ATP synthase assembly and maintenance in seed plants
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: ATP synthase and its dimerization are essential for cristae formation and mitochondrial biogenesis. In plants, the absence of canonical j and k subunits raises the question of how ATP synthase assembly and dimerization are supported in this lineage. We identify MTF5, a fast-turnover, seed plant-specific protein critical for embryogenesis and mitochondrial biogenesis. Loss of MTF5 causes embryo arrest and altered mitochondrial morphology. A conditional complementation line partially rescues the embryo-lethal phenotype but shows growth defects and mitochondrial morphology changes. MTF5 interacts with another fast-turnover protein, MTF5P, and co-migrates with ATP synthase dimerization-associated subunits, supporting a role in ATP synthase assembly and maintenance. Structural predictions reveal a helical architecture comprising a long central α-helix flanked by shorter helices, but do not establish direct correspondence with canonical j and k subunits. Our findings uncover an interaction module for ATP synthase assembly and maintenance that is essential for seed plant growth and development.

title: SMYD1 trimethylates myosin K129 to restrain cardiomyocyte hypercontractility
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mutations in the force-generating motor protein myosin are common etiologic drivers of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), a prevalent inherited cardiac disease. However, whether deregulation of myosin post-translational modifications also contributes to HCM remains unknown. Here we show that SMYD1 selectively catalyzes trimethylation of cardiac β-myosin heavy chain at lysine 129 (MyHC-K129me3), and that loss of this activity promotes cardiomyocyte hypercontractility and is linked to HCM pathogenesis. A biochemical-proteomic coupled strategy identifies MyHC-K129 as the principal physiological substrate of SMYD1 in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs). The SMYD1-MyHC co-crystal structure reveals extensive interactions underlie K129 substrate specificity and shows that the HCM-associated SMYD1F272L mutation disrupts S-adenosyl-L-methionine binding, thereby compromising catalytic activity. K129me3 loss alters the myosin motor domain intrinsic mechanical behavior, decreasing maximal ATP turnover rate and motility. Finally, eliminating K129 methylation enhances contractility and force generation in iPSC-CM monolayers and engineered cardiac tissues. Collectively, our results uncover a pivotal role for the SMYD1-MyHC-K129me3 axis in restraining cardiac contractility, providing insight into the pathogenic mechanism of an HCM-associated SMYD1 mutation.

title: A neuroimmune dichotomy for T cell immunity in the mesenteric iymph node in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Peripheral nerves innervate lymphoid organs, yet how they decode immune signals and direct adaptive immunity remains unknown. Here we show, using three-dimensional tissue imaging, in vivo calcium recordings, single-cell transcriptomics, and chemogenetics in mice, that the mesenteric lymph node (mLN) harbours functionally antagonistic neural circuits that govern T cell fate. Vagal sensory neurons selectively detect IL-1β and TNF-α and release calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), which suppresses Foxp3⁺ regulatory T (Treg) cells and expands cytotoxic CD8⁺ effector T (Teff) cells. Conversely, sympathetic neurons sense IL-6 and release norepinephrine (NE), promoting Treg accumulation while restraining effector responses. During Citrobacter rodentium infection, the sympathetic–NE–Treg axis is protective, whereas the vagal–CGRP axis drives immunopathology. Treg-specific deletion of the CGRP receptor or the β₂-adrenergic receptor confirms that these opposing signals converge on Treg cells to calibrate mucosal host defence. These findings establish the mLN as an autonomic rheostat for intestinal immunity.

title: Tomato NLR R1L mediates SlSPL3 degradation to trigger a growth-to-defense switch against Phytophthora infestans
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Intracellular nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) receptors activate effector-triggered immunity (ETI), a key branch of plant immunity conferring robust resistance. The downstream signaling mechanisms of ETI receptors remain unclear. We characterize tomato NLR protein R1L that specifically recognizes the Phytophthora infestans effector AVR1. R1L is predominantly cytoplasmic and partially relocalizes into the nucleus upon infection. With helper SlNRC1, R1L and AVR1 trigger a hypersensitive response (HR). R1L positively regulates tomato immunity against P. infestans. Yeast two-hybrid screening identified SlSPL3, a positive regulator of growth and development, as a direct R1L interactor. SlSPL3 binds the GTAC-box motif in the SlLTP3 promoter and activates this negative immune regulator. R1L counteracts SlSPL3-mediated immune suppression by promoting the ubiquitin-mediated degradation of SlSPL3. Thus, the AVR1-R1L-SlSPL3-SlLTP3 module mediates a growth-immunity trade-off. In uninfected plants, SlSPL3 promotes growth and suppresses immunity via SlLTP3. Upon infection, R1L-mediated SlSPL3 degradation activates immunity and represses growth. This study elucidates a pathogen perception-transcriptional reprogramming-immunity axis, offering insights into plant defense and growth-immunity balance.

title: A small RNA regulates iron homeostasis and host mucus colonization in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Symbiotic bacteria in the human intestinal microbiota provide many pivotal functions to human health and occupy distinct biogeographic niches within the gut. Yet the molecular basis underlying niche-specific colonization remains poorly defined. To address this, we conducted a time-resolved dual RNA-seq experiment to simultaneously monitor the transcriptional co-adaptations of human commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and human gut epithelial cells in a hypoxic, mucus-producing, epithelial co-culture system. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of mucus-associated versus supernatant Bacteroides populations unveiled small RNAs (sRNAs) that are differentially regulated between spatially segregated subpopulations. Among these, we identified IroR as a key sRNA that facilitates B. thetaiotaomicron adaptation to iron limitation and host glycan availability, partly by modulating expression of capsule-associated surface states. This work provides new insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of gut colonization and underscores a previously underappreciated role for bacterial sRNAs in shaping mutualistic interactions between the human microbiota and the gut epithelium.

title: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neural decoding is a widely-used machine learning technique for investigating how behavior, perception and cognition are represented in neural activity. However without careful application data leakage can occur, where information from the test set contaminates the training set, leading to biased estimates of decoding performance and potentially invalidating biological conclusions. Here we show that leakage can be introduced in neural decoding studies by common supervised and unsupervised preprocessing steps, including dimensionality reduction. We reveal that in some cases leakage can paradoxically decrease decoding performance relative to unbiased estimates, and we provide theoretical analyses explaining how this occurs. We also show that, for autocorrelated neural time series, randomized k-fold cross-validation can dramatically overstate decoding performance. Based on these findings, we provide detailed recommendations for avoiding data leakage in neural decoding.

title: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Since early 2024, highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus (clade 2.3.4.4b) has caused outbreaks in U.S. dairy cattle, infecting other mammals including humans. Here, we evaluate the protective efficacy of two commercially available seasonal influenza vaccines against a human-derived bovine H5N1 isolate, A/Texas/37/2024, in influenza-naïve female ferrets. All unvaccinated ferrets develop severe disease and succumb to infection or meet humane euthanasia criteria. Immunisation with an inactivated influenza vaccine reduces viral titres in multiple respiratory and extrapulmonary tissues and delays disease progression but does not prevent fatal outcomes. By contrast, five of six ferrets immunised with a live attenuated influenza vaccine survive challenge and show more effective control of viral replication in the nasal mucosa. Live attenuated vaccination induces stronger T-cell responses, while the absence of detectable neutralising activity against the challenge virus suggests that cellular immunity, rather than neutralising antibodies, may contribute to protection. These findings demonstrate that seasonal live attenuated influenza vaccination can provide cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus, potentially through cellular immune responses in the respiratory tract.

title: Evolutionary Neuroskeletal Biology
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nerves reach deep into bone, where they influence how the skeleton grows, remodels, and repairs. Yet almost everything we know about neuroskeletal biology comes from mice and humans. The influence of nerves on bone is largely unknown in other vertebrates, whose physiology differs markedly from that of mammals: birds mobilize a fifth of their skeletal minerals to build each eggshell, some lizards regrow their tails, salamanders cannot regenerate after denervation, and fish maintain their skeleton without bone cells. In this Perspective, we outline a comparative framework for understanding bone innervation and detail what this framework can offer fields ranging from evolution and paleontology to medicine.
