title: Mechanistic insights into intracellular phase separation and maturation of FUS LC revealed by in-cell NMR
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fused in sarcoma (FUS) forms dynamic biomolecular condensates through phase separation, a process associated with stress responses and neurodegenerative diseases. Here, we use in-cell NMR spectroscopy to directly observe condensate formation of the FUS low-complexity (LC) domain in living cells. We identify a two-step process: initial droplet formation followed by time-dependent maturation, characterized by reduced internal mobility. Deletion mutant analysis reveals that while initial condensate formation is driven by collective multivalent interactions, the reversible amyloid core (RAC) region is essential for the subsequent maturation. Intracellular droplets form at concentrations well below the in vitro threshold, which cannot be explained by macromolecular crowding alone. Notably, droplet formation is suppressed under nutrient starvation, suggesting that ATP-dependent cellular activities indirectly promote FUS condensation. These findings demonstrate that the metabolically active intracellular environment modulates FUS condensate behavior, providing mechanistic insights into early events in pathological aggregation and establishing a general framework for studying condensates in cells.

title: Iron supplementation in iron-deficient Kenyan infants: a randomised controlled trial of vaccine immunogenicity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Iron deficiency is common in early infancy, but whether supplementation improves vaccine immunogenicity is uncertain. In this randomised, double-blind trial in coastal Kenya (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04744818), 288 breastfed, iron-deficient infants aged six weeks received daily oral iron (3 mg/kg/day; n = 143) or control (n = 145) until 24 weeks during routine immunisation; follow-up continued to 52 weeks. Primary outcomes were diphtheria and pertussis IgG responses during supplementation. Secondary outcomes were antibody responses to oral and inactivated poliovirus, Haemophilus influenzae type b, tetanus, hepatitis B, and 10-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. Vaccines were given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks. Iron supplementation reduced iron deficiency (OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34–0.71; p

title: CD300LD drives osteoclastogenesis and inflammatory bone loss by sensing cholesterol and activating FES SYK STAT3
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Osteoclasts are essential for bone remodeling and homeostasis. Their excessive activation drives pathological bone loss disorders such as periodontitis and arthritis. Current osteoclast-inhibiting therapies are limited by adverse effects and poor specificity, underscoring the importance to identify new regulators of osteoclastogenesis. Here, we conducted a pooled CRISPR–Cas9 screen targeting cluster of differentiation (CD) genes to uncover novel modulators of osteoclast differentiation and identified CD300LD, a single-pass transmembrane protein, as a potent driver of osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deletion impaired osteoclastogenesis in cell line and primary bone-marrow–derived macrophages. In vivo, myeloid-specific Cd300ld knockout mice exhibited significantly reduced alveolar bone loss and osteoclast numbers in experimental periodontitis, as well as attenuated joint inflammation and bone erosion in arthritis models, whereas bone remodeling during skeletal development remained unaltered. Mechanistically, cholesterol acts as extracellular activator for CD300LD to activate osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deficiency intracellularly inhibited phosphorylation of FES, SYK, and STAT3. Consistently, loss of Fes, Syk or Stat3 recapitulated the Cd300ld-deficient phenotypes, establishing a CD300LD–FES–SYK–STAT3 signaling axis essential for osteoclast differentiation. Together, these findings identify CD300LD as a critical, previously unrecognized driver of osteoclastogenesis and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for inflammatory bone loss.

title: Hepatokine AGP2 mediates physical exercise-induced bone augmentation through liver-bone signaling communication
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Physical exercise promotes bone health. However, its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Here, we identified the hepatokine AGP2 as an osteoanabolic mediator of exercise. Exercise increases circulating AGP2 levels in mice and humans. Hepatocyte-specific Agp2 knockout substantially attenuates exercise-induced bone formation, whereas hepatic AGP2 overexpression prevents bone loss in ovariectomized mice. Mechanistically, exercise-induced lactate promotes hepatic Agp2 expression through histone H3K14 lactylation. Secreted AGP2 directly binds the Wnt co-receptor LRP5, activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling, promotes osteoblast differentiation, and suppresses osteoclast activity. Recombinant AGP2 administration also alleviates bone loss in mouse models of osteoporosis. Thus, these findings delineate a critical role of liver-bone crosstalk in mediating the beneficial effects of exercise on bone metabolism, highlighting AGP2 as a key mediator in exercise-induced bone anabolism and suggesting AGP2 as a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of metabolic bone disorders.

title: Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

title: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-enhanced framework for knowledge-guided campus-scale building retrofit design
abstract: Urban-scale building envelope optimization is constrained by the computational burden of iterative simulation. This study proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced framework that replaces the search phase of conventional optimization: literature-screened envelope solutions are retrieved from a curated corpus and then cross-checked through physics-based EnergyPlus simulation, rather than located through exhaustive parametric search. The corpus comprises 20,247 initially identified publications screened to a core of 338 studies, together with an experimentally characterized database of 502 envelope materials, of which 65 were used in the assemblies evaluated here. A three-stage progressive retrofit strategy — conventional high-performance insulation; vacuum insulation panels, aerogel and phase change materials (PCMs); and optimized PCM hybrid assemblies — was applied to seven reference buildings on Yonsei University's 86-building campus in Seoul, Korea. A systematic literature review established that whole-building field-measured savings are systematically 0.25–0.75× of simulation-only upper bounds, a correction embedded directly in the retrieval thresholds and screening criteria. The seven reference buildings produce a simulated mean building-level EUI reduction of 21.5%, ranging from 9.5% in high window-to-wall-ratio modern buildings to 39.6% in thermally deficient heritage structures, while campus-wide analysis of all 86 buildings yields 15.7% (124.4 to 104.9 kWh/m 2 ·year). EnergyPlus models were not calibrated against sub-metered operational data, so all reported reductions are simulation-based screening estimates. The framework offers a scalable, computationally efficient route to envelope retrofit planning for large institutional portfolios and urban decarbonization programs.

title: Stochastic assessment of eight emergency electricity supply configurations for urban shelters: Performance limits and the role of vehicle-to-shelter
abstract: Emergency electricity planning for urban shelters requires comparing heterogeneous supply resources under uncertain, time-varying demand. This study assesses eight specified emergency electricity-supply configurations, including two Vehicle-to-Shelter (V2S) arrangements, for a 1000-person shelter during a 72-h grid outage. A common framework combines paired Monte Carlo simulation, hourly supply–demand matching, continuous resource-state evolution, and access-conditioned variance decomposition, while retaining configuration-specific constraints on power, usable energy, infrastructure continuity, resource access, and deployment timing. Across nine demand and disaster-severity scenarios, adequacy declined as shelter services expanded and cold-season demand increased, while access-dependent resources were additionally constrained by infrastructure continuity, allocation, and arrival. High coverage of the specified diesel-generator configuration depended strongly on its usable energy in the most demanding scenario, where a 20% stock reduction lowered mean energy coverage ratio (ECR) from 0.819 to 0.659. Similar aggregate coverage also concealed different temporal risks. Under hot conditions with moderate disaster severity, a mobile power-supply truck and a local-plus-external V2S arrangement had nearly identical mean ECRs (0.368 and 0.367) under baseline access assumptions but different temporal shortfall patterns. The truck provided no support before allocation and arrival, whereas locally parked EVs supplied limited early power. Access-state differences accounted for most observed ECR variance for the access-dependent configurations in the two examined scenarios, distinguishing conditional resource capability from unconditional shelter adequacy. These findings support mechanism-based screening by power, endurance, immediate availability, and credible access arrangements, while suggesting a potential role for V2S as a conditional supplement rather than a universal substitute for dedicated backup supply.

title: Operating-point-dependent power-flow linearisation for joint siting, sizing, and dispatch of long-duration energy storage in distribution grids
abstract: Long-term energy-storage planning in distribution grids involves long time series, non-linear network constraints, and mixed-integer siting and sizing decisions. Especially detailed AC formulations are computationally challenging for long optimisation horizons. To address this challenge, we propose an operating-point-dependent linearisation of the AC power-flow equations using sensitivity coefficients and integrating them into a mixed-integer linear program for the joint siting, sizing and dispatch of different flexibility options over long time horizons. An iterative AC power-flow validation and relinearisation procedure is used to ensure approximation accuracy. Different approaches to select the linearisation points are benchmarked, either by using each operating point or by clustering approaches, using k -medoids while retaining the original injection and network data. The method is evaluated on SimBench distribution networks and benchmarked against non-linear AC-OPF formulations. Operating-point-dependent linearisation enables computationally tractable storage planning over long time horizons while preserving detailed network information. Clustering can reduce computational effort by about 40 % , provided that the original operating-point data are retained. The linearised model deviates from the lossless AC-OPF benchmark by approximately 0.3 % in storage power and 0.6 % in energy capacity. To demonstrate the use of the method, we develop a case study where household flexibility and grid scale storage are co-optimised in a full-year planning problem. The results show that aggregate household flexibility primarily affects storage sizing, whereas its spatial distribution influences local grid conditions and optimal siting.

title: Comparative analysis of PV allocation rules in heterogeneous energy communities for collective self-consumption
abstract: This paper investigates how photovoltaic (PV) electricity allocation rules shape the technical, economic, and distributional performance of collective self-consumption schemes at both community and individual levels. A unified analytical framework is developed to compare four allocation mechanisms—static, hourly-variable, dynamic, and priority-based—across three community configurations: a prosumer-only community, an expanded community with fixed PV capacity, and an expanded community with PV capacity scaled to demand. The study is based on a real-case study of the CERCA energy community in Spain, using one year of measured hourly consumption, meteorological, and tariff data. Results show that allocation rules significantly influence both technical and economic outcomes. In the reference scenario, self-consumption ( SC ) rises from 0.39 to 0.41 (static, hourly-variable) to 0.45 (dynamic, priority), while IRR increases from 10.0% to 11.7% and payback decreases from 8.1 to 7.2 years. Community expansion with unchanged PV capacity improves local PV utilization, reaching SC values of 0.58–0.59, maximum IRR of 12.7% and payback of 6.7 years. At the individual level, priority allocation achieves the highest returns but the greatest dispersion of benefits (the coefficient of variation ( CV ) of individual SC is in the 20.7%–41.8% range), whereas dynamic allocation delivers comparable performance with a more balanced distribution ( CV of individual SC up to 9.2%). Sensitivity analysis shows that, for fixed PV capacity, profitability is maximized with 13–15 additional consumers, yielding an IRR of up to 13.3%. Overall, allocation rules are crucial in shaping both efficiency and equity in energy communities, with direct implications for policy and market design.

title: Technology trajectories and critical raw materials in sodium-ion battery innovation: An LLM-assisted patent analysis
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising complement to lithium-ion batteries for cost-sensitive and resource-resilient energy-storage applications. Despite growing technological and industrial interest, the structure of SIB innovation remains insufficiently understood because existing patent studies have largely focused on aggregate filing trends. To address this gap, this study develops a high-resolution patent landscape through large language model-assisted classification of 9670 patent families across technological domains, battery components, electrode material classes, assignee types, regions, and cathode-related critical raw materials. The results show that SIB innovation remains strongly materials-driven, with material-related inventions accounting for almost 86% of all patent families. Within this landscape, layered transition-metal oxides account for 51% of cathode-related patent families, while hard carbon represents 44% of anode-related patent families. Innovation activity is also highly concentrated geographically, with more than 94% of the analyzed patent families including at least one Chinese assignee. At the organizational level, companies focus more strongly on near-term material pathways, whereas public organizations show greater engagement with alternative chemistries. Furthermore, critical raw materials (CRMs) continue to play a central role in SIB cathodes: 76% of cathode patent families require at least one CRM, 15% include one conditionally, and only 9% contain no CRM. The degree of this exposure varies substantially across cathode classes, with manganese, nickel, phosphorus, and vanadium emerging as the most prominent CRMs. Overall, these findings show that the strategic value of SIBs depends on material selection, regional innovation capacity, and chemistry-specific CRM exposure, with implications for research, industry, and policy.

title: A wearable reconfigurable surface electrode network for spatiotemporal control of hand motor output
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transcutaneous electrical stimulation can elicit hand movements by activating peripheral nerves and muscles. Here, we present a wearable system integrating programmable constant-current stimulation, a flexible 32-electrode forearm array with full-array active–return routing, and real-time path and parameter updating. Human-derived skin–electrode load tests showed a mean current-delivery accuracy of 94.0%, while four-hour reassessment showed 93.5% within-participant action-category agreement. Using reconfigurable active–return routing and an anatomy-informed two-level traversal strategy, we established current-path-to-action maps spanning 12 wrist and hand action categories, with spatial patterns broadly consistent with superficial forearm flexor and extensor compartments. Data-glove and inertial measurements quantified parameter-dependent finger-joint responses and action-specific wrist rotations. The mapped actions were sequentially combined for feedback-guided, stimulation-assisted task-level hand operation, supporting wearable functional electrical stimulation for task-oriented hand assistance and rehabilitation research.

title: Subambient Synthesis of Freestanding Monolayer Cubic ZrO2 Crystals with High Dielectric Permittivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) polymorphic materials offer access to unconventional crystal structures that trigger exotic properties and functionalities beyond equilibrium phases. However, extending this opportunity to metal oxides remains highly challenging because both thickness reduction and phase transformation involve large energy barriers in such strongly bonded ionic structures. Here we report an atomic-freezing conversion strategy that kinetically stabilizes freestanding 2D metastable oxide crystals under subambient conditions. Single-crystalline cubic ZrO2 of monolayer thickness is produced and stabilized below room temperature, although this phase is typically stable only at temperatures above 2000 °C in bulk. Structural analysis reveals that the layered ZrNCl precursor contains a Zr atomic framework that matches the (111) planes of cubic ZrO2. During conversion, suppressed atomic motion under low temperatures and 2D confinement preserves the nonequilibrium cubic structure. The resulting 2D cubic ZrO2 exhibits a high dielectric permittivity of ∼23.5 and enables MoS2 field-effect transistors with an on/off ratio of ∼108 and a subthreshold slope as low as 63.5 mV dec–1. This approach also applies to cubic HfO2 and tetragonal Bi2O3, providing a general kinetic route to bypass thermodynamic phase constraints and expanding access to metastable oxides in the 2D limit.

title: Quantitative prediction model of FB-113-driven self-assembly nanopesticides
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nanopesticides offer new opportunities to improve pesticide efficacy and utilization efficiency; however, they are often complex to produce and exhibit low cargo loading, except for those formed through molecular self-assembly. Currently, the formation of these self-assembly nanopesticides remains difficult to predict, heavily relying on serendipitous observation and trial-and-error screening. Here, we report that the widely used and environmentally benign biopesticide synergist fluorescent brightener FB-113 drives the self-assembly of various pesticides into nanoparticles with ultrahigh loadings exceeding 80%. We developed an interpretable Quantitative Pesticide Structure-Assembly Prediction model (QPSAP), which reveals hydrophobicity, halogenation, polarity, and topological structure of pesticide molecules as key descriptors associated with FB-113-mediated self-assembly propensity. QPSAP was applied to large-scale virtual screening of a pesticide library to identify novel candidates for FB-113-mediated self-assembly, demonstrating complete concordance between predictions and experimental outcomes in a prospectively tested validation subset. The resulting nanopesticides enhance foliar wetting, adhesion, photostability, and transcuticular penetration, thereby increasing insecticidal and acaricidal efficacy against multiple pests while exhibiting improved crop compatibility and a reduced acute toxicity profile under the tested conditions. This work advances self-assembly nanopesticides from empirical formulation toward predictive, computationally screenable design, representing a significant advancement in safe and efficient pesticide nanoformulations.

title: Directional atomic-ordering gradients enable fatigue-resistant superelasticity in carbon tube aerogels
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Elastic inorganic aerogels are highly attractive for weight-sensitive applications in extreme environments, yet integrating high strength, large-strain recoverability and fatigue resistance within a single architecture remains a longstanding challenge. Here we show that directional atomic-ordering gradients in carbon tube aerogels provide a structural route to overcoming this trade-off. Guided by finite-element analysis, we create atomic-ordering gradient junctions through stepwise-modulated chemical vapor deposition, producing a radial increase in carbon ordering across load-bearing tube walls and inter-tube junctions. Multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the directional gradient enables the outer crystalline region to function as a sliding-enabled stress-relief layer, thereby promoting stress delocalization, suppressing bond rupture and reducing irreversible energy dissipation before network densification becomes dominant. As a result, the directional-gradient aerogel sustains reversible compression up to 95% strain, reaches a maximum stress of 8.0 MPa, and retains ~87% of its initial maximum stress after 10,000 cycles at 90% strain with only ~6% permanent deformation. These findings show that controlling atomic ordering at carbon tube junctions offers an effective way to improve the mechanical robustness and fatigue resistance of highly compressible porous solids.

title: Negative-Charge-Transfer Ligand Holes Enhance Ferromagnetism and Topological Transport in van der Waals Magnets
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Many prototypical 3d van der Waals (vdW) magnets contain heavy ligands with closed p shells, whose strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC) influences the magnetism only indirectly through p–d hybridization. Here we show that negative charge transfer (NCT) creates spin-polarized, SOC-active holes in the ligand p states bordering the vdW gap, coupling magnetic exchange and topological transport within the same states. First-principles calculations identify the synthesized MnSiTe3 as an NCT d5L ferromagnet comprising high-spin Mn2+ and one formal Te 5p ligand hole per f.u. The Te-derived holes strengthen both intralayer and, in particular, interlayer ferromagnetic exchange, favoring ferromagnetic over antiferromagnetic interlayer order by a surprisingly large 84.1 meV/f.u. SOC within the partially occupied Te 5p manifold produces an easy-plane magnetocrystalline anisotropy of 3.6 meV/f.u. The resulting simulated Curie temperature reaches 464 K. The SOC-active Te 5p holes further generate multiple Weyl points, yielding a calculated intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity of 760 Ω–1 cm–1 that remains large over a broad energy window around the Fermi level. All those results stand in sharp contrast to ligand-shell-closed vdW magnets. This NCT ligand-hole picture and the resulting magnetic and transport responses also extend to the synthesized MnGeTe3 and the predicted iodides Cr0.5Mn0.5I3 and MnI3. These results establish NCT as a chemical strategy that makes the vdW interface magnetically and topologically active. Substituting later 3d metals or heavier p ligands into existing vdW magnets drives them toward the NCT regime, providing a design principle for the discovery of new NCT candidates.

title: Large 77Se NMR Signal Enhancements in Solutions by Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization at 9.4 T for Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract 77Se nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a key method to probe selenium functional centers in biology and materials science, yet its practical application is severely hindered by its intrinsically low sensitivity due to the low gyromagnetic ratio (19% of 1H) and natural abundance (7.6%). Overhauser effect dynamic nuclear polarization (OE-DNP) has recently emerged as a promising method for generating steady-state signal enhancement in high-field liquid NMR at room temperature. However, its application to 77Se has remained unexplored to date. Here, we present liquid-state OE-DNP as a route for 77Se NMR. At 9.4 T, we report 102 to 103 fold signal enhancements for organoselenium compounds, including the drug candidate ebselen, with polarization buildup within seconds. The large enhancements are the result of efficient electron-to-nuclear polarization transfer with OE-DNP coupling factors of ≳|0.4|, the highest reported so far at high magnetic fields (≥3 T) for NMR-active nuclei. The replenishable signal enhancements allow reaction monitoring by NMR on timescales longer than nuclear T1. As a proof of concept, we monitor a diselenide metathesis reaction over 48 h, capturing species evolution for kinetic studies. This effect can be further expanded to the heavier chalcogen, tellurium, as demonstrated by 123Te OE-DNP with similar efficiency.

title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Heterochromatin typically represses genes
                    1,2
                    , yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation
                    3–7
                    . How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent
                    8
                    . In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly
                    8
                    . By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

title: Suppressing interfacial water reactivity with an Eu20-encapsulated giant polyoxoniobate for stable zinc anodes
abstract: A water-stable giant polyoxoniobate (1Eu), featuring an Eu20 cluster encapsulated within an Nb88 shell, is introduced as an electrolyte additive for aqueous zinc batteries. Its abundant nucleophilic oxygen sites reconstruct hydrogen-bond networks and regulate Zn2+ solvation, thereby suppressing interfacial water reactivity and promoting uniform Zn deposition for stable and reversible Zn anodes.

title: Achieving reversible triphasic switching of dizwitterionic azobenzene for selective molecular recruitment
abstract: Photoresponsive dizwitterionic azobenzene achieves highly reversible triphasic switching among homogeneous solution, liquid-liquid phase separation of coacervate droplets, and ordered crystals. This solution-coacervate-crystal triphasic transition enables hierarchical enrichment and stepwise sorting of fluorescent dyes and biomacromolecules, paving the way for programmable artificial cell compartments and smart separation materials.

title: Molecular-level pre-mixing enables robust high-entropy coating for sodium-ion battery cathodes
abstract: Uniform high-entropy coatings are challenging to construct on sodium-ion layered cathodes because conventional solid-state and wet-chemical routes are intrinsically constrained in achieving multicomponent homogeneity. Here, molecular-level pre-mixing is enabled by a high-entropy Prussian blue analog serving as an “all-in-one” precursor. During reactive annealing, the precursor consumes residual surface alkalis while forming a homogeneous high-entropy interphase, thereby enhancing initial Coulombic efficiency, rate capability, cycling stability, and air stability.

title: Computer vision links electroplated lithium morphology to lithium metal battery performance
abstract: Morphology is critical to materials research, yet its analysis often relies on subjective, qualitative observations that are difficult to quantify. Using lithium metal as a model, this study combines large-area automated microscopy with computer vision to establish quantitative descriptors of metal deposits. These measurements enable objective comparisons of lithium growth in different electrolytes and a combined criterion for rapid electrolyte screening. More broadly, this framework offers a transferable route toward quantitative, reproducible morphology analysis across materials science.

title: Ambient Pressure Drying Cellulose–Graphite Foam with Ordered Pores: Mechanical Robustness, Thermal Insulation and Self-Extinguishing Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ordered porous foams with excellent thermal insulation hold great promise for widespread applications in the construction sector and related engineering fields. Nevertheless, conventional fabrication of ordered porous cellulose-based foams is constrained by high equipment costs, high energy consumption and long production cycles, severely hindering their large-scale production. In this work, ordered porous cupric-ion-crosslinked cellulose–graphite composite foams are fabricated via ambient-pressure drying. TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibrils (CNF) promote flake graphite (G) exfoliation through interfacial hydrogen bonding, and construct a robust three-dimensional (3D) dual-crosslinked network via intrinsic hydrogen bonds and Cu2+-hydroxyl coordination, which sustains the ordered pore architecture during drying. The resultant foam features a uniform honeycomb-like structure, with a maximum compressive stress of 122.7 ± 11.9 MPa at a density of 0.353 ± 0.011 g/cm3, a thermal conductivity as low as 0.0764 ± 0.0004 W·m–1·K–1, and intrinsic self-extinguishing properties. Furthermore, the foam exhibits good structural stability and chemical resistance, and shows no obvious short-term phytotoxicity to wheat under the tested conditions. These preliminary results suggest that the material may have potential for applications in ecological agriculture and forestry, although further validation is required. Importantly, the foam derived from forestry residues benefits from a cost-effective and scalable fabrication route, rendering it a competitive alternative to petroleum-based foams for construction and industrial applications.

title: NIR-Activatable Implant Nanocoating: Spatiotemporally Controlled Drug Release, Photothermal Bactericidal Activity, and Peritoneal Adhesion Suppression
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bacteria readily colonize the surfaces of biomedical implant materials and form biofilms, leading to uncontrollable infections, which remain a critical clinical challenge to be resolved. Existing antibacterial coating strategies predominantly rely on unitary bactericidal mechanisms and rarely satisfy the simultaneous demand for antiadhesion capability, limiting their clinical applicability. Herein, we present a dual-functional PMCA coating that synergistically couples near-infrared (NIR) light-triggered on-demand drug release with durable antiadhesion performance. Mesoporous polydopamine nanoparticles (MPDAs) served as both carriers for chlorhexidine (CHX) and inherent photothermal transducers. CHX-loaded MPDAs were encapsulated with aldehyde functionalized hyaluronic acid (AHA) to construct core–shell nanoparticles, which were further anchored onto aminated polypropylene substrates. This design integrates bactericidal and antiadhesion functions into a single system. Under NIR irradiation, it can trigger drug release through the photothermal effect to achieve bacterial killing, while the outermost AHA layer provides durable resistance against intestinal adhesions via hydration and physical barrier effects. The inner MPDA serves as a CHX reservoir, enabling NIR-triggered drug release for bacterial killing. The outer AHA layer confers durable antiadhesion performance through physical barrier effects and hydration. This strategy synergistically combines photothermal-triggered drug release with hydration layer barrier effects, simultaneously addressing bacterial infection and postoperative intestinal adhesions, and offers a valuable reference for the development of biomedical implant materials.

title: Probing the Hidden Interfaces in Cr-LiF Conversion Cathodes in Thin-Film Solid-State Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conversion cathodes based on transition metal fluorides enable multi-electron redox reactions and high theoretical energy densities, making them promising candidates for next-generation solid-state batteries. Here, we elucidate the nanoscale structural, chemical, and redox evolution of Cr-LiF conversion cathodes integrated into thin-film solid-state batteries with a LiPON solid electrolyte using advanced transmission electron microscopy. Comparison of the discharged and charged states reveals a reversible Cr0/Cr2+ redox process mediated by CrF2 formation, while no evidence of higher chromium oxidation states is observed under operating conditions. We identify the formation of a Cr3+-rich cathode–electrolyte interphase composed primarily of a mixed CrOxNy phase and reveal pronounced cycling-induced compositional gradients and interfacial transformations. Extended cycling promotes Ti diffusion from the current collector into the cathode, leading to the formation of TiOF2/TiFx species that scavenge fluoride and locally deplete lithium. Together, these interfacial reactions reduce the fraction of electrochemically active cathode material, causing an initial capacity fade that subsequently stabilizes with cycling while largely preserving charge transport. Our results show that the capacity decay in Cr-LiF cathodes is dominated by self-limiting interfacial degradation, underscoring interface engineering as the critical strategy for advancing high-performance conversion-type solid-state batteries.

title: Engineering Antiferromagnetic (LaVO3) m /(PrVO3) n Superlattices
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this study, we demonstrate the atomic-scale engineering of antiferromagnetic (LaVO3)m/(PrVO3)n superlattices grown by molecular beam epitaxy on (001)-oriented SrTiO3 substrates. Our work achieves precise layer-by-layer control, revealing how interface-driven structural distortions can be systematically tuned. X-ray diffraction and reciprocal space mapping confirm both the epitaxial strain state and the high crystalline quality of the superlattices, with satellite peaks indicating atomically sharp interfaces between LaVO3 and PrVO3 layers. High-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy further uncovers layer-resolved atomic displacements, where La3+ and Pr3+ exhibit antipolar motions modulated by the superlattice periodicity. The designed alternate stackings of LaVO3 and PrVO3 yield a unique antiferromagnetic transition temperature (TSO), which can be tuned by adjusting their relative proportions. This behavior exists despite the distinct spin-ordering temperatures observed in the constituent materials. Layer-resolved spectroscopic measurements reveal that the hybridization of La and Pr 5d orbitals with O 2p orbitals is also modulated and directly correlated with the oxygen octahedra rotations. By determining the orbital hybridization and mapping the cation displacements as proxies, we can indirectly visualize the trilinear coupling between oxygen octahedral rotations and antipolar rare-earth displacements. Notably, the interfacial oxygen octahedral connectivity between the cubic SrTiO3 substrate and orthorhombic vanadate layers significantly influences the structural distortions. These distortions, initially almost quenched near the interface, relax over 5–6 unit cells, demonstrating how strain and interfacial effects propagate through the superlattice. This study illustrates how artificial superlattices can be engineered to control structural distortions at the atomic scale, offering a pathway to tune magnetic properties and explore new routes to promote polar instabilities through strain-distortion relationships in perovskite oxides.

title: Deep Learning-Assisted Highly Sensitive Hydrogel Sensors for Underwater Breaststroke Motion Recognition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ion-conductive hydrogels hold immense promise for flexible electronics, but their inherent swelling in liquid environments severely limits amphibious applications. Herein, a highly conductive, anti-swelling hydrogel designated as PASLC was developed via the one-pot photo-initiated copolymerization of acrylic acid (AA), lauryl methacrylate (LMA), sulfobetaine methacrylate (SBMA), and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB). When the molar ratio of hydrophilic to hydrophobic monomers was optimized to 150:3, the resulting PASLC-3 hydrogel achieved optimal swelling equilibrium, with a swelling ratio of only 4% after 7 days of immersion in water. Concurrently, this microenvironment effectively mitigates ion leakage and facilitates dynamic strain-induced conductive pathways, yielding an unprecedented seawater gauge factor (GF) of up to 12.974, which surpasses the value obtained in air. Furthermore, the hydrogel exhibits excellent stretchability (751.80% fracture strain), durable multi-substrate adhesion underwater, and superior biocompatibility (97% L929 cell viability at 24 h). Benefiting from this holistic design, PASLC-3 reliably enables real-time motion monitoring and Morse code transmission even after 7 days of seawater soaking. Integrated with deep learning neural networks, this sensor precisely decodes breaststroke kinematics, providing an attractive paradigm for robust, anti-swelling amphibious human–machine interfaces.

title: Ganglioside-Mediated Membrane Diffusion and Its Effects on EGFR-Ligand Interactions in Highly Controlled Biomimetic Systems Enabled by Chemoenzymatic Synthesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The structural heterogeneity of membrane lipids, including glycosphingolipids (GSLs) such as gangliosides, creates significant challenges in elucidating their roles in biological processes. Advances in carbohydrate synthesis have enabled the preparation of not only naturally occurring gangliosides but also structurally modified variants with tailored glycan headgroups and/or ceramide lipid tails. Here we report the design of a biomimetic system with a panel of gangliosides featuring diverse glycan headgroups, sphingosine chain lengths, and fatty acyl chain compositions to investigate how subtle perturbations in membrane biophysical properties influence protein interactions involving the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Gangliosides containing the fluorophore nitrobenzoxadiazole (NBD) positioned at different locations along the fatty acyl chain were analyzed with fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) to evaluate membrane diffusion behavior. Substantial differences were observed depending on tag location. When positioned at the terminus of the fatty acyl chain, the NBD moiety may loop back toward the lipid–water interface, potentially accounting for the lower diffusion coefficients observed. Longer fatty acyl and sphingosine tails, as well as modified sialic acid forms, resulted in sizable reductions in diffusion, and mobile fraction analysis revealed these changes may arise through distinct mechanisms. Finally, surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was employed with the functional biomimetic interface to probe EGFR-ligand interactions in the presence of neighboring gangliosides. The results indicate that GM3 does not substantially alter the EGF-binding affinity of the EGFR extracellular domain, consistent with previous reports that the regulatory effects of GM3 on EGFR may arise from more complex membrane-dependent mechanisms.

title: Ion-Gel-Enabled Residual Stress Release and Defect Passivation toward Durable Flexible Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible perovskite solar cells (FPSCs) are considered promising candidates for next-generation photovoltaics owing to their mechanical flexibility and ultrahigh power-to-weight ratio. However, their commercialization is primarily hindered by insufficient mechanical and operational stability. Repeated bending exacerbates interfacial ion migration, severely limiting both the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and the operational lifetime of FPSCs. In this study, ionogel (IG) is directly incorporated into the perovskite precursor. Located at grain boundaries, it homogenizes Pb–I complex stability via hydrogen-bonding and coordination, narrowing the nucleation window to suppress non-radiative recombination, interfacial ion migration and residual stress. Consequently, the IG-modified devices achieve stabilized PCEs of 24.97% for rigid perovskite solar cells (PSCs) and 22.73% for FPSCs. Unencapsulated devices retain 84% of their initial PCE after 1200 h of continuous operation at the maximum power point under 1-sun illumination. Furthermore, the FPSCs exhibit excellent mechanical durability, retaining 88.7% of their initial PCE after 10,000 bending cycles with a bending radius of 5 mm.

title: NIR Responsive Ag2S/MoS2 Nanohybrid Actuators Enable Phototactic Locomotion and Photodetection for Biomimetic Soft Robots
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Near-infrared (NIR) photodetectors have attracted significant research interest because of their wide-range of applications in areas such as military surveillance, optical communication, and night vision. Light-driven wireless actuators offer advantages for remote and contactless control. Over the past decade, light-driven soft actuators have emerged as promising enablers for the development of artificial robots and biomimetic devices. The realization of multifunctionality within a single materials system that integrates both NIR photodetection and actuation is of crucial importance for advanced optoelectronics and soft robotics. In this article, we report a simple and effective approach to fabricate light-responsive systems based on different weight ratios of Ag2S and MoS2. These devices simultaneously function as a photodetector and actuator through Ag2S/MoS2 nanohybrids. The Ag2S/MoS2 nanohybrid photodetector device exhibits a responsivity of 5.70 mA/W and detectivity of 1.92 × 109 Jones. For actuation, in configuration A, the maximum bending angles obtained for MoS2, Ag2S/MoS2, and Ag2S are 90, 73, and 99°, respectively. In configuration B, the Ag2S/MoS2 nanohybrid exhibits enhanced bending performance of 104°. Whereas the maximum bending angle for MoS2 is 53°. For pure Ag2S (S5), a stable actuator could not be formed in this configuration. This actuator is capable of performing versatile motions, enabling a wide range of soft robotic structures such as a blooming flower, a human push-up weightlifter, an artificial hand, and a soft gripper. This research is anticipated to open new pathways for the design of advanced light-responsive soft actuators and robotic systems.

title: Stabilizing Large-Sized SWIR InSb Quantum Dots through Zinc Acetate Post-treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The short-wave infrared (SWIR) spectral region exhibits multiple prominent advantages for cutting-edge imaging and sensing applications. Colloidal InSb quantum dots (QDs) are promising candidate materials for the fabrication of high-performance, cost-effective, and heavy-metal-free SWIR photodetectors. Existing studies have systematically investigated the synthetic kinetics of InSb QDs and developed a variety of synthetic strategies to extend the material photoresponse range. Nevertheless, research focusing on surface chemistry regulation via post-treatment strategies remains insufficient. In this work, we propose a post-treatment strategy with zinc acetate (Zn(OAc)2) for stabilizing large-sized InSb QDs without modifying the original synthesis conditions. The post-treatment effectively improves the yield of large-sized InSb QDs and extends the photoresponse wavelength from ∼1400 to ∼1900 nm, producing two times the QD product of the control sample. Further analytical measurements indicate the underlying mechanism of surface chemistry modification, which provides a theoretical guideline for the selection of post-treatment chemical reagents. The generality is validated by recovering large-sized QDs from discarded byproducts with the Zn(OAc)2 treatment. We fabricate two-terminal photoconductors to characterize the photoresponse of Zn-treated InSb QD films under 1535 and 1875 nm laser excitation, showing improved air stability. This work develops a practical approach for stabilizing large-sized InSb QDs, which can be compatibly integrated with existing synthesis strategies.

title: Substrate-Termination Dependent Photovoltaic Effect in Ferroelectric Tunneling Junctions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric tunneling junctions (FTJs) based on ferroelectric oxide films provide a promising platform for multifunctional nanoelectronic devices. While interfaces are known to be vital in determining device performance, their role in governing the photovoltaic (PV) behavior of FTJs remains unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a substrate-termination-dependent PV effect in Pt/BaTiO3/Nb-doped SrTiO3 (NSTO) FTJs with atomically engineered interfaces. By selectively preparing SrO-terminated (A-type) and TiO2-terminated (B-type) NSTO interfaces, we achieve deterministic control of the PV response. Remarkably, a pronounced PV effect, characterized by an open-circuit voltage of ∼0.25 V and a short-circuit current magnitude of ∼0.7 nA, is observed exclusively in the high-resistance (OFF) state of A-type FTJs, whereas B-type FTJs exhibit negligible photoresponse. This PV signal is stable, fatigue-resistant, and uniform across devices. Synchrotron-based photoemission and optical spectroscopy reveal termination-induced modifications of the local electrostatic potential, work function, and low-energy optical onset. First-principles calculations further show that the SrO-terminated interface undergoes stronger interfacial electronic reconstruction, exhibiting reduced interface-projected indirect and direct excitation gaps compared with the TiO2-terminated interface. Together with the experimentally observed low-energy indirect band-edge tail, these results indicate the formation of a more photoactive, weakly indirect interfacial electronic structure in A-type junctions. Taken together, the observations are consistent with interface-sensitive photoexcitation coupled to polarization-dependent carrier separation and collection, with the lower OFF-state conductance additionally favoring the retention of a photovoltage. These findings establish atomic-scale interface termination engineering as an effective strategy to integrate PV functionality into oxide FTJs, enabling nondestructive optical readout and multifunctional device operation.

title: A Proline-Functionalized Carboxymethyl Chitosan/Calcined Bone Composite Achieves Craniofacial Bone Regeneration via Dual Osteogenic–Angiogenic Bioactivity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Repairing critical-sized craniofacial bone defects remains challenging due to limited self-regeneration capacity and the coupled requirement for osteogenesis and angiogenesis. Carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS) has been widely explored for bone repair, yet its bioactivity requires further enhancement. Inspired by the organic–inorganic architecture of native bone, we developed a biomimetic composite by grafting proline onto CMCS and incorporating magnesium ions together with calcined bone (CB). The composite exhibited excellent biocompatibility, promoted osteogenic differentiation and angiogenic tube formation in vitro, and upregulated key genes involved in both processes (RUNX2, OPN, VEGF, KDR, and ANG), demonstrating that the introduction of proline and Mg2+ promoted both osteogenesis and angiogenesis. In rat calvarial and rabbit alveolar bone defect models, the composite stimulated robust bone formation, with significantly improved bone mineral density, bone volume fraction, and elevated CD31 and OCN expression, achieving enhanced regeneration compared with that of the clinical standard Bio-Oss. Collectively, this biomimetic organic–inorganic composite strategy simultaneously promotes bone formation and vascularization, offering a competitive candidate for craniofacial bone defect repair.

title: MnCO3–Ag Heterojunction Sonosensitizer for Enhanced Sonodynamic Therapy and Silver Ion Release against Implant-Associated Bacterial Infection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Implant-associated infections caused by biofilm-forming pathogens remain a major clinical challenge. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) represents a promising non-antibiotic antibacterial strategy. However, its therapeutic efficacy is often limited by the low reactive oxygen species (ROS) yield and poor biodegradability of the sonosensitizers. Herein, we developed MnCO3–Ag nanoparticles (Mn-Ag NPs) as a biodegradable Schottky heterojunction sonosensitizer for the treatment of implant infections associated with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). The Mn-Ag heterointerface promotes charge separation under ultrasound (US) irradiation and enables efficient generation of multiple ROS. Meanwhile, ROS generated under US irradiation promotes the oxidative release of Ag+ from the Ag phase, enabling a cascade sonodynamic/ion-release antibacterial mechanism that couples ROS-mediated damage with Ag+-mediated bactericidal activity. In vitro antibacterial experiments showed that Mn-Ag NPs reduced the number of viable MRSA by 2.5 log (99.7%) in 96-well plates. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that Mn-Ag NPs under US induced oxidative stress in MRSA and disrupted biosynthesis, DNA-binding processes, and metabolic regulation. In a murine implant-associated infection model, Mn-Ag NPs reduced viable MRSA by 2.6 log (99.7%) under US irradiation, alleviated tissue inflammation, and promoted tissue recovery. In addition, Mn-Ag NPs gradually degraded in the acidic infected microenvironment. This work highlights a biodegradable Schottky heterojunction strategy for enhancing charge separation and ROS generation, thereby enabling synergistic sonodynamic/Ag+-mediated antibacterial therapy against biofilm infections.

title: Draw-Ratio-Programmed Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fibers for Controllable Unidirectional Contraction and Intelligent Textile Integration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers are promising candidates for soft actuators. However, it remains difficult to combine a low-temperature actuation onset, room-temperature retention of a mechanically programmed length, and textile processability in a single LCE fiber. Inspired by the energy input, state retention, and triggered release sequence of biological latch-mediated spring actuation (LaMSA), this study combines continuous spinning with room-temperature post-curing draw-programming to fabricate a high-performance, unidirectionally contracting LCE fiber. UV curing establishes the permanent network and its reference length, whereas subsequent mechanical stretching writes a recoverable extended state without a second curing step. Wide-angle/small-angle X-ray scattering (WAXD/SAXS) measurements show increased axial orientation after programming, and tensile-mode DMA shows that the programmed state has a higher storage modulus E′ and undergoes gradual softening between 30 and 54 °C under fixed-length test conditions. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) identifies a thermal transition over approximately 25–54 °C, with a peak at 42.5 °C. When the fiber is free to move, photothermal heating releases the programmed deformation and drives contraction toward the cured reference length. Endpoint photographs show retention of the programmed length for more than one month in the observed fiber, and a load-lifting demonstration reaches 1100 times the fiber weight. The λs = 3 fiber also exhibits a tensile strength of 5.6 MPa and an elongation at break of 174%, allowing continuous processing on an automated flat knitting machine. Local programming further enables artificial-muscle models, light-controlled mechanical switches that retain the actuated state, and cotton/LCE knitted structures. The resulting one-way program–retain–release response provides a material and device basis for soft systems in which the final recovered state is maintained without continuous holding power.

title: A Functionally Decoupled Dual-Yarn Architecture for Scalable Sensing and Electrothermal Textiles
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible sensing elements that combine mechanical compliance, operational stability, and scalable manufacture remain a central challenge for smart textiles. Inspired by the functional segregation between the helical sensory endings of muscle spindles and the protective sheaths surrounding peripheral nerve fascicles, we propose a yarn-level functional decoupling strategy based on a dual-yarn architecture. A strain-responsive conductive yarn (SRCY) and a strain-insensitive conductive yarn (SICY) were fabricated independently by industrial hollow-spindle wrapping. The SRCY adopts a biomimetic spring–sheath helical structure, in which reversible intercoil-contact modulation enables stable strain sensing with favorable linearity at 0–40% strain and response and recovery times of 63 and 69 ms, respectively. The SICY contains a uniformly distributed helical conductive layer that provides stable electrical conduction and stable low-voltage Joule heating. The two yarns were integrated into an electrothermal sensing knitted fabric (ESKF) through a loop–inlay structure, which physically separates the sensing and Joule-heating pathways and suppresses signal crosstalk. A smart wristband incorporating the ESKF achieved 95.17% action-level accuracy for hand-gesture recognition using a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN). This functionally decoupled dual-yarn strategy provides a scalable route to multifunctional conductive textiles for wearable electronics and human–machine interfaces.

title: Enhanced High-Temperature Stability of Spinel NTC Thermistors Enabled by Synergistic Suppression of Ion Redistribution and Oxide Precipitation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spinel-structured negative temperature coefficient (NTC) thermistors are widely employed for temperature sensing but suffer from poor stability at temperatures above 300 °C. Herein, we demonstrate that the poor high-temperature stability of spinel-structured MgMn2O4 is driven by the synergistic effects of Mn ion redistribution and MgO precipitation at grain boundaries during thermal aging, which alter Mn valence states and cation site occupancy, thereby accelerating resistivity drift. In this work, Al doping is introduced to stabilize the spinel framework. Al doping transforms tetragonal MgMn2O4 into a thermally stable cubic MgAl2O4-type spinel, effectively suppressing Mg migration and MgO precipitation. Thus, the Al-doped ceramics exhibit excellent aging stability, enabling reliable temperature sensing up to 1000 °C. These results identify the key role of oxide precipitation in the thermal degradation of spinel NTC thermistors and guide the design of stable thermistors for elevated-temperature sensing.

title: Rattlesnake-Inspired Near-Infrared Sensing Based on Photothermal-Induced Asymmetric Interfacial Ion Rearrangement
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional near-infrared (NIR) light sensing materials, reliant on inorganic or organic semiconductors, are often limited by their photoelectric conversion efficiency, cooling volume, and recyclability. Inspired by the pit organ of rattlesnakes, this work presents an NIR sensing strategy based on photo-thermal-electric conversion. An NIR sensing unit is constructed based on Au@ITO-graphite asymmetric electrodes and ionogel, effectively coupling interfacial photothermal and thermoelectric conversion. NIR light energy is rapidly converted into heat due to the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of Au nanoparticles (Au NPs). This thermal stimulus induces asynchronous ion adsorption and desorption at asymmetric electrode–electrolyte interfaces, generating a measurable open-circuit voltage even under nearly zero temperature gradient. The NIR sensing unit, with an electrode spacing of 0.1 mm, exhibits a sensitivity approximately 70 times higher than that of symmetric electrodes. Moreover, the NIR sensing unit can be disassembled and reused, and the Au@ITO electrodes exhibit at least 5 times of reusability and stability. This mechanism allows us to construct a sensing array for spatial NIR mapping and a biomimetic system that replicates the complete “perception‑to‑orientation” behavior sequence. This work provides a material-agnostic strategy for application in ultrathin, environmentally friendly, and self-powered NIR sensing systems.

title: Interface-Stabilized P2-Type Na0.67(Mn0.65Fe0.20Co0.10Cu0.05)O2 by Ultrathin Al2O3 Coating for Enhanced Sodium Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical performance of the P2-type layered oxide cathodes for Sodium-ion Batteries (SIBs) is considerably limited by interfacial instability, transition-metal (TM) dissolution, and structural degradation during prolonged cycling. In this study, we made an ultrathin, amorphous Al2O3 surface layer on Na0.67(Mn0.65Fe0.20Co0.10Cu0.05)O2 (NMFCCO) by a precipitation-assisted hydrothermal method to improve its interfacial stability. An initial discharge capacity of the NMFCCO-Al2O3 electrode at 0.1C reaches 202 mAh g–1 within a voltage window of 2.0–4.2 V, which is comparable to recent high-capacity P2-type cathodes. Furthermore, the coated electrode exhibits 81.5% of its initial capacity after 300 cycles at 1C compared with 79.3% for NMFCCO. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy indicated reduced interfacial impedance following surface modification, while post-cycling structural and morphological analyses suggested improved preservation of electrode integrity. These improvements are consistent with the protective role of the ultrathin Al2O3 coating in mitigating interfacial degradation during repeated Na+ extraction and insertion. This work highlights Al2O3 surface modification as a promising strategy for improving the cycling durability of Cu-containing P2-type layered oxide cathodes for sodium-ion batteries.

title: Complex [Ru(bpy)3]2+-Templated Hybrid Metal Halides with Improved Luminescence for Advanced Optoelectronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Zero-dimensional (0D) organic–inorganic hybrid metal halides (HMHs) have attracted intense interest for their rich selectivity of composition and exceptional luminescence properties. However, the exploration of functional A-site cations is very limited, and their roles are not well understood. Herein, we introduce the intrinsically emissive complex [Ru(bpy)3]2+ (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine) as an A-site building block to construct a family of 0D HMHs with the general formula [Ru(bpy)3]MCl6 ([M], M = Sn, Te). [M] not only preserves the orange-red metal-to-ligand charge transfer emission of [Ru(bpy)3]2+ but also exhibit a nearly 10-fold enhancement in photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) compared to that of unhybridized [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2. More interestingly, through alloying with multiple M4+ cations (Sn4+, Te4+, Zr4+, Hf4+, W4+), high-entropy [SnTeZrHfW] crystals are successfully synthesized with improved thermal stability and antithermal quenching behavior. The representative [Sn] analog demonstrates broadband emission spanning from 550 to 800 nm with a high PLQY of 54.1%, promising for efficient red LEDs and near-infrared imaging. Moreover, its strong X-ray radioluminescence performance affords a flexible scintillation screen with a spatial resolution of 17.6 lp mm–1 and low detection limit of 1.99 μGy s–1. This work provides a paradigm for designing high-entropy 0D HMHs with functional cationic chromophores, advancing their applications in solid-state lighting and radiation imaging.

title: Self-Propelled Magnesium-Based Janus Micromotors Enabling Enhanced Drug Delivery into Cartilage for Osteoarthritis Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage damage. Intra-articular injection is the preferred therapeutic route for OA, yet drugs are rapidly cleared from the synovial fluid, and they poorly penetrate the dense, avascular cartilage. Herein, a self-propelled Janus micromotor is developed for enhanced intra-articular drug delivery into cartilage for OA treatment. In this system, the magnesium (Mg) particle acts as the power source, reacting with synovial fluid to generate hydrogen gas for propulsion, while the poly(allylamine hydrochloride) (PAH)-modified poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) layer enables charge-assisted targeting toward negatively charged cartilage for drug penetration. In vitro co-culture studies show that the micromotors rapidly overcome the viscous synovial fluid barrier, deliver drugs to the cartilage surface, and facilitate deep penetration before clearance. Cell experiments demonstrate that micromotors attenuate IL-1β-induced chondrocyte injury and promote GAG and Col II synthesis. Furthermore, in an OA rat model, micromotors loaded with both the anti-inflammatory drug triacetyl andrographolide (A100) and the cartilage-repair drug kartogenin (KGN) inhibit inflammatory factor expression while upregulating Col II, thereby disrupting the vicious cycle of inflammation and cartilage degeneration and efficiently promoting cartilage repair. This well-designed A100/KGN@PAH-PLGA-Mg micromotor offers a promising strategy for improved OA therapy.

title: Energy Storage Properties of Natural Clinoptilolite-Based Anodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Improved Capacity and Stability via Magnesiothermic Reduction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the morphology, chemical composition, and electrochemical performance of natural clinoptilolite subjected to thermal and chemical treatment. Magnesiothermic reduction of this natural zeolite resulted in an increase in the Si/O ratio and the formation of a new crystalline silicon phase. SEM observations showed that the original particle morphology was largely preserved, whereas EDS and XRD confirmed changes in the elemental and phase composition, respectively. The suggested partial reduction of SiO2 was additionally confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), which revealed a substantial decrease in the surface aluminum content and densification of Si species on the modified surface. Electrochemical studies showed that the clinoptilolite-based materials can be used effectively as negative electrodes in lithium-ion batteries. Cyclic voltammetry indicated stable electrochemical properties, with a predominantly capacitive contribution at higher scan rates and a greater contribution from diffusion-controlled processes at lower scan rates. In turn, galvanostatic tests confirmed the high specific capacity, reaching 668 mAh/g for the material after magnesiothermic reduction, with a capacity retention of ∼94% after 1000 cycles. The results indicate the potential use of the tested materials as negative electrodes with high specific capacity and long-term cyclic stability.

title: Directional codes for quantum LDPC error correction on square and hexagonal grid architectures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Utility-scale quantum computing requires quantum error correction to protect quantum information against noise. Superconducting hardware is a promising platform for fault-tolerant computation, but its typically two-dimensional nearest-neighbour connectivity restricts the variety of quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes that can be implemented efficiently. Here we introduce directional codes, a family of qLDPC codes compatible with square-grid and, in some cases, hexagonal-grid architectures. The key idea is to use the iSWAP gate to measure long range stabilisers using only local interactions, without requiring additional connectivity. We evaluate directional codes using a superconducting-inspired circuit-level Pauli noise model and compare them to the rotated toric code and bivariate bicycle codes. The best directional code family considered matches the logical error rate of the rotated toric code at physical error rate p = 10−3 but requires only a quarter to a third of the number of physical qubits to encode a given number of logical qubits.

title: Excited-state twisted intramolecular charge transfer enables reversible light control of rhodamine-graphene binding
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Reversible light control of supramolecular interactions underpins fundamental processes in nature, inspiring artificial molecular devices and adaptive materials. Existing approaches rely on light-modulated interconversion between ground-state species characterized by distinct binding properties. Here, we introduce twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) as an excited-state specific lever to modulate dye–surface adhesion. Using rhodamine B base (Rhb) as the photoactive species, we combine femtosecond spectroscopy with theoretical calculations to provide a direct observation of TICT formation and its thermal equilibrium with the locally excited state. We show that the associated dihedral twisting and charge redistribution weaken Rhb-graphene binding, enabling light-induced dye desorption in water. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate that the out-of-plane TICT conformations induce steric hindrance against the graphene basal plane, significantly reducing the binding affinity and lowering the thermodynamic barrier of the dye-surface desorption. This synergy between experiment and theory establishes excited-state conformational dynamics as a general strategy to control supramolecular interactions in host-guest systems in physiological conditions, with implications for sensing, delivery, and materials science.

title: Scalable 3D hybrid integrated photonic computing chiplets
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The exponential surge in artificial intelligence computing power demand is driving a transition from electrons to photons across the infrastructure. Although integrated photonics has revolutionized communications and computing, its scaling for large-scale information processing is constrained by monolithic scalability, modulation efficiency, and multi-chip integration. Here, we present HyPec, a hybrid photonic extensible chiplet architecture that synergizes thin-film lithium niobate modulation chiplets with femtosecond laser-written three-dimensional functional chiplets. Through function disaggregation, HyPec partitions high-performance active modulation from the 3D photonic routing network. This chiplet architecture facilitates seamless multi-chip connectivity across diverse material platforms to achieve aggregate performance beyond monolithic limits, thereby allowing the system to scale through the addition of functional chiplets. To validate the advantages of this architecture, we experimentally built a co-packaged photonic computing chiplet system that implements a scalable graph solver and further identifies critical protein residues in structural biology networks. This work establishes a scalable hardware path for integrated photonic computing, with broader implications for high-density optical interconnects and photonic quantum information systems.

title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot-superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man's Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron-hole character, but lack topological protection3-5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man's Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6-8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man's Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

title: A probabilistic region-based model for evaluating the integrated hosting capacity of photovoltaics and electric vehicles in power distribution networks
abstract: With the wide-spread integration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems and electric vehicles (EVs) into power distribution networks, several security-related issues may arise, including overloading, voltage violations, and power quality issues. The hosting capacity assessments aim to determine the distribution network's ability to accommodate the PVs and EVs, and can provide effective signals for the planning and deployment of PV systems and charging stations. However, existing hosting capacity evaluation methods typically assess PV and EV resources independently, while neglecting their mutual and bidirectional interplay. This conventional treatment cannot characterize the coupled relationship between PV and EV hosting capacities, since the feasible ranges of these two resources are jointly constrained by network operational limits rather than being independent of each other. To address this issue, this paper proposes the concept of probabilistic hosting capacity region (PHCR) to characterize the integrated hosting capacity (IHC) of distribution networks for PV and EV resources under uncertainties. The proposed PHCR can provide a visual and comprehensive representation of the feasible ranges of PV and EV capacities that the network can host with specified probabilities, considering the interplay between PV generation and EV charging loads. Besides, an efficient evaluation model is developed, incorporating network operation constraints, PV output uncertainties, and EV charging-load variability. On this basis, a numerical method based on vertex enumeration and combinatorial search algorithms is combined to effectively calculate the PHCR from the distribution network model. Case studies on modified IEEE 33- and IEEE 123-bus distribution networks demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency advantages of the proposed method. In the IEEE 123-bus system, the proposed model reduces the computation time by 81.6% compared with the point-by-point simulation method, even while maintaining high accuracy with an area error below 0.3%. Thus, the proposed PHCR framework offers a reliable and comprehensive tool for distribution network planning and operation, thereby supporting transition to a low-carbon power distribution network.

title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
abstract: Augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings. Yet making them viable for comfortable, all-day use remains deeply challenging, constrained by hard trade-offs of size, power and display performance. This calls for fundamentally new ways to generate and control light with high precision in an ultracompact form factor. Here we examine how integrated photonics can help bridge the technology gap in AR hardware. We review the basics of AR displays and recent advances in integrated photonics for new AR display components and architectures, then turn to key challenges and future directions, from component development to system innovation and scalable manufacturing, and highlight broader opportunities for synergy with fields such as quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.

title: A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies
abstract: Potent immune responses against diverse HIV strains have ignited the field, but major hurdles remain.

title: Single-Molecule DNA Sequencing with Nanopores
abstract: Abstract DNA sequencing is indispensable in healthcare, agriculture, environmental protection, and understanding of biology. DNA sequencing with nanopores uses a unique principle where individual DNA strands are threaded through a ring-like nanopore, which acts as a read head to electronically detect the bases. Due to the simple principle, nanopores enable sequencing at previously unachieved speeds and read lengths as well as direct sensing of epigenetically modified bases. The electrical nature also allows highly portable devices to be used in the clinic or the field. This review places DNA nanopore sequencing within the context of other DNA sequencing technologies and explains its functional principle and the essential components of commercial nanopore sequencing platforms. The advantages of nanopore sequencing are demonstrated with relevant case studies, and nanopore sequencing is compared to other technologies in terms of sequencing parameters such as read length, throughput, cost per base, and accuracy. A brief outlook discusses how the current shortcomings of nanopore sequencing can be addressed with future advances.

title: A fine-grained reconstruction of barley’s evolutionary history
abstract: Chromosome-scale genome sequences from across the barley genus Hordeum reveal large structural variation, evidence of ancient genetic exchange and extensive divergence of regulatory sequences. These evolutionary processes have generated diversity that could be used to improve cultivated barley. Genome sequences across Hordeum reveal conserved chromosome ends and coding genes, but divergent chromosome centres and regulatory DNA.

title: Integration of Mott neurons and spintronic memories for event-driven spiking neural networks
abstract:
Abstract
                  Spiking neural networks provide energy-efficient, event-driven computing, but separating volatile neuronal dynamics from non-volatile memory imposes costly signal transfer and conversion. Here we demonstrate a hybrid compute-and-store core that directly integrates thermally coupled vanadium dioxide Mott leaky integrate-and-fire neurons to spintronic memory. The neurons require no external resistive or capacitive elements for temporal integration and write their output spikes into either domain-wall racetracks or spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions without amplifiers or analogue-to-digital converters. In racetracks, spike number and amplitude are converted into domain-wall displacement, spatially preserving temporal histories and enabling up to six spikes per processing cycle. Distinct spike trains generated from encoded input patterns produce separable non-volatile states, demonstrating event-based processing and read-out. A network model parameterized by experimental leaky integrate-and-fire neuron dynamics achieves 96.3% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition. Functional coupling of a 500-nm leaky integrate-and-fire neuron to a 100-nm spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junction further establishes nanoscale compatibility.
