Yet, very close to the latter, numerical rupture solutions change their character due to frictional rate nonlinearity, involving rate-strengthening friction, and rupture continuously propagates through the “forbidden” super-Rayleigh range into the supershear regime, without a sharp supershear transition. These results demonstrate that frictional rate dependence, generically observed in experiments, can have profound implications for fast earthquake propagation.

title: Ion‐Pair Mediation Enables Low‐Viscosity, Nonflammable Ternary Hybrid Electrolytes for High‐Voltage Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) have garnered attention as promising energy storage devices owing to their intrinsic safety. However, the practical energy density of AZMBs is severely constrained by the narrow electrochemical window and sluggish kinetics inherent to conventional concentrated or viscous aqueous electrolytes. To address these limitations, a ternary hybrid system comprising a Zn(OTf) 2 /LiOTf dual‐salt matrix and low‐volume (5 vol.%) 1‐ethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (EMIMTFSI, abbreviated as EMT) ionic liquid is constructed. In the ternary system, EMIM + ‐TFSI − /OTf − ion pairs reconstruct the hydrogen‐bond network of the dual‐salt framework, thereby reducing bulk viscosity and broadening the electrochemical stability window to 2.76 V at low total salt concentrations. More importantly, these ion pairs undergo adsorption‐reduction‐anchoring to form an inner inorganic/outer organic bilayer, where OTf − /TFSI − decomposition generates a robust fluoride‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that subsequently anchors EMIM + as a dynamic cationic shield. Consequently, the Zn//Zn symmetric cells achieve an outstanding lifespan of 3215 h at 1 mA cm −2 . Zn//MnO 2 ‐CNT battery demonstrates 88.21% capacity retention after 1100 cycles at 1 A g −1 within a high‐voltage range (0.8–2.0 V), and Zn//LiMn 2 O 4 battery exhibits a high discharge plateau of 1.86 V v s. Zn. This work offers a promising electrolyte design strategy for high‐voltage and long‐cycle‐life AZMBs.

title: Ion‐Pair Decoupler Tunes Solvation Chemistry for Room‐Temperature Polymer Electrolytes With Built‐In Flame Retardancy
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐state polymer electrolytes for high‐energy lithium‐metal batteries are severely constrained by low room‐temperature ionic conductivity. However, mainstream approaches focus on regulating the aggregate structure and flexibility of polymer chains while neglecting the ionic solvation microenvironment, which caps ionic conductivity gains at a marginal level. Here, an innovative ion‐pair decoupling strategy is proposed to reshape the Li + solvation chemistry within polymer matrices and to facilitate rapid ionic conduction. The ion‐pair decoupler, diethyl phosphoramidate, promotes the dissociation of lithium salt into a configuration dominated by solvent‐separated ion pairs by coordinating with Li + via its electron‐rich P = O groups and anchoring TFSI ‒ through hydrogen bond donors. Consequently, the ionic conductivity of the engineered electrolyte increases 24.6‐fold at 25°C. Li symmetric cells achieve stable cycling over 850 h, and Li||LiFePO 4 cells deliver a high‐capacity retention rate of 96.5% after 400 cycles at 25°C. Furthermore, the designed electrolyte exhibits excellent self‐extinguishing flame‐retardant properties by combining gas‐phase radical scavenging and condensed‐phase char‐forming mechanisms. Thus, a single molecular design simultaneously serves as an ion‐pair decoupler and an intrinsic flame retardant, establishing solvation‐chemistry tuning as a new paradigm for safe, room‐temperature solid polymer electrolytes.

title: In Situ Formation of Inorganic‐Rich Interphase via SiO2 Additive for High‐Performance Sodium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium metal batteries (SMBs) are promising candidates for next‐generation high‐energy‐density storage systems, yet their practical application is hindered by dendritic growth and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation. Herein, we report an in situ interfacial regulation strategy by introducing amorphous SiO 2 (a‑SiO 2 ) into Na metal anodes through an accumulative roll bonding process. We reveal that SiO 2 undergoes electrochemical reduction reaction with Na, generating SiO x (12 O—a beneficial inorganic SEI component that enhances interfacial ion transport and mechanical robustness. Furthermore, a‐SiO 2 exhibits superior interfacial reactivity and strong adsorption affinity toward fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), promoting a NaF‐rich SEI that suppresses electrolyte decomposition. This synergetic inorganic‐rich SEI homogenizes Na deposition and accelerates ion diffusion kinetics. As a result, the Na/a‑SiO 2 symmetric cell achieves an ultralow overpotential of 24 mV at 0.5 mA cm −2 and stable cycling for over 1350 h. When paired with the Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 O 2 F cathode, the full cell delivers excellent rate capability (73.9 mAh g −1 at 60 C) and cycling stability with 80% capacity retention after 8000 cycles at 20 C. This work establishes SiO 2 as a scalable and effective inorganic additive for tailoring SEI chemistry, offering a practical pathway toward high‐energy and durable SMBs.

title: Unified Grain‐Boundary and Electrode‐Interface Engineering Enables High‐Performance Magnesium‐Based Thermoelectrics
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐performance thermoelectric devices require not only intrinsically efficient materials but also minimized transport losses across multiple interfaces during device integration. However, internal transport interfaces and external electrode contacts are typically optimized independently, creating a persistent challenge in translating material‐level advances into device‐level performance. Here we establish a unified interface engineering strategy in Bi‐rich Mg 3 (Sb,Bi) 2 thermoelectrics by using Nb as a multifunctional interface modifier. In Mg 3 Sb 0.7 Bi 1.3 , Nb‐rich internal interfaces regulate grain‐boundary carrier transport, while Nb foils provide chemically stable and low‐resistance electrode contacts. First‐principles calculations and atomic‐scale characterization reveal that the Bi‐rich composition suppresses extensive Nb‐related reactions while enabling electronically favorable confined interfaces. Nb incorporation increases the weighted mobility to 315.6 cm 2 ·V −1 ·s −1 and achieves a room‐temperature zT above 0.8, while Nb foil contacts yield an intrinsic contact resistivity of 1.8 µΩ·cm 2 . Integrating Nb‐engineered n‐type Mg 3 Sb 0.7 Bi 1.3 with p‐type MgAgSb enables Mg‐based thermoelectric modules with a conversion efficiency of 3.8% at Δ T = 100 K and a maximum cooling temperature difference of 82.7 K at a hot‐side temperature of 373 K. This work establishes a general interface design principle for thermoelectrics, demonstrating that interface modifiers for bulk transport optimization can also serve as electrode‐contact materials to bridge the gap between high‐performance materials and practical devices.

title: In Situ Polymerized Interfaces Enable Robust and High‐Performance Dry‐Coating Electrodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Dry‐coating electrode technology eliminates the use of toxic N‐methyl‐2‐pyrrolidone and offers a promising route for sustainable battery manufacturing. However, its practical implementation remains limited by the weak interfacial mechanics among rigid cathode particles, polytetrafluoroethylene nanofibers, and conductive carbon additives. These fragile interfaces reduce mechanical robustness and interfacial stability, thereby compromising both processability and electrochemical performance. Here, we report an in situ polymerization strategy using a polymerizable deep eutectic liquid additive, which forms an adhesive polymer network upon photopolymerization, thereby reinforcing contact among electrode components and improving electrode robustness. The resulting dry‐coating LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) electrodes exhibit a 55% increase in elongation at break and deliver a reversible specific capacity of 121 mAh g −1 at 5 C with a mass loading of 10 mg cm −2 . A 3.77 Ah Li||NCM811 pouch cell achieves maximum cell‐level energy and power densities of 412 Wh kg −1 and 574 W kg −1 , respectively. In addition, a 0.60 Ah graphite||NCM811 pouch cell retains 70% of its capacity after 870 cycles. Our results establish in situ polymerization as a viable route for mechanically robust, high‐performance dry‐coating electrodes.

title: Ferroelectric‐Field Gating Suppresses the Outward Migration of Active Oxygen Intermediates in Li‐Rich Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Li‐rich layered oxides deliver high capacities through cation–anion co‐redox chemistry. During high‐voltage charging, however, peroxide/superoxide‐like O─O intermediates migrate down their concentration gradient from oxygen‐redox‐active regions toward particle surfaces, accumulating at the interface. This accumulation accelerates irreversible O 2 evolution and structural degradation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and rapid capacity fading. Here, we construct a spontaneously polarized ferroelectric LiNbO 3 interfacial layer that generates a built‐in electric field to regulate oxygen redox in Li‐rich cathodes. This electric field suppresses concentration‐gradient‐driven migration and interfacial enrichment of charged active oxygen intermediates, limiting O 2 evolution and preserving a uniform surface‐to‐bulk distribution of oxygen electronic states at high delithiation. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 310 mAh g −1 , an initial Coulombic efficiency of 99.97%, and 79% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, this strategy enables Li‐metal pouch cells to achieve an energy density of 620 Wh kg −1 and graphite‐based pouch cells to maintain stable operation over 2000 cycles. This work establishes ferroelectric‐field regulation as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxygen redox chemistry in Li‐rich cathodes.

title: Desymmetrization of Acyclic meso ‐1,3‐Diols by Cu─H‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Silylation
abstract: ABSTRACT A nonenzymatic desymmetrization of acyclic meso ‐1,3‐diols by Si─O coupling with a hydrosilane is reported. The C s ‐symmetric diols undergo enantioselective monosilylation with a Cu─H/( R , R )‐Ph‐BPE catalyst system. The choice of hydrosilane was critical for suppressing undesired bissilylation, with a tertiary homobenzylic silane providing the best results. A series of simple alkyl‐substituted 1,3‐diols was converted into the corresponding silyl ethers with high enantiomeric ratios, with an unsubstituted methylene unit in the 2‐position identified as the most favorable scaffold for efficient and selective desymmetrization. Further modifications of the obtained enantioenriched products additionally emphasize the synthetic value of the reported methodology.

title: 3D-Printed BiFeO3@TiO2 Heterojunctions with Post-UV Activation for Enhanced Visible-Light Photocatalytic Degradation of Acyclovir
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A method for 3D-printed photocatalytically active hybrid materials is reported. To this end, methacrylate-based resins doped with TiO2 particles decorated with BiFeO3 nanoparticles (BiFeO3 @TiO2) are developed for digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing technique. Upon DLP printing, the BiFeO3 @TiO2 particles are embedded in a polymer matrix, deactivating the materials for photocatalytic processes. However, after 24 h post-print UV activation, the resin is locally decomposed, exposing the BiFeO3 @TiO2 particles and thereby activating the materials with respect to their photocatalytic performance. Comprehensive characterization (TEM–EDS, XPS, FTIR, PL, TGA, reflectance) confirms the activation of the material's surface, yielding improved charge-separation efficiency. Under 440 nm irradiation, the UV-activated monolith achieved 71% acyclovir degradation, with a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.050 h–1, 2.7 times higher than that of unactivated structures and 7.5 times higher than that of a 3D-printed TiO2 (P25) reference sample. The photocatalyst retained 96% of its initial activity after six consecutive 24 h photocatalytic cycles, demonstrating excellent long-term stability. This print–activate strategy provides a practical route for overcoming catalyst encapsulation in DLP-printed photocatalysts and enables reusable visible-light-active monolithic architectures for water-treatment applications.

title: Atomic-Scale Visualization of MnOH x Reconstruction via Hydrogen Spillover for a Poisoning-Resistant Oxidation Pathway
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen spillover offers a route to modulate oxide surface chemistry, yet how it governs the reaction pathways of oxide-catalyzed CO oxidation remains elusive. Here, we show that hydrogen spillover hydroxylates MnOx on Pt(111) to form the MnOHx overlayer, with dynamically reconstructed triangular domains. High-pressure scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that MnOHx exhibits a distinct CO oxidation pathway without carbonate accumulation at room temperature. Microscopy, spectroscopy, and theory identify bridging hydroxyls within MnOHx interior domains as the key reactive motifs that react with CO. Consistent with this mechanism, hydrogen spillover also enhances CO oxidation over MnOx/Pt nanoparticle catalysts, linking atomic-scale insight to practical catalytic performance. These findings demonstrate that tailoring hydroxyl configurations can suppress poisoning and redirect oxidation pathways, offering a strategy extendable to other low-temperature oxidation reactions.

title: Modulation of Oxygen Vacancy Charge-State Evolution via Rare-Earth Praseodymium Doping for Improving the Photostability of Amorphous InZnO Thin-Film Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal oxide thin-film transistors (MOTFTs) used as backplanes for large-area and high-resolution OLED displays require simultaneously high carrier mobility and operational stability. Light-induced instability arising from the generation and persistence of photocarriers in the oxide semiconductor remains a critical challenge. Trace praseodymium (Pr) doping substantially enhances the illumination stability of amorphous InZnO (a-IZO) TFTs while maintaining high electron mobility has been reported, yet the underlying electronic mechanism remains elusive. Here, combining first-principles calculations with experimental investigations, the mechanism of enhanced photostability in Pr:IZO MOTFTs was revealed. We found that redox-active Pr dopants act as dynamic charge buffers to regulate the photoinduced charge redistribution and oxygen vacancy (VO) charge state evolution in a-IZO. The localized Pr 4f electronic states participate in a reversible charge redistribution process during the photoinduced ionization–recovery cycle, which suppresses the evolution of VO toward kinetically trapped charge states, preserves the electronic accessibility of VO related gap states for carrier recapture, and reduces photoinduced lattice reconstruction. Time-resolved transient absorption measurements further confirmed that Pr incorporation accelerates photocarrier relaxation, shortening the characteristic fast decay lifetime from ∼47 to ∼6 ps. These findings establish a direct correlation between localized electronic state evolution and photoexcited carrier dynamics and may provide a new strategy based on redox-active cation engineering to overcome the long-standing mobility–stability trade-off in metal oxide semiconductors.

title: Hierarchically Porous Metal–Organic Frameworks as Multifunctional Platforms for Synergistic Chemo-Photo-Biocatalytic Enantioselective Synthesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a promising platform for the precise customization of multifunctional composites, enabling the optimization of synergistic effects between catalysts and significantly enhancing both stability and catalytic performance. Despite this potential, this idealized system is still in the exploratory stage. Herein, we integrated a chemical catalyst with a photoenzyme-based enantioselective catalytic platform into a single system, achieving the sequential transformation from C2-alkylation to asymmetric Mannich reaction products. A hierarchically porous (HP) UiO-67 material was constructed as the supporting platform. Through a post-synthetic ligand exchange strategy, Pd(II) and Ru(II) catalysts were simultaneously immobilized, while wheat germ lipase (WGL) was encapsulated within the mesoporous channels, yielding the multifunctional catalyst WGL@HP-UiO-67-Pd/Ru. This catalyst afforded satisfactory yields of 62–94% in the C2-arylation reaction and enantioselectivities of 69–93% in the asymmetric Mannich reaction. In this sequential catalytic transformation, the multifunctional catalyst afforded an overall efficiency of 47.6%, corresponding to a 3.8-fold enhancement over the homogeneous catalyst system. These findings provide deeper insight into the role of multifunctional catalysis in sequential reactions and underscore its considerable promise for the asymmetric synthesis of organic compounds and pharmaceutical agents.

title: Fe,Ni Co-modification Balances Activity and Stability in RuO2 for Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) needs oxygen evolution anodes that combine high-current-density performance with long-term operational stability, yet RuO2, the most active benchmark oxide catalyst, dissolves under sustained anodic operation. Catalyst development almost always selects compositions by activity measured at 10 mA cm–2 in three-electrode cells, a regime far below device conditions. Here, we synthesize a library of transition-metal-modified RuO2 catalysts and show that this selection criterion fails in an operating electrolyzer. Screening across Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni modifiers identifies RuO2–FeNi as the optimal balance, with a Tafel slope of 47 mV dec–1 and a Ru mass activity of 1357 A gRu–1 at 400 mV overpotential, 14 times that of commercial RuO2, despite the smallest electrochemically active surface area in the series. In a membrane electrode assembly, RuO2–FeNi reaches 1 A cm–2 at 1.82 V in polarization measurements at 80 °C. In a separate 200 h durability test at 250 mA cm–2 and 60 °C, its cell voltage rises by 274 mV, most of it within the first 25 h, whereas RuO2–Fe, which reaches twice the current density at 1.82 V, rises by 560 mV within 64 h under the same protocol. Density functional theory traces the activity of RuO2–FeNi to Fe/Ni co-incorporation, which renders Ru electron-deficient, downshifts the Ru 4d band center, and moderates the adsorption of oxygenated intermediates; higher compositional complexity introduces electronic disorder without further benefit. Intermediate compositional complexity, selected by device-level testing rather than by screening activity, emerges as the design target for Ru-based AEMWE anodes.

title: Highway-Inspired Hollow Fillers to Improve CO2 Transport in Mixed-Matrix Membranes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Inorganic fillers play a critical role in mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) to improve membrane separation performance. However, it is faced with a persistent trade-off: low filler loading is insufficient to achieve significant performance enhancement, while high filler loading introduces stress defects that weaken membrane strength. Developing highly efficient porous fillers capable of delivering substantial separation improvements at low loading offers a solution to this challenge. Herein, we report the design of etched KMnF3 (KMnF3-EC) fillers inspired by the Maxwell dispersion theory and highway transport concepts. These fillers possess a hollow core and a highly porous shell, which maximize pore volume per unit mass of filler and create rapid gas transport pathways. Incorporation of KMnF3-EC fillers into Pebax membranes resulted in remarkable gas separation performance at an ultralow filler loading (1.5 wt %), yielding a 120% increase in gas permeability and a 57.1% enhancement in gas selectivity. Owing to such low filler loading, the membranes maintained excellent mechanical properties, with elongation at break exceeding 800% and a Young’s modulus above 100 MPa. Direct benchmarking against commonly used porous fillers revealed that KMnF3-EC improves gas separation performance with an order-of-magnitude greater efficiency. These findings provide a promising strategy for designing advanced fillers that overcome the challenging MMM performance–mechanical strength trade-off, thereby facilitating the development of durable and energy-efficient membrane separation.

title: Ice Plant-Inspired Hierarchical Nanofibrous Film for Outdoor-Stable Passive Radiative Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Daytime radiative cooling provides a low-energy approach for passive thermal management. However, existing materials primarily focus on cooling intensity, often neglecting critical issues such as nighttime overcooling, pollutant adhesion, and long-term stability. Inspired by the bladder-like epidermal structures of Mesembryanthemum crystallinum leaves, this work developed a biomimetic nanofibrous film based on poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (P(VDF-HFP)). To translate this natural hierarchical morphology into an effective light-regulating structure, P(VDF-HFP) nanofibers were used as the supporting framework, while TiO2 was introduced as a surface scattering and functional component. Through a precursor-based strategy and electrospinning, a uniform hierarchical inorganic particle/polymer fibrous structure was constructed. This multiscale architecture enhances solar scattering and regulates mid-infrared emission. The film achieves an AM1.5G-weighted solar reflectance of 90.5% over 0.3–2.5 μm, while its infrared emission is mainly concentrated within the atmospheric window. This spectral selectivity supports daytime heat dissipation while limiting radiative heat loss outside the atmospheric window. Outdoor tests demonstrated that the nanofibrous film exhibited a temperature up to 5.8 °C lower than that of a commercial white fabric reference under identical conditions. Moreover, it retained high whiteness after 230 h of UV irradiation and exhibited photocatalytic pollutant-degradation capability. This bioinspired hierarchical design offers a practical strategy for developing flexible radiative cooling materials with high reflectance, selective emission, and environmental stability.

title: Low-Hysteresis and Overshoot-Free Capacitive Strain Sensor for Silent Speech Recognition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional capacitive strain sensors suffer from mechanical hysteresis, signal overshoot, and delayed response due to viscoelastic relaxation in solid dielectric materials. We address these limitations through a synergistic structure–material design combining an auxetic porous conductive framework with a solid–liquid hybrid dielectric. The auxetic architecture reversibly deforms to suppress hysteresis, while the confined ionic liquid eliminates viscoelastic relaxation, enabling rapid, stable signal output with negligible overshoot. In situ scanning electron microscopy characterization reveals dynamic liquid-bridge formation and rupture during deformation, establishing the mechanistic link between multiphase dielectric evolution and capacitance modulation. Our sensor demonstrates exceptional performance: <2% hysteresis, 57 ms response time, negligible overshoot, gauge factor of 3.1, and stability over 8500 cycles. A wearable silent speech recognition system validates its practical applicability, achieving a classification accuracy of 93.9%. This work establishes a generalizable design strategy for soft strain sensors with simultaneously suppressed hysteresis, minimal overshoot, and fast response, enabling next-generation wearable electronics and intelligent interfaces.

title: Supramolecular Manipulation of Copper Nanoclusters Boosts Chiral Optical Performances
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) performance of chiral metal nanoclusters is generally limited by random ligand motion, which induces non-radiative decay and impairs chiral coupling, resulting in low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) and weak intrinsic chirality. Here in this study, drawing inspiration from the art of marionette puppetry, where a puppeteer controls a puppet through strings attached to strategic points, we construct hydrogen-bonded organic superstructures (HBOSs) composed of cyanuric acid and 1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triamine to manipulate chiral glutathione-capped copper nanoclusters (GSH-Cu NCs). The hydrogen-bonding interactions between HBOSs and GSH-Cu NCs act as the "strings" that precisely direct their spatial arrangement and effectively restrain random ligand motion. The manipulation processes harness the orientation of nanoclusters and balanced the electric and magnetic dipoles, therefore boosting the chiral optical performances including increased PLQY to 94.15% and amplified CPL over an order of magnitude to –1.39 × 10–2. Additionally, the composites also exhibit thermally reversible fluorescence between –20 and 20 °C, demonstrating the reversible nature of hydrogen-bonding interactions. The red-emitting GSH-Cu NCs/HBOSs phosphors are integrated with commercial phosphors onto an InGaN chip, yielding white light-emitting diodes that exhibit near-ideal CIE coordinates of (0.33, 0.34) and a high color rendering index of 92.1. Our study offers a strategy to overcome the trade-off between electric and magnetic dipoles which further provides insights for the design of next-generation high-performance optoelectronic devices.

title: Comparative Study of Naphthalene Diimide Terminal Groups for Buried-Interface Modification in Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract SnO2 serves as a leading electron transport material in n–i–p perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet its practical deployment is constrained by interfacial defects and energy-level mismatch. Herein, two naphthalene diimide (NDI) derivatives—DPNDI with pyridine terminals and NDI-N with dimethylamino terminals—are introduced at the SnO2/perovskite buried interface to investigate the effects of terminal groups on interfacial chemistry, crystallization, and charge dynamics. Theoretical calculations and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm that DPNDI coordinates Pb2+ via pyridine N, while NDI-N coordinates via carbonyl O. Both form a dipole layer that retards crystallization, reduces defects, and minimizes voids and strain. NDI-N has a larger dipole due to intramolecular charge transfer from the dimethylamino groups to the NDI backbone, which improves SnO2 conductivity and reduces the conduction band offset to 0.08 eV, facilitating electron extraction. Consequently, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) increases from 19.88% (control) to 21.81% (DPNDI PSCs) and 24.17% (NDI-N PSCs). Unencapsulated NDI-N devices show superior storage stability, retaining 68.97% of initial PCE after 1000 h in N2 vs 50.22% for control. Under continuous maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in air, however, the encapsulated control device retains only 87.74% of its initial efficiency after 500 h, markedly lower than the 92.67% retained by encapsulated NDI-N devices.

title: Molecular Dipole Engineering of NiO Hole Injection Layers for Suppressed Exciton Quenching and High-Performance Quantum Dot Light-Emitting Diodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT), the most widely used hole injection layer (HIL) in quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs), suffers from intrinsic acidity and hygroscopicity, limiting device stability and long-term performance. To address these limitations, inorganic nickel oxide (NiO) nanoparticles (NPs) have emerged as a promising alternative HIL owing to their superior chemical robustness and favorable energy levels. However, the practical performance of NiO-based QLEDs remains constrained by surface defect states, including Ni3+ species and oxygen vacancies, which induce interfacial non-radiative recombination and hinder efficient hole injection. Here, we report a self-assembled monolayer (SAM)-assisted interfacial engineering strategy using 4-bromomethyl benzoic acid (4-BMBA) to passivate NiO NP surfaces and optimize the NiO/quantum dot interface. The 4-BMBA SAM simultaneously suppresses defect-mediated exciton quenching, improves energy-level alignment, and facilitates hole injection, resulting in significantly enhanced charge balance. Photoluminescence and time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal suppressed non-radiative recombination and prolonged exciton lifetime, while impedance spectroscopy demonstrates reduced interfacial resistance and a lower charge injection barrier. Consequently, the optimized QLEDs exhibit a low turn-on voltage of 2.2 V, a maximum luminance of 54,660 cd m–2, an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 20.34%, and a current efficiency (CE) of 28.89 cd A–1. These results represent one of the highest reported performances among QLEDs employing inorganic HILs for II–VI and III–V colloidal quantum dots. This work establishes SAM-mediated defect passivation as an effective strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and charge injection in inorganic HIL-based QLEDs, providing a versatile platform for next-generation high-efficiency and stable quantum dot optoelectronic devices.

title: Infrared–Thermal Co-driven CO2–Ethanol Coupling to Diethyl Carbonate Enabled by Electron-Rich Lattice Oxygen
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals represents a promising pathway for CO2 mitigation and utilization. The direct synthesis of diethyl carbonate (DEC) from CO2 and CH3CH2OH is particularly attractive owing to its high atom economy. However, the direct thermocatalytic synthesis of DEC remains inefficient because of unfavorable thermodynamics and the substantial kinetic barrier for coupling CO2 with ethoxy species (CH3CH2O*). Herein, an IR-thermal co-driven catalytic strategy was developed over reconstructed CeO2 (CeO2-500), enabling a DEC formation rate of 9.3 mmol g–1 h–1 without any dehydrating agent, representing a 3.1-fold enhancement compared with unreconstructed CeO2. This enhancement is attributed to the reconstruction-induced local defect structures in CeO2, which create an electron-rich lattice oxygen environment that strengthens CO2 adsorption and activation. Meanwhile, local structure modulation enhances IR light absorption and generates mildly oxidative charge carriers, which accelerate CH3CH2O* formation and promote its coupling with activated CO2 to form the key CH3CH2O-CO* intermediate, thereby boosting DEC formation. Thermal energy facilitates the transport of IR-induced charge carriers and lowers the kinetic barrier for DEC formation. This work provides an IR–thermal co-driven catalytic strategy for efficient CO2 conversion into value-added carbonates.

title: Smart pH-Switchable Nanozyme-Hydrogel Platform with Phycocyanin-Stabilized Mn-Doped Prussian Blue for Synergistic Photothermal-Multienzyme Cascade Therapy of Infected Wounds
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Infected wound healing remains a major clinical challenge due to persistent bacterial infection, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), prolonged inflammation, and impaired tissue regeneration. Here, we develop a smart composite hydrogel (PPB/PB-Mn@PC) by integrating Mn-doped Prussian blue nanozymes surface-modified with phycocyanin (PB-Mn@PC) into a dynamic polyvinyl alcohol/pullulan/borax (PPB) hydrogel. The system features pH-responsive accelerated release of PB-Mn@PC in the acidic infected microenvironment, combined with excellent self-adaptive filling, self-healing, and tissue adhesion properties. The PB-Mn@PC nanozymes exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency under 808 nm laser irradiation and multienzyme-mimicking activities. Notably, their catalytic behavior dynamically switches: predominant SOD/CAT-like ROS scavenging under neutral conditions for cytoprotection, and enhanced POD-like activity under acidic conditions that supports bacterial killing without a proportional increase in freely diffusible ·OH, thereby limiting collateral oxidative burden. In vitro, the composite hydrogel demonstrates excellent biocompatibility, efficient broad-spectrum antibacterial activity (including biofilm disruption), ROS scavenging, and promotion of macrophage M2 polarization. In vivo, in S. aureus-infected full-thickness wound models, the smart hydrogel significantly reduces bacterial burden, accelerates wound closure, enhances re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis, while effectively suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-α). This work presents a rationally designed smart hydrogel platform that integrates dynamic mechanics, intelligent microenvironment-responsive release, and synergistic photothermal-multienzyme therapy, offering a promising strategy for the efficient management of infected wounds.

title: Sequential Defect Engineering Enables External-Reductant-Free In Situ Formation of Cu2S Electron Reservoirs in a TiO2/SCN/Cu2S S-Scheme Heterojunction for Noble-Metal-Free Photocatalytic H2 Evolution
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Noble-metal-free photocatalytic H2 evolution is often limited by the need for external reductants to generate low-valence cocatalysts and by poorly controlled interfacial charge transport. Here, we establish a sequential defect-engineering strategy that uses trace sulfur in sulfur-doped carbon nitride (SCN) as an intrinsic reductant and sulfur source to construct Cu2S directly on a preformed TiO2/SCN heterojunction. This sequence simultaneously avoids noble metals and external reducing agents while promoting intimate Cu-S interfacial bonding and the formation of oxygen and copper vacancies. The resulting TiO2-SCN-Cu2S S-scheme heterojunction delivers 38.06 mmol g−1 H2 in 6 h (average rate: 6.34 mmol g−1 h−1), 21-fold higher than TiO2-SCN and 1.57-fold higher than a TiO2-SCN-Pt benchmark containing 3.6 wt % Pt, tested at the same total catalyst mass. Experiments, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, finite-difference time-domain (FDTD), and machine-learning trend analysis collectively show that the copper-addition sequence controls copper speciation, defect population, light harvesting, and interfacial charge separation. This work identifies sequentially programmed Cu2S formation and vacancy generation as an integrated design strategy for reductant-free, noble-metal-free S-scheme photocatalysts.

title: Tuning Surface Termination of Perovskite Nanocrystals to Control Interfacial Charge Transfer and Photocatalytic Efficiency
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Efficient extraction of photogenerated charge carriers remains a major challenge in metal halide perovskite nanocrystal (MHP NC) photocatalysis because of rapid electron–hole recombination at the nanocrystal surface. Although interfacial binding between the NC surface and charge-acceptor molecules is known to facilitate charge separation, the influence of nanocrystal surface termination on this process remains largely unexplored. Herein, we investigate how the surface termination of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals (CPB NCs) regulates interfacial binding with para-substituted aniline (PSA) hole acceptors bearing –SH, –COOH, and –NH2 anchoring groups and how these interactions influence photocatalytic performance. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal a complete reversal in hole-transfer efficiency upon changing the surface termination from Pb-rich to Br-rich, demonstrating that surface-dependent preferential interactions govern interfacial charge-transfer dynamics. These findings are further validated through the photoreductive homocoupling of phenacyl bromide via C–C bond coupling, where Pb-rich CPB NCs exhibit significantly superior photocatalytic activity owing to stronger coordination-like interactions with the anchoring groups. Overall, this work establishes surface termination as a critical design parameter for controlling interfacial charge transfer and provides a rational strategy for developing highly efficient perovskite nanocrystal photocatalysts.

title: Metallic–Ionic Copper Cooperative Interfacial Engineering Enables Stabler and Fast-Charging Silicon Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon is considered one of the most promising anode materials for next-generation lithium-ion batteries because of its exceptionally high theoretical capacity. Nevertheless, its practical use is constrained by coupled mechanical degradation, unstable solid electrolyte interphase evolution, and sluggish charge transport during cycling. Herein, we propose a previously unexplored metallic–ionic cooperative interfacial engineering strategy that fundamentally reconstructs the silicon interface through the synergistic integration of a hydrogen-bonded mucic acid network and hybrid Cu0/Cu+/Cu2+species. Unlike conventional metal modification, the coexistence of metallic and ionic copper forms a multifunctional interface that can simultaneously accommodate stress, improve electron/Li+ transport, and regulate the chemical evolution of the interfacial phase, resulting in the formation of a thin, dense, inorganic SEI rich in LiF, which suppresses the continued decomposition of the electrolyte and interfacial degradation. Benefiting from this integrated regulation mechanism, the optimized Si@MA*Cu anode exhibits an ultralow electrode thickness expansion of only 4.5% after 200 cycles, corresponding to a 97.3% reduction relative to pristine silicon, together with a reversible capacity of 1550.0 mAh g–1 after 400 cycles at 1 A g–1 and a high–rate capacity of 1375.5 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1. Electrochemical tests show faster charge transfer, enhanced Li+ diffusion, and dominant pseudocapacitance, while DFT calculations reveal that hybrid Cu states reconstruct interfacial electronic structure, boost Fermi–level electronic density, strengthen Li adsorption, and lower Li+ migration barriers. This study establishes a paradigm for metal-ion synergy by combining mechanical adaptation, interfacial phase control, and charge transport, providing a general interfacial design principle for developing durable, fast-charging, and high-energy alloy-type battery electrodes.

title: Intrinsic High-κ Elastic Dielectrics from Dual-Fluorinated Polyurethane Urea Enable Low-Voltage Stretchable Organic Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Low-voltage operation in intrinsically stretchable transistors fundamentally relies on gate dielectrics that reconcile intrinsic stretchability with a high dielectric constant (high-κ). However, reconciling enhanced dielectric performance with robust mechanical resilience remains a persistent challenge. Here, we report a molecular engineering strategy to synthesize a series of functionalized polyurethane urea (PUU) by rationally incorporating distinct functional groups into the hard-segment domains. Among the synthesized variants, the difluorinated analogue (2F-PUU) achieves an optimal trade-off, combining a high κ of 7.06 at 1 kHz, exceptional stretchability up to 1623%, strain-insensitive dielectric behavior, solvent reprocessability, and an ultralow surface roughness of 0.273 nm. Stretchable organic transistors employing 2F-PUU as the gate dielectric operate at a low voltage of –10 V and sustain stable electrical performance under 50% tensile strain. Moreover, a 5 × 5 transistor array based on 2F-PUU delivers a 100% fabrication yield, with a peak mobility of 0.51 cm2 V–1 s–1 and a maximum on/off current ratio exceeding 104. Collectively, this work establishes a viable molecular design roadmap for intrinsically stretchable high-κ dielectrics, paving the way toward low-power, mechanically durable stretchable organic electronics.

title: Isolation of Open‐Shell Vinylidene Complexes of Iridium, Ruthenium, and Osmium
abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐shell vinylidene complexes are prone to undergo fast, ligand‐centered radical reactions. Herein, we describe the synthesis of paramagnetic Ir, Ru, and Os complexes with terminal N‐heterocyclic vinylidene ligands. Under inert conditions, these complexes remain stable over extended periods, allowing for isolation on a preparative scale and crystallographic analyses (for Ir and Ru). The results of computational investigations, EPR spectroscopic, and reactivity studies imply that the radical is largely localized on the vinylidene ligand.

title: VEGF-Rich Engineered Apoptotic Extracellular Vesicles Loaded with Quercetin for Androgenetic Alopecia Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is a progressive hair loss disorder characterized by follicular miniaturization, oxidative stress-induced dermal papilla cell apoptosis, downregulated angiogenic genes, and insufficient vascularization in the perifollicular microenvironment. Current pharmacotherapies are limited by transient efficacy and side effects, necessitating novel delivery systems that simultaneously address the vascular insufficiency and oxidative burden to halt and reverse follicular miniaturization. In this study, we constructed genetically engineered apoptotic extracellular vesicles (ApoEV) from adipose mesenchymal stem cells (AMSCs) that were functionalized with vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) to promote angiogenesis and loaded with Quercetin (QUE) for antioxidant defense (VEGF ApoEV@QUE). The VEGF ApoEV@QUE significantly promoted human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) proliferation, migration, and tube formation. In addition, it promoted dermal papilla cells (DPCs) proliferation, protected DPCs from oxidative stress by activating the Wnt/β-catenin and AKT/GSK3β signaling pathways. In the AGA mouse model, subcutaneous injection of VEGF ApoEV@QUE accelerated the telogen-to-anagen transition, increased hair follicle density, and enhanced perifollicular vascularization compared to monotherapies. Biosafety analysis revealed no overt systemic toxicity in this short-term model. This study demonstrates that engineering ApoEV to co-deliver surface-anchored angiogenic factors and intracellular antioxidants provides an enhanced dual-action therapeutic strategy for AGA.

title: An Injectable Hydrogel Integrating Antibacterial and Antioxidant Functions for the Treatment of Periodontitis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by microbial dysbiosis and sustained by a dysregulated host response, in which excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial dysfunction, and persistent inflammation contribute to progressive periodontal tissue destruction. Here, we developed LAEPL-SA, an injectable composite hydrogel prepared by conjugating α-lipoic acid (LA) to ε-poly-l-lysine (EPL) and incorporating the resulting LAEPL into a sodium alginate (SA) network. The system was designed to simultaneously reduce the microbial challenge and excessive oxidative/inflammatory injury within the periodontal microenvironment. EPL contributed direct cationic antibacterial activity, whereas LA provided antioxidant and cytoprotective effects associated with reduced ROS accumulation. LAEPL-SA exhibited favorable injectability, self-healing behavior, rheological stability, wet hydroxyapatite-surface retention, and antibacterial activity. Compared with LA-SA, LAEPL-SA showed stronger antioxidant effects and improved protection against oxidative injury. In H2O2-stimulated human periodontal ligament stem cells, LAEPL-SA reduced intracellular and mitochondrial ROS accumulation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, decreased apoptosis, and suppressed inflammatory responses. In a ligature-induced rat periodontitis model, LAEPL-SA reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure, decreased osteoclast activity, and alleviated alveolar bone resorption. These protective effects were accompanied by activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway. Collectively, LAEPL-SA provides a multifunctional local therapeutic platform that integrates antibacterial activity with attenuation of excessive oxidative and inflammatory stress for periodontitis treatment.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: Nitrogen‐Rich Covalent Organic Frameworks Enable Reversible Lithium Deposition in Anode‐Free Lithium Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Poor lithium reversibility and sluggish interfacial kinetics limit the areal capacity and rate capability of anode‐free lithium batteries. A nitrogen‐rich covalent organic framework (COF) as an interphase layer promotes uniform lithium deposition, enabling plating/stripping at 20 mAh/cm 2 in Li/Cu cells and anode‐free full‐cell operation at 4.1 mAh/cm 2 , as reported by Z. Ouyang, S. Zheng, S. Li, et al., Angewandte Chemie Novit 2 (2026): e70027.

title: A quasi-particle theory for the dynamics of polycatenated architected materials
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Architected materials derive unusual mechanical responses from geometry rather than mostly by their chemistry. Polycatenated architected materials (PAMs), composed of interlinked rigid units, have been shown to display hybrid solid–fluid behaviors. Frequency-sweep rheological experiments have revealed a transition from strong shear thinning at low frequencies to pronounced shear thickening above a critical frequency. Because neighboring PAM units are connected, rather than freely rearranging, conventional granular theories do not readily explain their behavior. Here, we develop a one-dimensional analytical model to capture the frequency-response of PAMs based on a quasi-particle description. Quasi-particles are defined as segments of PAMs that are either fully stretched or fully compressed. Modeling their interactions produces an effective viscosity that captures both asymptotic scaling laws and the critical frequency. These predictions agree quantitatively with simulations and experiments. Our results reveal that PAM’s frequency-dependent response arises from competing effects between dissipation and inertia. More broadly, our results establish an analytical foundation for understanding the dynamics of PAMs and provide design principles for tuning their responses.

title: Membrane‐Fusion Navigated Cell Membrane Anchoring Enhances Pyroptosis for Photoimmunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Pyroptosis, a membrane disruptive and highly immunogenic form of programmed cell death, remains underexploited in cancer photoimmunotherapy due to the lack of general design principles beyond photosensitizer engineering. Here, we establish a membrane confined strategy that directly programs pyroptotic execution by targeting the plasma membrane as the primary reaction interface. A membrane fusogenic liposomal system enables precise anchoring of a caged perylene bisimides (PBI) onto the cell membrane, bypassing complex molecular modification. Upon light irradiation, PBI undergoes photocyclization to generate an active photosensitizer (CBI) and a protonic acid in situ. This dual output synergistically amplifies reactive oxygen species (ROS) production within a confined lipid environment, promoting lipid peroxidation, GPX4 downregulation, and membrane destabilization. Consequently, pyroptosis is efficiently triggered alongside ferroptosis, leading to enhanced tumor cell killing and immune activation both in vitro and in vivo. By shifting the design paradigm from molecular optimization to cell membrane control, this work reframes the plasma membrane from a passive barrier into an active reaction platform, providing a general and modular strategy for programmable pyroptosis‐based photoimmunotherapy.

title: Coupled hydrogen spillover and CO2 activation sites in high-entropy catalysts for CO2 reduction
abstract: Converting CO2 into useful chemicals via reverse water-gas shift reaction offers a promising route toward sustainable carbon utilization. However, catalysts often struggle to coordinate hydrogen and CO2 activation while remaining stable under demanding reaction conditions. The present work developed high-entropy oxides with Li and Al dual-atom doping to promote cooperative alloy-oxide interfaces with coupled H2 and CO2 activation sites, thereby enabling fast, selective, and stable CO production. These findings provide a general strategy for integrating multiple functions into robust catalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

abstract: This Review highlights lithium–arene complexes (LACs) as versatile liquid lithium sources and establishes the PAH/LAC pair as a reversible lithium carrier, enabling lithium extraction and donation across the battery lifecycle.

title: Anode-free configurations through separator-mediated interfacial regulation for practical sodium metal batteries
abstract: Functionally engineered separators regulate Na + transport and interfacial chemistry. They homogenize ion flux, stabilize the SEI, and suppress dendrites to improve reversibility, especially in anode-free sodium metal batteries.

abstract: A polymerizable ionic buffer suppresses ion migration at perovskite grain boundaries through chemical stabilization and physical confinement.
