title: Binuclear copper enzymes enable selective radical (pseudo)halogenation
abstract: Synthetically valuable new-to-nature reactions in copper enzymes remain largely underexploited in chemical synthesis. Now, the combination of binuclear copper enzymes and a photoredox catalyst can efficiently perform enantioselective decarboxylative (pseudo)halogenation starting from redox-active esters.

title: The power of O vacancies in electrocatalysis
abstract: Non-stoichiometric oxide materials are essential to chemistry, but controlling their synthesis towards a tuneable number of unpaired electrons trapped in the oxygen vacancies remains challenging. Now, a new synthetic strategy leveraging template chemicals renders these materials available for electron-driven electrocatalytic selectivity.

title: Sustained changes to urban mobility after COVID-19 reinforced socioeconomic inequalities in Argentina, Chile and Colombia
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Urban mobility is central to economic activity, social inclusion and access to services. COVID-19 caused disruptions to mobility globally, yet its long-term impacts in Latin America remain poorly understood. Using > 170 million anonymised and aggregated location records from Meta-Facebook users in Argentina, Chile and Colombia (April 2020-May 2022), we examine changes in overall mobility volume relative to pre-pandemic baselines across socioeconomic and rural-urban gradients. Two years after the pandemic onset, mobility in the highest-density urban cores remained ~ 25–50% below baseline across the three countries, while the top 33% most affluent communities had not returned to baseline. These differences are explained by the scale of the initial mobility shock rather than by subsequent recovery rates. Our findings reveal how a global shock can entrench disparities in human mobility, with implications for urban resilience and planning in unequal nations. Our study underscores the need for proactive policies to prevent long-lasting mobility inequalities.

title: Disagreements in global urban growth projections amplify uncertainties in deforestation and carbon emissions
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Global urbanization is profoundly reshaping 21st-century land systems, yet its future trajectory remains highly uncertain. Existing projections exhibit divergent urban growth patterns even under identical socioeconomic scenarios. Here, by synthesizing six urban growth projections, we reveal substantial disagreements in the extent and location of urban growth by 2100. These disagreements are amplified by land-system feedbacks, driving cross-dataset variation in urban-induced deforestation (1.75–4.91 million km2) through direct forest conversion and indirect cropland displacement, assuming lost production is compensated by cropland expansion elsewhere. The associated emissions exhibit an absolute range of 29 to 76 GtCO2 by 2100. Across 100 countries, this range accounts for an average of 3% of unconditional Nationally Determined Contribution emission budgets, reaching 26% in specific countries. Our findings establish cross-dataset disagreement as an important source of uncertainty in land and climate assessments, highlighting the need for robust spatial planning across plausible urban futures.

title: Dominant role of Southeast Asian emissions in anthropogenic increases in global tropospheric ozone and southward tropical growth, 2000–2019
abstract: Widespread increases in tropospheric ozone (O3) have been reported over the past two decades, with changes in anthropogenic emissions, particularly in Asia, identified as an important driver. Here we use global model sensitivity simulations to quantify changes in global tropospheric O3 burden and associated radiative forcing (RF) attributable to anthropogenic emission changes from 2000 to 2019, and assess the contributions from different Asian regions. Changes in anthropogenic emissions increased the global tropospheric O3 burden by 12.0 ± 0.5 Tg and global mean RF by 0.030 ± 0.002 W m–2 under fixed 2015–2019 meteorological fields. The increase was larger during 2000–2010 than during 2010–2019 and occurred predominantly in the tropics. Southeast Asia was the largest regional contributor over 2000–2019, accounting for 5.7 ± 0.4 Tg of the simulated global tropospheric O3 burden increase and 0.020 ± 0.002 W m–2 of RF. During 2010–2019, the increase in tropospheric O3 burden attributable to anthropogenic emission changes was larger over 0–30°S than over 0–30°N, indicating a southward shift in the tropical response driven primarily by Southeast Asian emissions. East Asia shifted from a major positive contributor during 2000–2010 to a negative contributor during 2010–2019. These results highlight the increasing importance of anthropogenic emissions from tropical Asia in shaping the global distribution of tropospheric O3 and its climate forcing.

title: Programming Sodium-Storage Kinetics through Linear Quinone Oligomerization
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quinone-based organic cathodes enable reversible multielectron redox reactions but suffer from dissolution and sluggish sodium-storage kinetics. Here, two structurally homologous linear quinone oligomers, biphenyl–quinone dimer (2BQ) and terphenyl–quinone trimer (3BQ), are compared to elucidate how backbone extension regulates sodium storage. Compared with 2BQ, 3BQ exhibits reduced crystallinity, enhanced electrochemical utilization, a narrower HOMO–LUMO gap, and lower oxidation reorganization energy. Consequently, 3BQ delivers a reversible capacity of 350 mA h g–1 at 0.05C and retains 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 1C, with enhanced rate capability and cycling stability. Operando FTIR and state-dependent XPS reveal reversible C=O/C–O–Na conversion, while density functional theory calculations elucidate an extended multielectron sodiation sequence. These findings establish controlled linear quinone oligomerization as an effective, rational molecular design strategy to reduce apparent dissolution tendency and improve carbonyl-site utilization and sodium-storage kinetics, providing insights into the development of advanced organic cathodes for rechargeable sodium-ion batteries.

title: Liquid Metal Interlayers Enable Zero-Pressure Sulfide Solid Electrolyte Lithium Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal anodes are essential for high-energy-density batteries with solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but the lithium-SSE interface suffers from contact loss and current constriction during cycling. External stack pressure can enhance contact retention but adds system-level limitations and accelerates lithium filament penetration. Here, a room-temperature liquid sodium–potassium (NaK) interlayer is demonstrated to stabilize the lithium–sulfide SSE interface under nominally zero stack pressure by combining stress-free morphological adaptability with Li transport capability. In situ X-ray computed tomography and other analytical methods reveal that the liquid layer reconfigures to preserve interfacial contact during Li plating/stripping. Finite Li solubility in the NaK also creates a dissolved-Li-mediated electrochemical pathway that supports Li stripping from a distant reservoir. The dual mechanical and transport functions of NaK enable stable full-cell cycling (600 cycles, >2 mAh cm–2) with layered-oxide composite cathodes under nominally zero applied stack pressure. These findings highlight a fundamental interfacial design concept based on a compliant interlayer that accommodates morphological evolution while supporting Li transport under minimal mechanical confinement.

title: Tailorable deep eutectic solvents for sustainable lignocellulose refining: from platform design to value-added products
abstract: Efficient utilization of renewable carbon requires lignocellulosic biorefineries that can deconstruct plant cell walls while preserving the value of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), constructed from programmable hydrogen-bond acceptors and donors, have emerged as tunable media for lignocellulose processing. This review discusses recent progress in the rational design of DESs for lignocellulosic biorefineries, focusing on binary, ternary, hydrated, biphasic, catalytic and biocompatible systems. By regulating acidity/basicity, polarity, hydrogen-bonding ability, viscosity, water tolerance, active sites and phase behavior, DESs can selectively disrupt lignin-carbohydrate complexes, stabilize or functionalize the components, and direct the downstream transformation of the components toward bio-based chemicals and functional polymeric materials. Component-oriented valorization routes are summarized, including cellulose-derived functional materials and platform chemicals, lignin-derived aromatics and functional polymers, and hemicellulose-derived furan chemicals. Key barriers to industrial deployment are also critically examined, including high viscosity, mass-transfer limitations, solvent loss, energy-intensive recovery, feedstock heterogeneity, incomplete mechanistic understanding and insufficient techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Future opportunities are highlighted in artificial-intelligence-guided DESs discovery, novel membrane and electrodialysis DES-recovery technologies, DES-compatible chemo-biocatalysis and closed-loop process integration. Tailorable DESs are expected to evolve from empirical solvent systems into predictive, recyclable and product-oriented platforms for sustainable production of bio-based chemicals, materials and fuels.

title: Chemical defects in semiconducting polymers and their impact on reproducibility and device performance
abstract: Synthesizing semiconducting polymers often introduces structural defects, altering optoelectronic properties and directly impairing device performance. This Perspective details defect origins, evaluation methods and mitigation strategies, demonstrating how controlling structural variability resolves batch-to-batch inconsistency while unlocking novel materials design opportunities.

title: Comprehensive synthesis of K48/K63 ubiquitin pentamers by graph-empowered automation
abstract:
Abstract
                  Linear, branched and heterotypic ubiquitin (Ub) chains regulate essential cellular processes, yet their structural and functional analysis remains limited by the difficulty of preparing defined, homogeneous samples. Here we establish a fully automated platform for the comprehensive synthesis of all 56 K48/K63-linked Ub tetramers and pentamers, by iterative cycles of K48- or K63-specific chemoenzymatic conjugations of chemically synthesized Ub monomers bearing a fast-cleaving lysine protecting group compatible with folded proteins. A graph-based digital encoding of Ub chain topologies enabled systematic enumeration and filtering of reaction pathways, guiding the selection of synthetic routes. This computational system generates reagent maps and executable code to direct iterative deprotection and conjugation cycles on a standard, laboratory liquid-handling robot. All 14 Ub tetramers and 42 Ub pentamers were obtained with high fidelity, as validated by SDS–PAGE and mass spectrometry. This work establishes a general framework for automated protein conjugate synthesis and provides access to the complete space of K48/K63 branched ubiquitin chains.

title: Synergistic Ethylene Glycol Synthesis via Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction Coupled With CH 3 OH Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Paired photoredox catalysis enables co‐valorization of CO 2 and small molecules to high‐value chemicals via concurrent oxidation and reduction half‐reactions. However, most systems feature decoupled half‐reactions with no intrinsic substrate‐product interplay, merely utilizing electrons and holes separately, and failing to realize convergent chemical synthesis. Herein, we demonstrate a tandem photoredox‐photothermal catalytic system for efficient ethylene glycol (EG) synthesis, comprising (i) the photoredox catalysis of CO 2 reduction integrated with C─C coupling of methanol (CH 3 OH) to EG over Cu‐doped Zn 0.75 Cd 0.25 S catalysts, and (ii) the photothermal conversion of syngas to CH 3 OH over commercial CuZnAl catalysts. Of note, the CH 3 OH formed in situ via CO 2 reduction can feed into the pool of oxidation substrates, while the co‐generated syngas (ideal H 2 /CO ratio ≈ 2) is further converted to additional CH 3 OH and then recirculated as a supplemental oxidation substrate. Such a tandem catalytic design achieves high atom‐ and redox‐economy for EG synthesis, delivering an exceptional apparent quantum yield of 24.1%, outperforming those previously reported for CH 3 OH coupling to EG under an inert atmosphere. This work highlights the promise of orchestrating photoredox‐based closed‐loop catalytic architectures for value‐added C 2+ chemical synthesis with high efficiency and selectivity.

title: Targeting chemotherapy-induced CD200 via a nucleoside-enhanced nanocarrier for cancer immunochemotherapy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has transformed cancer therapy, yet its efficacy is frequently undermined by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In addition, the immune-related toxicities restrict combination therapy targeting several immune checkpoints. Here, we identify chemotherapy-induced CD200 upregulation as a stress-adaptive resistance mechanism that reinforces tumor immune evasion under treatment pressure. Leveraging a tumor-restricted, nucleoside-enhanced nanocarrier, we achieve spatially selective silencing of tumor-intrinsic CD200, thereby reprogramming the tumor immune microenvironment, enhancing antitumor efficacy, and enabling effective combination with PD-1 blockade. Importantly, this strategy minimizes the colitis exacerbation associated with systemic CD200/PD-1 dual blockade in a DSS-induced susceptibility model, suggesting its potential to preserve immune homeostasis while reducing immune-related toxicity. Together, our findings establish CD200 as a context-dependent immune resistance node and demonstrate a nanotechnology-based framework for precise and safe immune checkpoint modulation.

title: Single‐Atom Based Dual‐Metal‐Active‐Site Catalysts for N 2 Conversion to Ammonia and Urea Synthesis: Geometric Coupling, Electronic Polarization, Reaction Partitioning, and Intermediate Steering
abstract: ABSTRACT N 2 conversion is increasingly recognized not as a simple activation process of an inert molecule, but as a coupled reaction network that requires synchronized N 2 adsorption, electron/proton transfer, intermediate hydrogenation, C─N coupling, product release, and side‐reaction suppression. Single‐atom catalysts provide atomic precision, well‐defined coordination environments, and tunable electronic structures, but their isolated active centers often struggle to satisfy the multiple and sometimes conflicting requirements of complex N 2 conversion. Single‐atom‐based dual‐metal‐active‐site catalysts are therefore emerging as cooperative catalytic architectures that integrate an atomically dispersed metal single atom with a second metal site in the form of an isolated atom, cluster, or nanoparticle. This review establishes a structure‐function framework for understanding these catalysts, focusing on dual‐site adsorption geometry, asymmetric electronic polarization, bifunctional reaction partitioning, and intermediate‐specific stabilization. Recent advances in ammonia and urea synthesis are discussed to reveal how dual sites regulate N 2 activation, proton supply, intermediate evolution, and selective C─N bond formation. Particular attention is given to metal‐metal interactions, support‐mediated charge redistribution, hydrogen transfer, and pathway‐dependent intermediate binding. Finally, key challenges, including precise dual‐site construction, quantitative synergy identification, and practical compatibility, are highlighted to guide the rational design of next‐generation dual‐site catalysts for sustainable N 2 conversion.

title: Beyond Lewis Acidity: Thiophilicity and Redox Stability as Design Principles for Sulphur‐Containing Polymerisation Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Catalysts for the ring‐opening copolymerisation (ROCOP) of sulphur‐containing monomers are almost invariably inherited from all‐oxygen chemistry, where performance tracks the barrier of the rate‐determining propagation step. We show that this transfer fails. The activity of Cr(III), Co(III) and Zn(II) complexes of a common salicylimine scaffold cannot be explained by computationally tracking monomer insertions and metal activity is better predicted off‐cycle. A revised experimentally supported computational hypothesis implicates metal thiolates, generated by side‐reactions at the chain end, to deactivate the catalyst by either binding too tightly to or reducing the metal centre. The resulting computational descriptors, thiophilicity and redox stability, are distinct from Lewis acidity and chemical hardness, and predicted Al(III) to be competent. Al(III) catalysis delivers recyclable sulphur‐containing copolymers with a high apparent weight of M n = 238.6 kg/mol. This unlocks previously underexplored processing methods for these types of materials such as melt‐spinning and scCO 2 ‐foaming. Our results suggest new structure–activity design rules for sulphur‐containing polymerisation catalysis which are urgently required to obtain technologically useful materials.

title: An Expandable Library of Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium‐Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐polymer‐electrolytes (SPEs) offer alternatives to next‐generation solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries, promising advantages in mechanical‐compliance, processability, cost‐effectiveness, and safety. While tremendous efforts have generated diverse SPEs since 1970s, SPE‐practicality remains limited by the trade‐offs among ion‐conductivity, high‐voltage stability, and Li 0 ‐electrolyte compatibility. Here, we establish the first SPE library covering 12 SPEs across five polymer families, which allows us to collect large datasets on chemistry, interfacial, and electrochemical properties that unveil their hidden connections. Correlation analysis of these descriptors reveals binding‐strength between polymer and Li + , subtle variations in polymer molecular structure, and solid‐electrolyte‐interphase composition as dictating factors. Also discovered is that the standard deviation of coulombic‐efficiency rather than its average value governs the battery cycling stability. The SPE library can be rapidly expanded through two structural engineering pathways: grafting diverse functional segments onto backbones and constructing compositionally‐complex SPEs. As a proof‐of‐concept, we fabricate several such SPEs and find improved high‐voltage stability through gradually increasing the complexity of the polymer matrices. A terpolymer‐based acrylates SPE exhibits outstanding Li 0 plating/stripping over 1800 h, stable cycling in LiCoO 2 ||Li battery with 100% capacity retention and an average coulombic‐efficiency of 99.91% ± 0.09% over 100 cycles. This work provides a transformative framework to design the future polymer materials.

title: Ring‐Retaining Polymerization of Vinylidenecyclopropanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Commodity feedstock‐derived vinylidenecyclopropanes (VDCPs) are a new class of allenic monomers stereoelectronically intermediate between butatrienes and allenes. While their butatriene character drives the C5 ring‐opening polymerization (C5‐ROP), the complementary allene‐type polymerization mode remains elusive. Herein we report this new pathway for VDCPs. Organonickel catalysts with coordinating counterions enable C2 ring‐retaining polymerization (C2‐RRP), yielding pendant alkylidenecyclopropane moieties. Computations ascribe this reactivity to strain‐release alkene coordination, which further enables one‐pot diblock copolymerization with conventional allenes.

title: Retained fuel removal from plasma-facing materials: effects of baking methods and hydrogen isotope exchange
abstract: Tungsten (W) is a prominent plasma-facing material for deuterium–tritium (D–T) fusion reactors, yet T fuel retention in W poses critical challenges to safety and operational viability. This study systematically compares three baking methods—vacuum baking, H2 gas atmosphere baking, and hydrogen (H) plasma baking—for removing D retained in W at 513 K, simulating realistic conditions for T removal in reactors. Experimental results demonstrate that D removal efficiencies reach 75% for vacuum baking after 16 h, 83% for H2 atmosphere baking after 16 h, and 99% for H plasma baking after 1 h. The superior performance of H2 atmosphere and H plasma baking is primarily driven by hydrogen isotope (HI) exchange, with efficiency strongly dependent on the concentration of H introduced into W. Higher H concentrations promote more complete exchange, leading to significantly reduced D retention. A multi-isotope Fill Level model was developed to simulate the end-to-end H plasma exchange process. The simulation reproduces the experimentally observed D removal kinetics and the emergence of HD desorption, with the D retention in good agreement with measurements. The pronounced disparity between H2 atmosphere baking and H plasma baking is fundamentally governed by the quantity of H entering W: H plasma promotes significantly greater H ingress, thereby enhancing HI exchange and resulting in a drastic reduction in D retention. This work provides both experimental validation and modeling support for HI exchange as an efficient T removal strategy.

title: Confinement property in the JT-60SA first operation phase
abstract: In JT-60SA, the global energy confinement time has been evaluated to be – s for 1 MA hydrogen discharges and compared with the ITERL-96P(th) scaling. Because local measurements of ion temperature , electron density and effective charge are not available in the first operation phase and the number of discharges and their parameter range are limited, the present results should not be considered definitive. As heating power increased, tends to shorten in the same trend as the scaling. is shorter than the scaling but approaches the scaling with increasing density. For 0.4–0.6 MW ohmic heating plasmas, increases with increasing collisionality and saturates. For 0.6–0.8 MW ohmic heating and electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECH) plasmas, continues to increase up to higher collisionality and reaches the scaling. The turbulence simulations with the trapped gyroLandau-fluid model assuming a linear profile show that the dominant turbulence mode is trapped electron modes. The linear growth rate decreases with increasing collisionality and saturates at a low level in the 0.4–0.6 MW ohmic heating plasma, suggesting the transition from the linear ohmic confinement regime to the saturated ohmic confinement regime. For 0.6–0.8 MW ohmic heating and ECH plasmas, the saturation occurs at higher collisionality, indicating that the linear confinement regime extends to higher collisionality. The global particle confinement time excluding recycling contributions, , has also been evaluated to be s, approximately twice , from the frequency responses in a density feedback control experiment. From and the effective particle confinement time including recycling , a recycling coefficient is obtained as . The sub-unity recycling coefficient indicates that wall recycling is insufficient to maintain plasma density, consistent with hydrogen retention due to the first hydrogen discharge with continuous gas injection.

title: Experimental and numerical investigation of backstreaming positive ions in an RF-driven negative ion source
abstract: Backstreaming positive ions (BSPIs) are an unavoidable byproduct in high-power negative ion-based neutral beam injection systems, posing a critical challenge to the long-pulse operational stability of ion sources due to the significant heat loads and material erosion they induce. This paper presents a comprehensive experimental and numerical investigation into the generation, spatial distribution, and thermal effects of BSPIs in the dual-radio-frequency (RF)-driver negative ion source at the HONOR test facility of CRAFT. Using a water-flow calorimetry diagnostic system, the dependence of the BSPI power fraction (PBSPI/Pbeam) on key operational parameters was systematically studied. The results show that the PBSPI/Pbeam ratio increases monotonically with the source filling pressure, rising from ∼2.05% at 0.3 Pa to ∼3.15% at 0.57 Pa. A non-monotonic dependence on beam energy is observed, with the ratio peaking at ∼2.65% at 161 keV. This trend is attributed to the competition between the improved geometric transmission efficiency of BSPIs—resulting from reduced beam divergence at moderate energies—and the intrinsic decrease in collision cross-sections at higher energies. Furthermore, the ratio is found to decrease with increasing extracted beam current, which is explained by the space-charge-induced beam divergence that reduces the geometric transmission efficiency through the acceleration grids. Distinct BSPI bombardment traces on the backplate exhibit an array pattern corresponding to the plasma grid apertures. Coupled thermal-fluid-solid simulations, incorporating the measured heat loads, indicate that under typical high-power conditions (190 kV, 16.2 A), the maximum backplate temperature remains well below the material safety limit. This work clarifies the key mechanisms governing BSPI generation and validates the thermal reliability of the backplate design, providing a solid basis for the development of high-power negative-ion-based neutral beam injection (NNBI) systems.

title: Grain boundary effects on surface modifications of tungsten under fusion-relevant helium plasma irradiation: coarse-grained vs nano-grained microstructures
abstract: Grain refinement is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving radiation resistance in nuclear materials, but the influence of grain boundaries (GBs) on helium (He) plasma irradiation-induced surface modifications in tungsten (W) remains unclear. Here, we compare the surface morphology evolution and subsurface bubble distributions of coarse-grained and nano-grained W under fusion-relevant He plasma irradiation. The samples were exposed simultaneously to 90 eV He ions at 1173 K. Although both microstructures ultimately developed similar fuzz composed of nanoscale tendrils, their early-stage evolution of surface roughening exhibited distinct differences. In the nano-grained W film, ∼600 nm thick, surface roughening was initiated by anomalous bubble growth at grain junctions. In contrast, coarse-grained W exhibited pronounced crystallographic-orientation-dependent roughening. Subsequent tendril nucleation and growth occurred in both microstructures, preferentially at highly convex surface regions. Moreover, subsurface bubbles were confined mainly to a shallow region approximately 100–200 nm beneath coarse-grained W, whereas they permeated the entire nano-grained film. These results indicate that GB-mediated bubble dynamics primarily govern surface evolution during the fuzz-incubation stage, while interface curvature and capillary-driven diffusion dominate tendril nucleation and subsequent growth. Thus, GBs exert a decisive influence during early-stage surface roughening but have limited effect on the later development of fuzz. These findings provide insight into the distinct and common mechanisms governing He-induced surface modification in W with different grain sizes and support a capillary-growth framework for fuzz formation.

title: Transport due to density gradient driven TEM & UM in advanced tokamak plasma configurations: role of negative triangularity and magnetic shear reversal
abstract: Advanced tokamak configurations can modify microturbulence through changes in magnetic equilibrium, trapped-particle dynamics, resonance conditions. In this work, global gyrokinetic simulations are used to study density-gradient-driven trapped-electron turbulence in tight-aspect-ratio shaped plasmas, focusing on the role of negative triangularity and reversed magnetic shear. In the positive versus negative triangularity comparison, negative triangularity is found to stabilize high- modes and reduce saturated particle diffusivity by approximately . Energy-exchange diagnostics show that this reduction is associated with a weaker participation of weakly trapped electrons, while zonal-flow shearing remains comparable between the two configurations. In the reversed-shear case for positive triangularity, despite larger linear growth rates, the saturated electron diffusivity is reduced by approximately as compared to positive magnetic shear case. This reduction is attributed to the diminished radial support of the perturbation in the reversed magnetic shear region. The combined effect of reversed magnetic shear and negative triangularity is further investigated, revealing that although both independently reduce saturated transport levels, their combination leads to enhanced nonlinear transport.

title: Impact of helium cooling channels and flow channel inserts on magnetohydrodynamic mixed convection in a liquid metal blanket
abstract: On the pathway toward full simulations for a liquid metal blanket, this study extends the work of Chen et al (2022 Nucl. Fusion62 026042) on mixed convection in a full-scale dual coolant lead lithium blanket by considering a more realistic case. In this study, the model incorporates the complex geometry of characteristic sub-components, including helium cooling channels and flow channel inserts (FCIs), to investigate their impacts in several key metrics: (1) Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) pressure drop, (2) electromagnetic coupling, (3) velocity distribution in both the bulk and gap regions, (4) flow behavior in blanket components, and (5) heat transfer. Based on the MHD-UCAS platform, these multi-region, multiphysics direct numerical simulations are performed on a highly refined mesh of cells under conditions relevant to the fusion reactor: the applied magnetic field of 5 T ( ), the PbLi velocity of 0.1 m s–1 in poloidal ducts ( ), and maximum volumetric heating of 30 MW m–3 ( ). The computational results incorporate the influence of the helium cooling channels and the FCIs on electromagnetic coupling, thereby altering the MHD pressure and flow distribution. Simultaneously, the FCIs divide the flow into bulk and gap regions, where localized reverse flow is observed mainly within the gap regions of the rear poloidal ducts. The anisotropic conductivity introduced by helium channels alters the velocity and temperature distributions, further complicating the MHD flow. In addition, localized hot spots exceeding the design temperature limit are found near the top of the U-turn and in the outlet reduced activation ferritic/martensitic steel walls, suggesting that enhanced cooling is required in these locations.

title: Dark Horse Absorbers for Indoor Photovoltaics: Toward Cheaper, Safer, and More Stable Alternatives
abstract: ABSTRACT Indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have emerged as a promising solution for powering low‐power electronic and Internet of Things (IoT) devices by harvesting energy from artificial light sources. The development of low‐cost, non‐toxic, and stable absorber materials is central to enabling sustainable and scalable development of indoor PVs. Among various candidates, chalcogenide and kesterite absorbers such as Se, Sb 2 S 3 , Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 , GeS, Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 and Cu 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4 have recently attracted attention due to their earth abundance, environmental benignity, and suitable optoelectronic properties for indoor light harvesting. This review provides a comprehensive overview of reported Indoor PV devices based on these absorber materials. Beyond comparing reported device performances, it critically examines the relationships between their fundamental optoelectronic properties, absorber processing, defect and interface engineering, device architecture, stability, sustainability, and demonstrated integration with IoT applications. Although research on these systems remains at an early stage, rapid progress has been achieved, highlighting their strong potential for next‐generation indoor energy harvesting. Finally, we outline key challenges and future research directions to guide the development of efficient, stable, and environmentally sustainable Indoor PVs for powering low‐power electronics and IoT devices.

title: Impacts of energetic ion on the unstable spectra of kinetic ballooning modes and zonal flow generation
abstract: Global gyrokinetic particle simulations are employed to investigate the interaction between energetic ions (EIs) and kinetic ballooning modes (KBMs) across different toroidal mode number ( ) regimes, encompassing linear dispersion relations, nonlinear wave-particle interactions, and wave–wave interactions. The results demonstrate that EIs exert non-perturbative destabilizing effects on low- KBMs, while stabilizing high- KBMs through thermal ion dilution. These opposing EI effects arise from the different strengths of finite Larmor radius (FLR) and finite orbit width (FOW) effects in low- and high- regimes. Single- and multi- nonlinear simulations reveal strong wave-particle interactions between EIs and low- KBMs, resulting in higher KBM saturation levels and enhanced EI transport. Additionally, although low-density EIs have little direct influence on zonal flow (ZF), they can indirectly increase the spatial scale of ZF in multi- simulations. Since ZF is generated via the beat-driven process and its structure is determined by the pump wave, the EI effects lead to the dominance of low- KBM components, thereby increasing the spatial scale of the ZF.

title: Extending frequency metrology to increasingly complex molecules: SI-traceable sub-Doppler mid-IR spectroscopy of trioxane
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bringing increasingly complex polyatomic molecules within reach of precision measurement experiments opens new prospects ranging from Earth sciences and astrophysics, to metrology and quantum sciences. Here, we demonstrate sub-Doppler mid-IR spectroscopic measurements of, to our knowledge, the largest molecule to date, 1,3,5-trioxane, (H2CO)3, in its ν5 CO stretching mode. To this end, we use an ultra-high-resolution ~10.3 µm spectrometer based on a sub-Hz quantum cascade laser remotely calibrated against state-of-the-art primary frequency standards via a metrology-grade fibre link. We perform saturated absorption spectroscopy at low pressure with ~100 kHz resolution. This allows measuring the absolute frequency of hundreds of rovibrational transitions at unprecedented statistical and systematic uncertainties for such a complex species, as low as 4.6 kHz and 6.2 kHz respectively. In addition to providing new spectroscopic information on trioxane, our work extends frequency metrology methodologies to ever larger molecular systems, confirming the potential of our technologies for bringing increasingly complex species within reach of ultra-precise measurement experiments.

title: Impact-stiffening materials modulated by host–guest interactions in polypseudorotaxanes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The development of high-performance impact-stiffening materials is critical for applications spanning personal protection to military defense. Conventional designs of such materials relying on strong noncovalent interactions often face a strength–toughness trade‑off. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a strategy that utilizes the dynamic threading–dethreading kinetics of host–guest complexes in polypseudorotaxanes to fabricate impact‑stiffening materials. Unlike binding‑strength‑governed designs, this approach is governed by kinetic mismatch between the dethreading time of the macrocycle and the external deformation time. This kinetic control decouples the static compliance from the dynamic stiffening threshold, enabling pronounced impact‑stiffening even with a modest solution‑phase binding constant. Under low shear rates, the macrocycles gradually slide from the polymer backbone, preserving flexibility. Upon high-speed impact, the dethreading of host–guest complexes cannot occur within the ultrashort loading window of deformation, kinetically freezing the network and increasing the storage modulus by 48‑fold (0.1–100 Hz, 25 °C). The material also exhibits self-healing, reprocessability, and strong adhesion. This work demonstrates rate-dependent host–guest disassembly as a design principle for adaptive impact-protective materials.

title: Learning beyond rigid manipulation with hybrid soft-rigid robots
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Rigid-soft robot hybrids promise to unite the precision and repeatability of rigid manipulators with the compliance and adaptability of soft structures. Yet, full-fledged rigid-soft manipulators remain largely unexplored, in part because the intelligence required to exploit this combination is still missing. Here, we introduce a hybrid robotic system obtained by the series interconnection of a rigid arm and a soft manipulator, and systematically examine its ability to perform both established and previously inaccessible manipulation tasks. We show that a tailored imitation learning algorithm–generally applicable to this class of hybrid systems–leverages the complementary roles of rigid precision and soft embodiment to acquire manipulation skills and generalize them in a single shot across task variations. As a result, the system matches or exceeds the performance of rigid robots in classical tasks such as stacking, while enabling qualitatively new behaviors, including grasping objects through narrow openings.

title: The nature of the phase transition in VO2 B-phase and a quantum entanglement perspective
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The well-known metal-to-insulator transition in rutile/monoclinic VO2 has been understood as a correlation-enhanced Peierls phenomenon. The lesser-known B-polymorph exhibits a similar resistivity jump, assumed to arise from an analogous transition. However, unlike rutile/monoclinic VO2, here the transition is isostructural, with dimers persisting both above and below the transition, challenging established interpretations. Here, we show that the phase transition in the B-polymorph is qualitatively different. Despite high conductivity and finite spectral weight at the chemical potential, the high-temperature phase lacks standard metallic screening and Drude peaks. Our theoretical analysis reveals that while the low-temperature insulating phase is driven by both Peierls and Mott physics, the high-temperature state is an anomalous insulator whose apparent metallicity arises from incoherent in-gap states that mimic a metal. We relate this unusual growth of incoherent states to temperature-dependent intra-dimer charge transfers. Finally, we propose a unified framework using an Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen-like quantum-entanglement measure to characterize and distinguish between different VO2 phases hosting dimers.

title: The heterogeneous transmission of geopolitical energy shocks: A structural framework
Dynamic B–OH intermediates enable photocatalytic conversion of CO2 into formic acid
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Remediating of flue gas pollutants and the mitigation of carbon emissions represent two interconnected yet often conflicting challenges in environmental management. Here we report a borane-assisted photocatalytic system that achieves synergistic co-conversion of CO2, NOx, and SO2 from flue gas into valuable liquid products-formic, nitric, and sulfuric acids-with near-complete selectivity and high stability. Central to this process is the in situ generation of dynamic B-OH intermediates at the borane-catalyst interface, which serve as proton relays to activate water-derived protons for CO2 reduction while promoting reactive oxygen species for pollutant oxidation. This mechanism enables approximately 77.02% of the hydrogen in formic acid to originate from water. The system demonstrates broad applicability across diverse photocatalysts and borane reagents, and exhibits sustained performance under simulated flue gas conditions. Our work establishes a sustainable and economically viable pathway for integrated carbon and pollutant valorization, offering a scalable strategy toward circular carbon economies.

title: Electron Bridge Effect Enhanced Tandem Catalysis for Efficient Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) offers a promising route for wastewater remediation and ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis under mild conditions. However, the activity of NO 3 RR is hindered by the high activation barrier of nitrate (NO 3 − ), as well as the low generation efficiency and restricted migration of active hydrogen (H ads ). The development of electrocatalysts that combine efficient synergistic active sites, rapid electron transfer, and unimpeded H ads migration pathways is crucial for enhancing NO 3 RR performance. Here, we report a molten salt etching strategy to successfully prepare a ternary metal boride MoCoB electrocatalyst. In this catalyst, Mo site can efficiently adsorb and activate NO 3 − , while Co site is responsible for H 2 O dissociation and H ads supply. Meanwhile, B site builds an electronic bridge to enhance the electron transfer and proton migration between Mo and Co sites. Benefiting from the synergistic mechanism of electron bridge effect‐enhanced tandem catalysis, MoCoB achieves an NH 3 yield rate of 61.89 mg h −1 mg cat −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 98.73%. Furthermore, a Zn‐NO 3 − /ethanol hybrid battery assembled with MoCoB cathode demonstrates high power density and durable long‐term cycling stability, and the production of high‐value ammonium acetate. This work provides guidance for designing efficient NO 3 RR electrocatalysts and offers insights into reversible zinc‐based battery.

title: SEI Evolution on Siloxene Anodes in Solid and Liquid Electrolytes via an Ion‐Sieving/Electron‐Conducting Interfacial Layer
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon anodes suffer from severe volume expansion and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which limit their use in both liquid and solid‐state batteries. Here, a two‐dimensional siloxene‐based LP@SONS, is constructed by anchoring polypyrrole nanoparticles and lithiated‐Nafion onto siloxene nanosheets. This architecture combines electron‐conducting pathways with a Li + ‐selective ion‐sieving layer, homogenizing Li + flux, restricting anion/solvent penetration, and buffering strain. The stable and compositionally identical platform enables direct comparison of SEI evolution in liquid and solid electrolytes. In liquid cells, the SEI grows in a bulk‐permeated (3D) manner, whereas solid electrolytes confine growth to a planar solid–solid contact, yielding a LiF‐rich, planar‐confined (2D) SEI that passivates rapidly. Remarkably, LP@SONS promotes thinner, more uniform, LiF‐rich interphases in both systems. As a result, it delivers high reversible capacity, excellent rate capability, and long‐term cycling in liquid and solid‐state batteries, with only ∼5% thickness expansion after 100 cycles. This work clarifies how electrolyte contact geometry governs SEI dimensionality and offers an interfacial engineering strategy for high‐capacity anodes.

title: Low‐Temperature‐Locked Crystallization Enables Stress‐Relaxed Antimony Selenide Thin‐Film Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Absorber quality is critical to the performance of thin‐film photovoltaics, particularly for antimony selenide (Sb 2 Se 3 ). Due to its quasi‐one‐dimensional crystal structure, the migration, rearrangement, and orientation evolution of Sb 2 Se 3 chains play a pivotal role in determining crystallization and microstructural behavior. However, rapid heating (as with conventional thermal annealing) typically induces competitive chain orientation and nonuniform stress relaxation. This results in defect generation, orientational disorder, and complex crystallization pathways that severely constrain device performance. To address these issues, we propose a low‐temperature pretreatment to precisely regulate the crystallization kinetics of Sb 2 Se 3 absorbers. Low‐temperature pretreatment applied to amorphous Sb 2 Se 3 films prior to annealing effectively suppresses atomic diffusion and structural disordering, while preserving short‐range ordered chain segments as structural motifs for subsequent crystallization. During the subsequent annealing process, progressive stress relaxation facilitates chain reorientation and crystal reconstruction, thereby influencing local Sb‐Se compositional evolution, promoting grain growth, and enhancing preferential orientation. This progressive ‘low‐temperature‐locking stress‐relaxation‐oriented reconstruction’ process markedly reduces residual stress and defect density, while improving charge transport and suppressing non‐radiative carrier recombination. As a result, our pretreated device achieved a power conversion efficiency of 9.78%. This strategy offers a general route to fabricating high‐quality, low‐stress, low‐defect chalcogenide films for efficient and stable photovoltaics.

title: Hybrid simulations of nonlinear zonal flow generation by multi- n toroidal Alfvén eigenmo...
abstract: In burning plasmas, zonal flows (ZFs) excited by toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) play a crucial role in improving energy confinement. In this work, strong self-generated ZFs are analyzed in a multi- TAE system through nonlinear hybrid simulations using the CLT-K code, where the ZFs are driven by self-beat interactions of TAEs. The results show that the strong ZFs dominate the nonlinear stage and significantly suppress the TAE activity. The ZF mode structures consist of the and harmonics, and are directly correlated with the spatial structures of TAEs. Further analysis of the ZF kinetic energy evolution demonstrates that a finite residual between the Reynolds and Maxwell stresses, arising from toroidal geometry, enables net energy transfer from TAEs to ZFs, with an additional contribution from the energetic particles (EPs) pressure response. In addition, the linear Lorentz force contributes either to ZF pumping or damping depending on the stage of the evolution. Strong ZF generation is favored in regimes with high EP pressure and low viscosity. A self-regulating process is identified: stronger TAEs drive stronger ZFs, which in turn regulates the TAE activity. These findings provide both numerical and physical insights into the role of ZFs in regulating EP-driven instabilities in tokamak plasmas.

title: The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.
