Tunable diffusive memristor arrays for neuromorphic temporal computing
abstract: Scaling diffusive memristors from single devices to integrated systems has been hindered by stochastic ionic motion and filament evolution. Here confined metal-ion migration enables controlled relaxation dynamics, as demonstrated in a 28 × 14 array for neuromorphic computing.

title: Geopolitical exposure in cross-border electricity transmission: Evidence from Baltic desynchronization and interconnection disruptions
Electron-Deficient β-Diketone Ligand Enabled Ni-Catalyzed Remote Dicarbofunctionalization of Alkenes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A nickel-catalyzed remote migratory dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes was realized with high efficiency and excellent regioselectivity without the assistance of a directing group. The formation of a thermodynamically stable allyl-metal intermediate and the use of an electron-deficient β-diketone ligand are the keys to the success of these remote diarylation and arylalkenylation. This protocol features a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group compatibility, providing a series of remote diarylated and arylalkenylated hydrocarbons in high yields. Notably, the allyl group represents one of the most synthetically useful handles in synthetic chemistry, and the synthetic values of this process have been demonstrated by the formal synthesis of allocolchicinoids, and by the preparation of a RARγ selective retinoid agonist in a highly efficient and step-economical manner.

title: Cation Pinning toward High-Concentration Formic Acid Fuel Cells
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Despite the high theoretical energy density of concentrated formic acid, direct formic acid fuel cells (DFAFCs) incorporating conventional nanoparticle or emerging single-atom anodes exhibit a precipitous power loss as fuel concentration scales. While CO poisoning is traditionally blamed, we show that this limitation is governed by interfacial acid–base kinetics. By implementing a cation-pinning strategy via rare-earth oxide-modified Rh single-atom sites, we stabilize OH– from water dissociation through interfacial ionic anchoring to trigger localized pH inversion. This modulation leads to the preferential enrichment of interfacial formate, identified here as the primary reactive species. Consequently, Dy2O3–Rh/NC delivers a mass activity 641-fold higher than that of nanoparticle benchmarks. The resulting anode achieves an exceptional peak power density of 375 mW cm–2, surpassing commercial Pd/C across all concentrations. This work establishes precision ionic management as a versatile approach to breaking performance limits in multiphase catalysis.

title: Rh2C3− Cluster-Driven Nitrogen Activation: Trapping a High-Energy Intermediate
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Converting inert and globally abundant molecules such as N2 into useful chemicals is central to sustainable energy and environmental chemistry. Herein, we investigate the gas-phase reaction of the Rh2C3− anion with N2 using mass spectrometry, anion photoelectron spectroscopy, and quantum chemical calculations. The experimental spectra of Rh2C3− and Rh2C3N2− exhibit closely similar features, indicating a preserved electronic core upon N2 attachment. Theoretical analysis further reveals that the end-on N2 adsorption complex is a trapped high-energy intermediate whose subsequent transformation is prevented by an activation barrier that necessitates additional energy input, and that this complex exhibits superior performance in the coconversion of diverse energy-bearing gas molecules. Furthermore, the subsequent application of oriented external electric fields provides a nondestructive and continuously adjustable means of modifying the intrinsic barrier heights, thereby effectively switching the reaction mechanism. These findings elucidate the complex reaction network of Rh2C3− with N2, establish a reliable spectroscopic fingerprint for identifying isomeric intermediates, and provide fundamental insights into electronic control strategies for catalytic nitrogen activation.

title: Ligand-Controlled Chemodivergent β-Methylene C(sp3)–H Heteroarylation of Aliphatic Acids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving ligand-controlled chemodivergence in C–H activation is still difficult because several competing reaction pathways are available when multiple C–H bonds are present. We describe a Pd(II)-catalyzed, chemodivergent β-methylene C(sp3)–H heteroarylation of free aliphatic acids in which two distinct classes of bidentate pyridone ligands each deliver a different product. These two ligands also overcome a long-standing inhibitory effect of heteroaryl iodides, demonstrating the potential of this protocol to serve as a general C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling method using readily available aliphatic acids as the alkylating partner. Mechanistic experiments and DFT analyses reveal that π–π stacking between the quinoline motif and the heteroaryl ring lowers the barrier for rotation of the carbon–palladium bond, favoring protodepalladation to the reductive Heck product, whereas the oxime ether ligand lacks this interaction and steers the key intermediate toward β-H elimination to give the oxidative Heck product.

title: Revisiting the Biosynthetic Cyclization of Indole Sesquiterpene Alkaloids: Proposal of a Spiro -Indolenine Pathway and Synthesis of Prelecanindole
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Indole sesquiterpene and indole diterpene alkaloids constitute a distinctive class of natural products characterized by complex polycyclic ring architectures and diverse potent biological activities. In indole sesquiterpenes, the characteristic indole-containing pentacyclic skeleton is biosynthesized from 3-farnesylindole through epoxidation followed by a sequential cationic cyclization. Although the cyclization enzyme has been identified, the details of its cyclization mechanism remain unclear. Here, we propose a new biosynthetic mechanism involving a spiro-indoleninium intermediate, which contrasts with the long-standing mechanism proposed in the 1970s that proceeds via a tertiary-to-secondary carbocation rearrangement. We demonstrated the feasibility of this new mechanism by means of density functional theory (DFT) calculations, which do not support the conventional mechanism and also by chemical emulation: the putative spiro-indolenine intermediate was synthesized from two fragments through stereoselective cyclopropanation as a key reaction and subsequently converted to prelecanindole, a common biosynthetic intermediate of indole sesquiterpene alkaloids, under mild acidic conditions.

title: Single-Atom Cerium Unlocks Efficient Hydrogen Spillover within Nonreducible Zeolites through a Proton–Electron Relay
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen spillover connects hydrogen activation with spatially separated catalytic functions, yet engineering efficient hydrogen transport through nonreducible zeolites remains an outstanding challenge owing to the absence of intrinsic pathways for coupled proton–electron transfer. Here, we show that isolated cerium atoms incorporated into Pt/USY transform the zeolite from a passive support into an active medium for solid-state hydrogen transport. In situ spectroscopy, isotopic tracing, and theoretical calculations reveal that atomically dispersed Ce species dynamically generate localized hydroxyl groups and oxygen vacancies that cooperatively establish a proton–electron relay, substantially lowering the kinetic barrier for hydrogen migration through zeolitic micropores. The resulting enhancement in hydrogen spillover extends hydrogen delivery to spatially remote Brønsted acid sites, suppresses coke formation, and significantly improves polyolefin hydrocracking stability. These findings establish hydrogen transport as a tunable design parameter in bifunctional zeolite catalysis and provide a general strategy for engineering hydrogen-transfer pathways in nonreducible porous materials.

title: A Bioinspired Thiolate-Bridged Diiron System for Functionally Replicating Hydrazine Dehydrogenase and Its Efficient Electrocatalytic Hydrazine Oxidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrazine dehydrogenase (HDH) catalyzes the oxidation of hydrazine (N2H4) to dinitrogen (N2) as the final step of anaerobic ammonium oxidation, an essential process in closing the nitrogen cycle. Despite extensive biochemical studies, the detailed mechanism of HDH at a molecular level remains elusive. An increasing number of studies indicate that the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) is also central to direct hydrazine fuel cells. However, known electrocatalysts for HzOR are predominantly heterogeneous systems, while molecular electrocatalysts are still scarce, especially those inspired by biological HDH. This scarcity not only limits mechanistic understanding but also hinders the development of efficient and tunable catalysts. To tackle these challenging issues, we sought inspiration from the biological HDH system, wherein multiple iron-containing heme subunits cooperatively promote efficient HzOR with the assistance of surrounding sulfur-bearing cysteine residues. Integrating these key features, we selected the thiolate-bridged diiron complex [Cp*Fe(μ-SEt)(MeCN)]2[PF6]2 (1, Cp* = η5-C5Me5) for functionally replicating HDH. Treatment of 1 with N2H4 induces disproportionation to afford the active diazene (N2H2) species, which can be captured by the diiron cooperative platform to yield [Cp*Fe(μ-SEt)2(cis-μ-η1:η1-HN=NH)FeCp*][PF6] (2). In the presence of appropriate electron and proton acceptors, complex 2 undergoes a two-electron oxidation, leading to N2 release and the regeneration of 1. Remarkably, both complexes 1 and 2 serve as efficient molecular electrocatalysts for HzOR. This diiron molecular system not only achieves the functional replication of HDH involving a key N2H2 intermediate but also establishes a bioinspired design strategy for developing multimetal cooperative electrocatalysts toward efficient HzOR.

title: State of temperature estimation for cylindrical lithium-ion batteries: challenges and solutions
Hydrogen-Bond Network-Assisted Ethylene and Hydrogen Photosynthesis from Methane over Isolated Ir Active Sites under Ambient Conditions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Direct conversion of methane to ethylene (DCM) is an attractive yet formidable challenge due to the difficult C–H activation and uncontrollable C–C coupling process. Herein, we report a hydrogen-bond network-assisted ethylene and H2 photosynthesis from methane over oxygen-vacancy-enriched TiO2-supported single Ir atoms (Ir1/TiO2–Ov) under ambient conditions. The Ir-induced lattice distortion drives spontaneous hydrolysis under humid conditions, generating a hydroxylated surface that endows coordinatively unsaturated Ir sites to activate the first methane molecule without light irradiation. Upon photoexcitation, surface hydroxyls are oxidized into dangling oxygen species (*O) on Ti sites, which promote the dehydrogenation of *CH3 to *CH2. In synergy with the Ir site, the adjacent *O species activate a second CH4 molecule and finally direct selective C–C coupling to form C2H4. Meanwhile, methane-derived protons migrate through the hydrogen-bond network via a Grotthuss mechanism to produce H2. The Ir1/TiO2–Ov catalyst achieves the production of ethylene (14.3 ± 0.7 μmol•gcat–1•h–1) and H2 (28.4 ± 1.2 μmol•gcat–1•h–1) for at least 210 h at 25 °C and atmospheric pressure under light irradiation. Our findings establish a hydrogen-bond network-assisted strategy for methane C–H activation and selective C–C and H–H coupling.

title: Synthetic Control of Quantum Phases in Organic Conductors: Molecular-Level Disorder Engineering and Pressure-Induced Superconductivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Structural randomness is a dominant factor governing electronic properties; however, the intrinsic effects of a disordered potential remain elusive due to the lack of a synthetic platform capable of introducing purely random potentials without carrier doping or altering the fundamental band structure. Here, we demonstrate the synthetic control of superconducting and insulating phases by exploiting the unique conformational flexibility of molecular conductors. Through precise thermodynamic control during crystal growth, we selectively synthesize the structurally ordered superconductor κ-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu[N(CN)2]Br (κ-Br; BEDT-TTF = bis(ethylenedithio)tetrathiafulvalene) and the structurally disordered insulating polymorph, κ″-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu[N(CN)2]Br (κ″-Br), possessing the exact same chemical composition. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm the metastable nature of κ″-Br, showing a packing arrangement of BEDT-TTF molecules and an electronic band structure nearly identical to those of superconducting κ-Br, but featuring a disordered anion layer. Optical conductivity spectra reveal low-energy excitations without a distinct gap, indicating that the insulating behavior originates from disorder-induced carrier localization. Furthermore, κ″-Br undergoes a pressure-induced insulator–superconductor transition, in stark contrast to postsynthetic X-ray irradiation which induced irreversible structural damage. This work represents the first demonstration of synthetic control of an ordered superconductor and a disordered insulator driven solely by orientational disorder in organic conductors. Our study provides new avenues for manipulating strongly correlated electron systems and for investigating the intrinsic effects of randomness, free from carrier doping or structural perturbation of conducting layers.

title: Stepwise Assembly of a Lavandulyl Moiety on Flavonoids Enabled by a 2″-Prenyltransferase
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lavandulylated flavonoids contain a characteristic branched C10 moiety, and the enzymatic basis underlying its biosynthesis remains poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the complete biosynthetic pathway of the lavandulylated flavonoid kurarinone from naringenin in the medicinal plant Sophora flavescens. The pathway involves four sequential steps, 8-prenylation, 2′-hydroxylation, 2″-prenylation, and 5-O-methylation, catalyzed by Sf8PT, SfF2′H, Sf2″PT, and Sf5OMT, respectively. Sf2′′PT represents the first characterized flavonoid 2′′-prenyltransferase (PT), catalyzing a second prenylation on the pre-existing prenyl side chain to complete the assembly of the branched lavandulyl moiety. The activity of Sf2″PT strictly depends on prior 2′-hydroxylation, establishing a defined order of enzymatic modifications that enables this noncanonical prenylation reaction. Ancestral sequence reconstruction and mutagenesis demonstrated that an inactive ancestral enzyme could be converted into functional 8PT or 2′′PT variants through one or seven amino acid substitutions, respectively. Collectively, this work establishes the enzymatic basis for stepwise lavandulyl moiety assembly and provides a framework for the enzymatic construction and engineering of branched prenylated natural products.

title: Departing Pathways in Aza-Diarylethene Photoswitching: Elucidating the Role of the Central Ring Allows Reprogramming of the Photoresponse
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aza-diarylethenes (aza-DAEs) are an emerging class of molecular photoswitches that allow reversible C–N bond formation and cleavage upon irradiation. They not only show high potential as T-type photochromes but also offer exciting opportunities for the exploration of unique reactivity control. Two types of these photoswitches are currently being investigated, which differ substantially in the nature of their metastable states. While classical DAE behavior is found in perfluorinated thiazole derivatives, an unexpected zwitterion formation and concomitant aromatization is observed for nonfluorinated pyrimidine derivatives. The latter offers reversible control over intramolecular charge separation and intrinsic three-state photoswitching. Their metastable state unleashes thiolate reactivity, which can be harnessed, e.g., in photoinitiation applications for smart polymer generation. Despite this promising progress, the reason for the divergent photochemical behavior in aza-DAEs is not yet understood. Here, we show that substitution of the central five-membered ring is responsible for the different photochemical outcomes and nature of the metastable state. Furthermore, our computational results provide systematic insights into the structural factors governing the relative stability of the neutral closed-ring and zwitterionic forms. We then use this knowledge to reprogram thioazole derivatives and render them into zwitterion-forming aza-DAEs. With these results, the predictable and rational design of aza-DAEs is enabled, which can now be radically changed in their photoresponses and tailored to specific desired properties and applications.

title: Electrochemical Allylic Carboxylation of Unactivated Alkenes with CO2
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract As both alkenes and CO2 are abundant and easily available feedstocks, carboxylation of alkenes with CO2 represents an attractive and sustainable strategy to synthesize value-added carboxylic acids. Despite substantial advances in carboxylation of π-bonds in alkenes, the carboxylation of C–H bonds in alkenes, which preserves the C═C bond in the synthesis of valuable unsaturated carboxylic acids, remains a longstanding challenge, particularly for unactivated alkenes owing to their intrinsically low reactivity. Herein, we report the first electrochemical allylic carboxylation of unactivated alkenes with CO2, providing a direct and selective approach to hard-to-obtain β,γ-unsaturated carboxylic acids. Moreover, this reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and applicability to late-stage diversification. Mechanistic studies indicate that the electrogenerated CO2 radical anion acts both as the carboxylation reagent and the hydrogen-atom abstraction species for the subsequent desaturation process, further uncovering the synthetic utility potential of the CO2 radical anion.

title: Immobilizing Ionomers by Strong Hydrogen Bonds for Highly Stable Industrial Water Electrolysis at 3.0 A/cm2
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Raising the operating current density can effectively reduce the high cost of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), but this approach is limited by rapid electrode degradation. Our previous research identified a critical degradation mechanism in which ionomer migration blocks mass-transport channels in the anode catalyst layer (ACL). Here, we find that each sulfonate group of the ionomer forms only about half a hydrogen bond on the IrO2 surface, indicating a weak catalyst–ionomer interaction. Rather than modifying the IrO2 surface, we propose to introduce additives that provide additional adsorption sites forming stronger hydrogen bonds (SHB) with the sulfonate groups. The resulting SHB-ACL maintains a stable ionomer distribution and pore network even after aging, and exhibits a roughly four fold lower degradation rate over 2500 h at 3.0 A/cm2. Furthermore, the electrode can be readily scaled up to 600 cm2. The improvement stability is at least in part attributable to enhanced interface interaction, although preserved porosity, water/gas transport, and interparticle contacts may also contribute. These findings offer a scalable route toward durable industrial PEMWE devices.

title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

title: Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines
abstract: Despite the importance of divergent synthesis to obtain different isomers for medicinal and material chemistry, divergent stereocontrol over four distinct selectivity factors remains a fundamental challenge. The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here, we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates geometric, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. We prepared diverse types of γ-amino esters from identical, readily available unsaturated esters and amines via synergistic palladium and acid catalysis, with each precisely obtained out of hundreds of potential telomers. We developed several chiral phosphoramidite ligands to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereomanipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor
abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

title: Mechanisms of nucleosome disruption shape epigenetic inheritance pathway choice
abstract: Maintaining cell identity requires duplicating the genome and epigenome during S phase. As DNA is copied, histones extracted from parental nucleosomes are transferred to nascent strands, which preserves the position of epigenetic marks. How the replisome coordinates these processes is unclear. Using reconstitution with purified yeast proteins, kinetic measurements, structural biology, mass spectrometry and genomics, we examined nucleosome-replisome encounter and histone transfer. Parental nucleosomes can be unwrapped ahead of the fork by the MCM helicase, aided by FACT and Ctf4, or by Tof1. Nucleosomal DNA unwrapping by MCM creates a FACT binding site, helping strip histones off DNA. Ctf4 enhances FACT-stimulated histone extraction, retains parental histones and hands them to Tof1, en route to lagging-strand redeposition. Thus, extraction via Ctf4 commits histones to lagging-strand transfer.

title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang
abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor–stroma borders harbor a MIF + fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor–adipose borders, featured an FLT1 + endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

title: Redox-Window-Guided Metal Node Editing of Copper Metal–Organic Frameworks for Recyclable Heterogeneous Cu(I) Catalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cu(I) catalysts are central to many bond-forming reactions, but integrating Cu(I) sites into recyclable porous solids remains difficult because Cu(I) is easily oxidized, over-reduced, or leached. Here, we report redox-window-guided metal node editing as an oxidation-state-programming strategy that converts hydrolytically fragile Cu(II)3BTC2 into a hydrolytically stable mixed-valence Cu(I/II) MOF catalyst. Phenolic reductants are selected by matching their oxidation potentials to the Cu(II)–to–Cu(I) window of Cu(II)3BTC2, enabling proton-coupled, inner-sphere single-electron transfer at Cu paddlewheel nodes. Hydroquinone gives the most controlled material, [p-Ph(OH)2]-Cu3BTC2, containing 33.4% Cu(I), ship-in-a-bottle [Cu(MeCN)4]+ complexes, mesopores, and enhanced stability under humid, acidic, and basic conditions. As a heterogeneous catalyst for hydrative amide synthesis, [p-Ph(OH)2]-Cu3BTC2 affords 92% yield, negligible Cu leaching, five-cycle recyclability, and the highest turnover number among compared Cu(I) catalysts.

title: Physical field coupling in hydrogen production: A critical review from single-field to multi-field synergistic mechanisms
Strengthening Metal–Oxygen Bonds via Ionicity–Covalency Asymmetric Connection: 4f Electronic Configuration Effect
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise control over the characteristics of metal–oxygen (M–O) bonds by regulating the electron redistribution between the metal and oxygen under perturbation conditions is crucial for maintaining the structural stability of transition-metal oxides. However, its development has always been hindered by the strong coupling between orbital hybridization and charge localization. Herein, by leveraging the strong ionicity of the Ce–O bonds in CeO2, we constructed an ionicity–covalency asymmetric bonding network, in which the ionic Ce–O is atomically coupled with the covalent M–O (M = Ni/Co). The reduced Ce–O coordination in this special structure weakens the O 2p → Ce 4f charge transfer and further elevates the ionic character of Ce–O bonds, thereby activating the reversible 4f electronic configuration transition. Critically, this configuration undergoes reversible transformation under potential fluctuation, reshaping charge redistribution within the M–O bonding motifs and then suppressing irreversible M–O bond degradation. Harnessing this mechanism enables transition-metal oxides to express a robust framework for the whole structure under repeated redox cycling. Incorporating this resulting CeO2/NiCo2O4, a large-scale alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) stack delivers significantly stable operation for over 350 h at 6 A under a 12-h intermittent experimental protocol. This finding offers a fundamental insight into the dynamic charge distribution in M–O bonds under potential perturbation for universal structural protection.

title: Spatio-temporal fair allocation of active-power support among microgrids: A distributed optimization framework
Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance
abstract: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures interact with strategic infrastructure, political legitimacy and transition finance. The central argument is temporal: political commitments, infrastructure development and financing arrangements evolve at different speeds, generating misalignment between strategic ambitions and implementation capacity. Institutional risk compression is introduced as the governance mechanism through which socio-political durability, regulatory credibility and financial arrangements interact to contain or amplify uncertainty. The framework is explored through a case study of Sicily, a strategic Mediterranean energy node connecting North African gas corridors, renewable development, grid interconnections and prospective EU–Africa energy partnerships. Evidence on infrastructure investment, renewable permitting and cross-border financing illustrates how geopolitical priorities interact with territorial distributional tensions, regulatory constraints and investment conditions. The analysis highlights three interconnected challenges: aligning commitments across different time horizons, reconciling system-wide infrastructure benefits with local legitimacy and distinguishing genuine risk reduction from the redistribution of financial exposure. The paper contributes a framework for understanding how geopolitical pressures are transmitted through regional energy transitions and identifies implications for EU energy security, infrastructure governance and transition finance.

title: Strategic autonomy and the energy transition: Rethinking Europe's geopolitical alignment
abstract: Europe's geopolitical alignment, its enduring deference to a US-led unipolar order, has come at the expense of its energy security and its ability to carry out the energy transition. This paper argues that greater strategic autonomy, the capacity and willingness to make economic and foreign policy decisions according to its own interests, would allow Europe to pursue both goals more effectively. It develops this argument in four parts. First, it characterises Europe's geopolitical alignment as a pattern of deference to US strategic priorities, sustained despite mounting costs to Europe's material interests, its standing and the multilateral order it claims to uphold. Second, it traces how this alignment shaped Europe's response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, contributing to a partly self-inflicted energy crisis followed by an abrupt and costly pivot to American liquefied natural gas that failed to resolve Europe's energy dependency. Third, it argues that on the energy transition Europe's interests are more closely aligned with Beijing's than with Washington's, although closer engagement deepens its dependence on Chinese clean technologies and critical raw materials. Europe should manage this trade-off by maintaining its de-risking approach and extending it to all its strategic dependencies, including those on the US. Finally, it argues that Europe will be unable to recalibrate its alignment and exercise strategic autonomy without building up its industrial and technological capacities and increasing its investment. Europe's choices will help determine the pace of the global energy transition, and with it, the world's chances of meeting its climate goals.

title: A mechanism-guided Bayesian physics-informed neural network for unified battery state-of-health monitoring using field data
A risk-averse bidding and scheduling strategy for process industry VPPs in demand response markets based on thermodynamically-enhanced RTN
Traffic-scenario-recognition-based energy management strategy with variable prediction horizon for connected fuel cell buses
When hydrogen is not fully flexible: Implications for sector-coupled energy models
Electric vehicles as mobile energy carriers: An activity-based agent-based model of residential PV origin energy flows and V2G
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) is turning transportation management into a coupled mobility and energy planning problem. Public EVCS deployment affects travel behavior, parking duration, and local electricity demand, while EV batteries may also provide flexible storage through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) operation. However, the extent to which EVs can redistribute residential photovoltaic (PV) energy depends not only on charging infrastructure but also on daily activity schedules, state-of-charge conditions, dwell times, and station-side constraints. This study develops an activity-based agent-based model to evaluate EVs as mobile carriers of residential PV-origin energy in an urban charging system. The model links home charging, activity-based travel, public charging, V2G discharge, stationary battery energy storage systems, and charging station feasibility constraints. The framework is applied to Eindhoven, the Netherlands. Results show that EVs can acquire substantial residential PV-origin energy through home charging, but consume only about 6% of it during daily travel. Most PV-origin energy remains stored in EV batteries when vehicles arrive at non-home locations, creating technical potential for redistribution. However, activity context is the dominant bottleneck limiting V2G opportunities, indicating that urban V2G potential is shaped less by infrastructure availability alone than by when and where eligible EVs are parked during daily routines.

title: Learning convex voltage constraints for transmission–distribution coordinated dispatch: A decoupled input convex neural network

An asymmetric multi-scale time-frequency fusion network with dynamic sparse experts and adaptive optimization for ultra-short-term load forecasting
Unlocking public EV charging flexibility for grid balancing: A year-long empirical assessment of unidirectional and bidirectional smart charging in Prague
abstract: The transition of imbalance settlement in the Continental Europe synchronous area to 15-minute market time units, together with rising shares of variable renewable generation, raises the operational value of sub-hourly demand-side flexibility. Electric vehicles at public charging stations are an attractive source, yet empirical estimates of the balancing value of public smart charging remain scarce. This paper quantifies the technical potential of aggregated public smart charging in Prague to absorb the 15-minute system imbalance of the Czech transmission system operator ČEPS, using a full year of real charging-session data: 286,492 sessions across 1051 charging points. An ex-post optimization on a session-level flexibility envelope evaluates four configurations: the unidirectional (V1G) and bidirectional (V2G) operating modes, each under two user-comfort scenarios in which the delivered energy is preserved exactly (S1) or relaxed to the greater of 80% of it or 30 kWh (S2). The fleet’s uncontrolled load is removed first, so the same energy is re-timed, not added. Public V1G absorbs 4.44% of the imbalance energy under S1 and 4.85% under S2; V2G absorbs 7.09% and 7.64%. Bidirectional operation increases the absorbed energy by more than half, whereas relaxing comfort adds only about half a percentage point, so the bidirectional-infrastructure axis carries far more value than the user-incentive axis. These figures are a best-case ceiling computed with hindsight, not an operational forecast; valued at Czech final settlement prices, the V2G potential is a gross avoided balancing cost of up to about EUR 480,000 per year.

title: Structural separation of adjacent photovoltaic arrays for area-based capacity attribution from high-resolution remote sensing imagery
Agentic predictive control for residential PV-battery systems: from natural-language scheduling requests to receding-horizon dispatch
Hydrogen-based green steel corridors: cost saving and emission reduction potentials of emerging trade routes
abstract: Deploying hydrogen-based direct-reduced iron (H 2 -DRI) technologies will be decisive to defossilize the global steel sector by replacing coal-based blast furnaces (BF) in conventional steelmaking. DRI can then either be directly fed into an electric-arc-furnace (EAF) and alternative electric smelting furnaces or transported as cold hot-briquetted iron (HBI) and a green commoditiy to a steel plant. The availability and expansion of low-cost renewable electricity and green hydrogen supply options is the essential and site-specific precondition to deploy H 2 -DRI plants that can be gradually switched from natural gas to hydrogen. However, near-zero emission steel made from H 2 -DRI needs to produced at competitive costs compared to fossil steel regulated under carbon emission pricing schemes. Based on revised green hydrogen cost forecasts in potentially low-cost countries like Australia or Oman, this study reveals the cost competitiveness of emerging green steel corridors built on international partnerships. With green HBI then exported to a representative EAF green steelmaking site, the analysis shows the potential cost savings of importing green HBI from renewable-rich countries when facing a future lack of affordable hydrogen supply options in leading steel countries like Germany or South Korea characterized by a high dependence on energy imports. Overall, low-emission crude steel based on 66 vol% H 2 -HBI imports achieves fossil cost parity in Germany in 2040 at increased carbon prices in the EU, while all 100% hydrogen-based steel scenarios inhere higher costs with a premium of 6%–13% over natural gas-based DRI-EAF crude steel at 828 € t −1 CS (with 0% scrap) at hydrogen costs ranging between 4.14 and 4.94 € kg −1 H 2 . In addition, a cradle-to-gate accounting of greenhouse gas emissions reveals that cost savings from HBI imports potentially come at the expense of up to 50% higher total emissions compared to an integrated H 2 -DRI-EAF plant running on iron ore pellet imports. All 100% H 2 -DRI-based scenarios yield an emission reduction between 42%–57% compared to a domestic benchmarked NG-DRI-EAF scenario at 1293 kg CO 2 (e) t −1 CS. The carbon footprint analysis further highlights the effect of upstream defossilization measures related to iron ore mining, pelletising and transport by rail and ship.

title: Conditional MHA-assisted online control for BESS frequency regulation: real-time evaluation of performance-based revenue and cycle degradation
Risk-aware operation of electric vehicle aggregators in uncertain electricity markets using game theory and Markowitz framework
Model-based prediction of temperature evolution in solid-state batteries with minimal experimental data: A case study on composite cathodes under thermal ramp
abstract: While solid-state batteries (SSBs) are presumed to be safer than conventional LIBs, recent studies suggest that they can undergo a quicker and more severe thermal runaway than LIB cells. We have developed a modelling framework to investigate safety of SSBs by linking material-scale measurements to electrode- or cell-scale thermal behaviour. The proposed framework directly incorporates differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) heat flow measurements obtained at a single heating rate as a time-dependent heat source to simulate the temperature evolution of electrodes and cells under prescribed thermal ramp conditions. With minimum experimental data and computational fitting efforts, our model allows for consistent thermal-safety comparisons across cell formats and rapid screening of SSB materials. We implemented our model for cathode composites of SSBs, consisting of LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 and eight different oxide- and sulphide-based solid electrolytes, exposed to a thermal ramp and simulated their temperature evolution. The simulations were run in three representative formats for SSBs: coin, single-layer pouch, and multilayer-pouch cells. The results show that the temperature increase in sulphide-based cathode composites is significantly higher than that of oxide-based composites. Among the different formats, the temperature increases considerably higher in cathode composites with multilayer-pouch format, compared to others. The model was also applied to two 24 Ah LIB cells under a 150 °C oven test, whose temperature evolution results has been reported in the literature. The simulated temperature evolution showed good agreement with the experimental measurements and the corresponding kinetic-based model under the investigated thermal conditions, demonstrating the capability of the simplified approach to translate calorimetric heat generation data into full-cell thermal behaviour and its potential applicability to battery systems with different chemistries.

title: Industry–region interactions shape decarbonisation policy effectiveness while renewable deliverability bounds transferability
System-level optimization of seawater-based water supply and cooling for large-scale green hydrogen and ammonia production under variable renewable operation
abstract: As green hydrogen and ammonia projects expand in arid coastal regions, coupled demands for process water (PW) and cooling water (CW) increasingly constrain cooling system (CS) selection and water supply infrastructure sizing. To address this research gap, a transferable methodology for designing and techno-economically evaluating cooling and water supply systems for large-scale seawater-based production is presented. It combines time-resolved renewable power and ammonia production modelling, CS performance models, water treatment plant (WTP) sizing, PW and CW storage simulation, and cost assessment. It is applied to the 1.5 GW Phase 1 Murchison Green Hydrogen Project in Western Australia as a case study, using hourly ERA5 climate data for 2015–2024. The investigated CS options include once-through seawater cooling (OTSC), dry cooling (DC), wet cooling towers (WCT), and adiabatic hybrid coolers (AHC). Storage-based optimization substantially reduced the required peak treatment capacities, lowering WTP capacity by 12.4% (to 273 m 3 /h) for PW and CW capacity by 20.6% (to 1,127 m 3 /h) for WCT, and 63.0% (to 636 m 3 /h) for AHC. These reductions translated directly into lower PW-related capital expenditure, operational expenditure, and levelized cost of water (−8.7%, −4.2%, and − 7.3%, respectively). On an integrated cost basis, WCT achieved the lowest levelized cost of cooling (5.96 USD/MWh th ), below DC (38.0%), AHC (44.7%), and OTSC (73.6%). A simplified cost-allocation sensitivity showed that neglecting water treatment and marine infrastructure requirements can alter the CS ranking. The analysis further indicated that CS and water supply make a non-negligible contribution to the total levelized cost of hydrogen, accounting for 2.0–7.4%.

title: Comparative multi-criteria assessment of hydrogen production pathways for nuclear microreactor deployment

Cost-carbon preference reversals between new and second-life batteries in stationary storage: a long-horizon comparative framework
