Component-resolved voltage-loss monitoring of PEM water electrolyzers from routine operating data
Full‐Process Synergistic Optimization of Buried Interfaces via Molecule‐Assisted Co‐Assembly for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are promising hole‐selective contacts for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet insufficient substrate anchoring and weak buried‐interface interactions limit device efficiency and stability. Here, we report a co‐assembled SAM (Co‐SAM) strategy that enables full‐process synergistic optimization of the perovskite buried interface by introducing tris(4‐fluorophenyl)phosphine oxide (TFPPO) into SAMs. TFPPO suppresses SAM aggregation in solution via its strongly polar P═O group and anchors onto NiO x , with its 4‐fluorophenyl arms proposed to interact with unanchored hydroxyl groups of SAMs to strengthen anchoring and refine their arrangement. Furthermore, TFPPO optimizes the interfacial chemical states while serving as an effective template to direct high‐quality perovskite crystal growth. Consequently, inverted PSCs based on the regulated SAMs achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 26.98% (stabilized PCE of 26.40%) and 20.65% for normal‐bandgap (1.54 eV) and wide‐bandgap (1.78 eV) devices, respectively. Moreover, a representative Co‐SAM‐modified device retains 97% of its initial efficiency after 1856 h of maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐1), and Co‐SAM‐modified devices retain 92.36% of their initial efficiency after 2408 h of continuous aging at 65°C (ISOS‐D‐2).

title: Hydroxyl‐Orchestrated Crystallization and Affinity Sites in Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for One‐Step Selective Ternary Ion Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT One‐step selective separation of multiple coexisting ions from complex aqueous media remains a formidable challenge. Here we report hydroxyl‐orchestrated covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that couple framework crystallization with hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket‐site formation, enabling ternary separation of Cs + , Sr 2+ and UO 2 2+ in a single step. Hydroxyl substitution decelerates interfacial polymerization while reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding to stabilize ordered frameworks, yielding high crystallinity. Concurrently, hydroxyl‐orchestrated enol‐imine to keto‐enamine tautomerization promotes the formation of hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket sites for selective UO 2 2+ chelation. The optimized membrane achieves a UO2 2+ uptake of 336 mg g −1 and a Cs + permeation flux of 0.26 mol m −2 h −1 , while exhibiting suppressed Sr 2+ permeation. Under ternary conditions, Cs + /Sr 2+ and Cs + /UO 2 2+ separation factors reach 81.5 and 326.9, with stable performance over repeated cycles. These findings establish hydroxyl‐orchestrated crystallization and pocket‐site engineering as a powerful approach for multi‐component ion separations.

title: Rational Regulation of Ligand Conformation Toward Topology Reconfiguration for Sieving Butane Isomers
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving one‐step purification of n ‐C 4 H 10 and iso ‐C 4 H 10 from their isomeric mixtures with high efficiency and high purity is highly desirable yet extremely challenging, as it critically necessitates adsorbents that integrate size‐exclusive sieving functionality, high n ‐C 4 H 10 adsorption capacity, and fast adsorption kinetics. Herein, we synthesize a novel cage‐like anion‐pillared MOF adsorbent (SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu) through ligand‐conformation‐directed topology reconfiguration. Compared with the pillar‐layer prototype SIFSIX‐TEPE‐Cu, SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu exhibits a distinctive “confined window–expanded cavity” synergistic pore structure, with pore apertures strategically situated between the kinetic diameters of n ‐C 4 H 10 and iso ‐C 4 H 10 , thus enabling size‐exclusive molecular sieving. Furthermore, the large cages and 3D pore architecture confer both a high n ‐C 4 H 10 adsorption capacity (46.6 cm 3 /g) and a rapid adsorption rate (2.3 × 10 −12 m 2 s −1 ). Both kinetic analyses and DFT simulations provide mechanistic insights into the preferential adsorption and diffusion of n ‐C 4 H 10 . Dynamic breakthrough experiments demonstrate that SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu enables one‐step purification of both n ‐C 4 H 10 and iso ‐C 4 H 10 from their binary mixture under various conditions, such as high temperatures, high gas flow rates, and high humidities. After one separation cycle, 23.8 L kg −1 high‐purity iso ‐C 4 H 10 (>99.99%) and 27.8 L kg −1 n ‐C 4 H 10 (>99.0%) can be obtained, respectively.

title: Toward a Visible‐Range Helicity Filter: Panchromatic Magnetic Circular Dichroism via 4f‐Orbital‐Based Charge Transfer in a Cerium(IV) Complex
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD)‐based light‐helicity filters provide a material‐based approach to controlling the helicity of light. However, helicity control across the entire visible spectrum using a single molecular species has not yet been demonstrated. Herein, we report a tetravalent cerium (Ce(IV)) complex exhibiting panchromatic MCD properties originating from 4f‐orbital‐based ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) transitions. A Ce(IV) complex containing four electron‐donating anionic diethyldithiocarbamate ligands was synthesized. This complex exhibits panchromatic light absorption with both positive (520–780 nm) and negative (380–520 nm) MCD signals. Relativistic time‐dependent density functional theory (TD‐DFT) calculations reveal that this panchromatic light absorption originates from multiple LMCT transitions. The strong spin‐orbit coupling (SOC) associated with the Ce(IV) 4f orbitals facilitates the mixing of singlet and triplet LMCT excited states, enabling panchromatic light absorption. The 4f‐orbital‐based transition properties also contribute to effective MCD signals governed by the Faraday B ‐term. These findings highlight the potential of panchromatic MCD in a Ce(IV) complex as a promising approach toward the development of visible‐range light‐helicity filters.

title: Anion‐Anchoring, Anti‐Swelling Polymer Interphase Enables Durable Lithium Metal Anodes in Localized High‐Concentration Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Localized high‐concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) can improve the cycling stability of lithium metal batteries by promoting anion‐rich solvation structures that favor the formation of inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs). However, their favorable interfacial chemistry is not self‐sustaining because the native SEI is heterogeneous and prone to repeated rupture during Li plating/stripping, thus progressively depleting active Li and electrolyte. Polymeric artificial SEIs have emerged as a complementary strategy for interfacial stabilization, but their effectiveness in LHCEs is limited by an inherent conflict: the polar functional groups that coordinate ions also coordinate solvents, causing polymer swelling, dissolution, and disruption of anion‐rich solvation structures. Here, we develop an anion‐anchoring and anti‐swelling artificial SEI (AS–SEI) by integrating imidazolium cations with long aliphatic side chains. Imidazolium cations enable anion anchoring to sustain the LHCE‐favored anion‐rich environment at the interface, while long aliphatic chains provide anti‐swelling behavior that protects anchoring sites from competitive solvation. Consequently, AS‐SEI exhibits a high Young's modulus (5.0–10.5 GPa) and a high Li + transference number (0.94), while promoting the formation of LiF/Li 2 O‐rich SEIs. Li||Cu cells achieve 480 cycles with 99.5% average Coulombic efficiency, while Li||NCM811 cells deliver ∼900 cycles with 80% capacity retention (a nearly threefold improvement), with the strategy remaining effective across ether‐, ester‐, and sulfone‐based LHCEs.

title: Selective Gas‐Phase Photocatalytic Methane‐to‐Methanol Conversion Over Gallium Oxynitride With Molecular Oxygen as the Sole Oxidant
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective oxidation of methane to methanol using molecular oxygen remains challenging because methane activation is often accompanied by deep oxidation of the desired methanol product. Here we report a metal‐decorated, partially oxidized GaON/GaN photocatalyst for gas‐phase methane‐to‐methanol conversion using molecular oxygen as the oxidant. The optimized Ag/GaON/GaN catalyst delivers a methane oxidation rate of 2.6 mmol g − 1 h − 1 with ∼85% CH 4 ‐to‐CH 3 OH selectivity under O 2 . When untreated room air is used as the oxidant in a closed‐loop recirculating system, the catalyst maintains an activity of 1.0–1.3 mmol g − 1 h − 1 in a 50 h test, with comparable methanol selectivity. Complementary mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support a mechanism in which partial surface oxidation promotes O 2 activation, while residual surface –NH species may moderate the resulting reactive intermediates through local H‐transfer processes, thereby suppressing methanol overoxidation. These results highlight partially oxidized oxynitride surfaces as a promising platform for selective methane upgrading under gas‐phase photocatalytic conditions.

title: Interfacial State‐Perturbed Triplet Energy Transfer in Dye‐Sensitized Upconversion Nanoparticles for Early HIV Diagnosis
abstract: ABSTRACT Early diagnosis of HIV infection is pivotal for curbing AIDS progression and enabling timely therapeutic interventions. However, current immunoassays remain constrained by inadequate sensitivity for detecting trace levels of the HIV‐1 p24 antigen during the seroconversion window period. In this study, we discover that subtle perturbations in the interfacial binding state of a carboxylated near‐infrared dye, Cypate, on sub‐7 nm NaGdF 4 :Yb 3+ /Er 3+ upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) dramatically modulate triplet energy transfer (TET) efficiency, resulting in a remarkable upconversion luminescence (UCL) response with a signal‐to‐background ratio as high as 375. By leveraging this interfacial state‐perturbed TET as a signal transduction model, we further develop a TET‐sensitized UCL immunosorbent assay (TET‐ULISA) for HIV‐1 p24 antigen detection. In this platform, the target p24 triggers alkaline phosphatase (ALP) to generate phosphate ions, which competitively displace Cypate from the UCNP surface, disrupting TET and producing a dramatic UCL response. The resulting TET‐ULISA exhibits high sensitivity for p24 antigen with a limit of detection as low as 112 fg mL −1 , representing an 860‐fold improvement over the corresponding ALP‐based method by employing the identical immunoassay steps, thus enabling early HIV diagnosis within the critical serological window period.

title: Programmable Skeletal Editing of Pyridines Into Regiodefined N ‐Alkyl Pyrazoles
abstract: ABSTRACT N‐ Alkyl pyrazoles are common motifs in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, yet their preparation as single regioisomers is often hampered by poor regioselectivity in the direct alkylation of NH‐pyrazoles. Here we report a skeletal‐editing strategy that converts readily available pyridines into regiodefined N‐ alkyl pyrazoles through selective two‐carbon deletion. The N‐ substituent is installed before pyrazole formation and retained through amine‐mediated Zincke‐type ring opening, acid‐promoted cyclization, and retro‐Mannich extrusion of a two‐carbon enamine, fixing the pyrazole regiochemistry at the precursor stage. The sequence contracts the C 5 N pyridine framework into a C 3 N 2 pyrazole, transferring the ring nitrogen, three carbon atoms, and their substitution pattern directly onto the product. The method accommodates diverse pyridine scaffolds and N‐ alkyl groups and enables the skeletal remodeling of structurally complex molecules, transforming a problematic regioselective N‐ alkylation into a programmable precursor‐design strategy.

title: Overriding Polarity Mismatch in Radical Difunctionalization of 1,3‐Dienes
abstract: ABSTRACT The difunctionalization of conjugated dienes poses a significant challenge in controlling regio‐ and stereoselectivity due to the presence of two conjugated double bonds. Conventional radical addition reactions adhere to the polarity‐matching principle, wherein nucleophilic alkyl radicals preferentially attack the electrophilic C4 position of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes. Consequently, the polarity‐mismatched C1‐selective addition has remained unexplored. Herein, we report a three‐component 1,4‐dicarbofunctionalization of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes with α ‐aminoalkyl radicals and alkyl bromides via dual nickel/photoredox catalysis. This protocol overcomes the inherent polarity‐mismatching effect, achieving unprecedented C1‐selective addition with complete 1,4‐regioselectivity and excellent E ‐stereoselectivity. The reaction provides efficient access to structurally diverse β ‐amino acid derivatives, featuring broad substrate compatibility and promising utility in the derivatization of complex molecules. Combined mechanistic investigations and DFT calculations reveal that both radical addition and C–C reductive elimination govern the regio‐ and stereoselectivity. Notably, a significant hyperconjugative interaction between the forming C–C bond and the carbonyl group of the 1,3‐diene in the transition state plays a pivotal role in directing the radical addition to the polarity‐mismatched C1 position.

title: An Artificial Phosphoinositide Phosphatase Inhibiting Pyroptosis Cascade for Sepsis Treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT Sepsis mortality remains largely driven by dysregulated pyroptosis, where gasdermin D (GSDMD) pores release lethal cytokines via phosphoinositide (PIP)‐mediated membrane recruitment. To disrupt this process, we engineer terbium‐doped ceria nanoparticles (TCNs) with sublattice‐induced oxygen vacancies and optimized Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ ratios, functioning as artificial phosphatases that achieve > 20‐fold enhanced dephosphorylation activity against the model substrate ( para ‐nitrophenyl phosphate) versus pristine nanoparticles. Mechanistically, TCNs dephosphorylate PIPs at the plasma membrane, disrupting the canonical pyroptosis cascade by simultaneously interfering with inflammasome activation and the N‐terminal domain of GSDMD (GSDMD‐NT) oligomerization, ultimately inhibiting lytic pore formation. This pan‐ PIP dephosphorylation approach overcomes the limitations of natural phosphatases by enabling efficient lipid dephosphorylation and preventing GSDMD membrane localization. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrate that TCNs significantly reduce pro‐inflammatory cytokine release and improve survival rates in a murine model of endotoxemic sepsis. This work establishes nanoparticle‐mediated PIP modulation as a potential strategy for sepsis immunotherapy, rebalancing immune homeostasis through precision pyroptosis attenuation.

title: Photocatalytic PVDF Degradation Coupled With Catalytic Targeted Li Replenishment Toward Low‐Energy Repair of Spent LiFePO 4 Electrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Directly repair is recognized as a promising route for recycling spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP), but it is challenged by uneven Li supplementation and high energy input. Herein, we propose a photocatalytic strategy for PVDF degradation coupled with targeted Li replenishment toward low‐energy repair of spent LFP materials. Supported by theoretical analysis and in‐situ characterizations, TiO 2 can generate photogenerated electron–hole pairs synchronously under UV irradiation. The photogenerated holes promote the formation of •OH radicals, which abstract hydrogen atoms from the methylene units in PVDF, triggering the scission of polymer backbones and thus enabling the effective degradation of PVDF. Meanwhile, the photogenerated electrons accumulated on TiO 2 create a strong reductive microenvironment conducive to the reduction of Fe 3+ to Fe 2+ , which reduces the Li + migration barrier and facilitates lithium replenishment. The TiO 2 catalyst can incorporate into the material lattice as a favorable dopant to optimize the performances of as‐repaired LFP material. Specially, the repaired LFP material with 2.5 mol% TiO 2 delivers a high discharge capacity of 140.6 mAh g −1 at 1 C with 99.8% capacity retention ratio after 100 cycles. Even at a high rate of 5 C, it maintains 98.3% capacity retention ratio over 1500 cycles.

title: Boosting DMF Electrosynthesis Over Bifunctional NiCo Catalysts via Methanol‐Supplemented *CHO Supply
abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional industrial routes for N,N ‐dimethylformamide (DMF) synthesis typically require harsh conditions of high temperature and pressure, leading to high energy consumption and a large carbon footprint. Electrosynthesis of DMF has emerged as a sustainable alternative; however, this pathway still faces the challenges of low activity and poor selectivity. In this study, we present an efficient bifunctional NiCo electrocatalyst synthesized via the electrodeposition method. This catalyst achieves a DMF Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 56% with a production rate of 518 µmol cm −2 h −1 . Combined in situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that NiOOH and CoOOH species act as potent oxygen‐transfer mediators, facilitating N–H bond activation and dehydrogenation of dimethylamine (DMA). These species also promote C–N coupling between the *N(CH 3 ) 2 intermediate and *CHO intermediates derived from both methanol and the self‐decomposition of DMA. Furthermore, we find that the introduction of methanol provides a sufficient supply of *CHO intermediates, thereby further enhancing the selectivity of DMF synthesis compared with using DMA as the sole substrate. This work not only identifies the origin of the *CHO donor and its pivotal function in DMF electrosynthesis but also provides a foundation for designing multicomponent synergistic catalysts for advanced electrosynthesis.

title: Supramolecular Iron(II)‐Anchored Porphyrin Glycoassemblies Enable Galectin‐Targeted Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Photodynamic therapy (PDT) relies on photosensitizers that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon light irradiation to trigger cytotoxic effects in target tissues. Porphyrins are among the most widely used PDT photosensitizers due to their strong visible‐light absorption and efficient ROS generation, although their broad application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation, and limited selectivity. Here, Fe(II)‐anchored porphyrin nanocages displaying peripheral lactose residues were prepared by coordination‐driven subcomponent self‐assembly to combine photodynamic activity with multivalent glycan presentation. The resulting cubic Fe 8 L 6 architectures were characterized by NMR spectroscopy, UV–vis spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and transmission electron microscopy. The zinc‐metalated porphyrin nanoassembly, [ 1‐Zn ][BF 4 ] 16 , generated both singlet oxygen and superoxide upon red‐light irradiation, providing access to multiple ROS pathways. Isothermal titration calorimetry revealed high‐affinity binding to galectin‐3 ( K d = 2.65 ± 0.26 µM), a lectin commonly upregulated in epithelial cancers. A549 cells treated with [ 1‐Zn ][BF 4 ] 16 exhibited potent light‐induced cytotoxicity with negligible dark toxicity, with a phototoxicity index (PI) of 55, while pre‐treatment with lactose or thiodigalactose was protective against [ 1‐Zn ][BF 4 ] 16 toxicity. These results demonstrate that coordination‐driven self‐assembly provides an effective strategy for integrating multivalent lectin recognition and photodynamic activity within a single nanoscale architecture.

title: Single‐Vesicle Membrane Order‐Resolved Super‐Resolution Imaging Reveals Cholesterol Enrichment and Its Functional Role in Extracellular Vesicle Uptake
abstract: ABSTRACT Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are heterogeneous in membrane composition, yet conventional lipid analysis cannot resolve individual vesicles. Here we develop membrane order‐resolved, spectrally encoded super‐resolution imaging to simultaneously quantify membrane order and size at the single‐EV level. Combining Nile Red single‐molecule spectroscopy with localization microscopy achieves ∼30 nm resolution and reveals pronounced vesicle‐to‐vesicle heterogeneity. Using defined liposomes, cholesterol enrichment, and pharmacological inhibition, we establish membrane order as a sensitive surrogate for relative cholesterol content in individual EVs. Application to EVs from breast, gastric, and oral cell lines reveals cell‐type‐ and tissue‐dependent differences. Most cancer‐cell‐derived EVs show higher membrane order and higher inferred cholesterol than non‐tumor counterparts, although MDA‐MB‐231 EVs are an exception. Functional assays demonstrate that increasing EV membrane cholesterol enhances cellular uptake and shifts internalization from clathrin‐mediated to non‐clathrin‐mediated pathways. These findings identify cholesterol enrichment as a frequent feature of cancer‐cell‐derived EVs and link membrane composition to uptake efficiency and pathway selection. This work provides a single‐EV analytical platform and new insight into how membrane lipid heterogeneity regulates EV‐mediated intercellular communication.

title: Revealing Oxidation‐State‐Dependent Selectivity in Urea Electrosynthesis Over Stabilized Co/CoO x Surfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic upgrading of CO 2 and nitrogen wastes offers a sustainable route for urea synthesis, yet its selectivity is limited by competing parallel reactions and operando catalyst reconstruction. Here, using cobalt‐based model catalysts, we demonstrate that product partitioning among competing pathways can be selectively directed by metallic and oxidized cobalt phases. By introducing oxophilic Cr 3+ to retard cathodic over‐reduction of cobalt oxides, we stabilize a non‐equilibrium Co/CoO x surface under working conditions. The optimized Co@CoO x ‐Cr 1 catalyst achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency of 40.1 ± 1.1% and a yield rate of 102.27 ± 3.31 mmol h −1 g cat −1 under pressurized CO 2 at −0.3 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support a proposed oxidation‐state‐dependent relay mechanism in which metallic Co favors CO 2 ‐to‐*CO conversion, stabilized CoO x motifs may promote *NH 2 formation, and their interface is inferred to facilitate *CO─*NH 2 coupling for urea formation. This work identifies the controlled stabilization of coexisting phases with distinct oxidation states as a strategy for steering selectivity in multi‐reactant electrocatalysis.

title: Unlocking Intrinsic Narrowband Organic Ultralong Afterglow Through Efficient Two‐Photon Ionization
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic ultralong afterglow (OUA) materials are exclusively constrained by their reliance on host–guest exciplexes, which inherently suffer from spectral broadening and limited color tunability. Here we demonstrate an effective strategy to achieve narrowband OUA by harnessing localized excitons of guests through efficient two‐photon ionization (TPI). Through engineering multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) guests, we achieve full‐color narrowband OUA emissions with full width at half maximum (FWHM) as narrow as 30 nm and unprecedentedly long durations exceeding 44 hours, which are comparable to commercial inorganic afterglow materials. The rigid planar molecular architecture of MR‐TADF not only promotes TPI but also reinforces host–guest interactions, thus fostering efficient charge separation to boost OUA properties. The intrinsic OUA can also be achieved based on fluorophore and metal–organic complex guests with planar molecular skeletons. The resultant materials enable promising applications in spectrally pure emergency afterglow lighting and sophisticated afterglow organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). The afterglow OLEDs exhibit a maximum luminance of 26481 cd/m 2 , an external quantum efficiency of 8.7%, and record‐breaking ultralong electroluminescence afterglow lasting over 15 minutes. Our findings establish a valuable design principle for modulating charge migration and exciton transitions towards developing next‐generation OUA materials.

title: Built‐in Electric Field Modulating Interfacial Charge Dynamics in V 2 AlC‐Derived Magnetic‐Dielectric Heterostructures for Broadband Microwave Absorption
abstract: ABSTRACT The tailored design of magnetic‐dielectric heterostructures offers considerable potential for high‐performance electromagnetic wave absorption, yet achieving efficient interfacial charge separation remains challenging. Herein, we constructed VC/FeCoNi/Al 2 O 3 heterostructures with built‐in electric fields (BIEFs) via the topological structural transformation of V 2 AlC in Lewis acidic molten salts. This transformation involves the redox‐potential‐driven substitution by Fe/Co/Ni cations, leading to in situ alloying within the VC interlayers to balance the electromagnetic parameters. Theoretical calculations reveal that the work‐function difference drives directional interfacial charge redistribution, as evidenced by experimental observations of charge transfer and surface‐potential differences. This charge redistribution reconstructs the local electronic states, leading to interfacial orbital hybridization and establishing BIEFs at the heterointerfaces. Atomic vacancies and lattice distortions generated during etching, coupled with the BIEFs, enhance interfacial and defect‐induced polarization. Consequently, the optimized composite achieves a wide effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.72 GHz (at 1.7 mm) and a minimum reflection loss of −48.3 dB (at 2.8 mm). This BIEF‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy offers a viable route for designing high‐performance broadband microwave absorbers.

title: Molecular Crystal Phase Transformation via Nonclassical Pathways: Surfactant‐Based Kinetic Control of Metastable Amorphous Intermediates
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular crystals serve as essential components in a wide range of functional products, yet their performance is often compromised by unpredictable phase transformations, particularly in aqueous environments. Although nonclassical, multistage pathways are frequently proposed for such transitions, the specific role of transient intermediates remains poorly understood. Here, we employ in situ atomic force microscopy and high‐resolution transmission electron microscopy to elucidate a nonclassical transformation pathway in the model molecular crystal piroxicam that proceeds via metastable intermediates. These intermediates serve as amorphous precursors that undergo densification prior to crystallization, facilitating a rapid transition from the anhydrate to a less soluble hydrate phase. The onset and kinetics of this transformation are tunable through the use of cationic surfactants with varying alkyl‐chain lengths. Longer‐chain surfactants cooperatively adsorb onto both dissolving crystal facets and nanodroplets in solution, creating a dense interfacial barrier that delays precursor formation and subsequent crystallization. This work presents a strategy to manipulate phase transformation pathways in molecular crystals by targeting the metastable intermediates via tailored additive‐interface interactions, enabling the predictive design of advanced materials with controlled phase behavior and enhanced performance reliability.

title: Tailoring the Na + Transport Microenvironment With an Anion‐Capturing Interface Enables Low‐Temperature, Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Na + desolvation and diffusion across the solid‐electrolyte interface (SEI) are two bottlenecks to fast charging at low temperatures in hard‐carbon sodium‐ion batteries. Here, we design an anion‐capturing interface that provides a customized interfacial environment to enhance interfacial dynamics at low temperatures. We demonstrate that phosphate can promote the formation of a homogeneous inorganic SEI by inducing anion enrichment near the inner Helmholtz plane. The phosphorus‐rich interface exhibits multiple benefits, including the formation of a built‐in electric field and a reduced energy barrier for Na + interphase diffusion. The hard carbon–phosphate interface (NP‐HC) anode maintains a capacity of 183.6 mAh g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 (−30°C). The pouch cell utilizing the NP‐HC anode achieves a 90.2% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at a 2 C rate. Even so, NP‐HC pouch cells can operate stably even at temperatures as low as −40°C, indicating their potential to enhance the performance of sodium‐ion batteries under harsh conditions.

title: A General Strategy to Identify Impurity‐Activated Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Synthetic Triarylamines
abstract: ABSTRACT Distinguishing intrinsic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) from impurity‐derived emission remains challenging in organic luminescent materials, particularly when trace emissive species evade routine characterization. Herein, we establish a diagnostic framework for identifying impurity‐activated RTP in synthetic triarylamines through route‐, fraction‐, and purification‐dependent validation, impurity reconstitution, and theoretical analysis. Using TPA, TPAO, and related heteroatom‐engineered triarylamines as representative systems, we show that nominally identical samples can exhibit different RTP behaviors depending on synthetic history and purification extent, despite appearing chemically indistinguishable by conventional analyses. Progressive purification induces blue‐shifted and narrowed emissions and ultimately eliminates afterglow, revealing hidden emissive species. Structural analyses identify trace C–H arylation byproducts generated during metal‐catalyzed coupling reactions as a representative class of RTP‐active impurities. Reintroduction of independently synthesized impurity candidates into rigorously purified hosts restores phosphorescence, providing direct functional evidence that synthesis‐derived byproducts can activate RTP. Theoretical calculations further show that these impurities possess lower‐lying triplet states and act as triplet‐energy traps. Extension of the workflow to related synthetic triarylamines reproduces purification‐dependent RTP loss and impurity‐enabled recovery, supporting the applicability of this strategy across the triarylamine systems examined here and establishing synthetic history and purification as critical variables in assigning the origin of organic RTP.

title: Mechanochemically Accelerated Sharpless Asymmetric Dihydroxylation With Expanded Substrate Compatibility
abstract: ABSTRACT The Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation is an established transformation in organic synthesis for the preparation of chiral vicinal diols. However, conventional biphasic solution‐based conditions (typically water/ t‐ BuOH) require long reaction times (up to ∼48 h) and large amounts of solvent. Moreover, they often exhibit limited substrate scope due to low solubility of the substrates and functional‐group incompatibility. Herein, we report the first mechanochemical protocol for the Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation, which affords the desired diols with excellent enantioselectivity, comparable to that of conventional methods. Notably, most substrates are fully converted within 30 min without the need for large quantities of solvent. Moreover, the mechanochemical conditions enable efficient reactions of substrates that are challenging to convert under solution‐based conditions, including poorly soluble, base‐sensitive, and catalyst‐coordinating compounds. The practical utility of this protocol is further demonstrated by the efficient dihydroxylation of an intermediate of a natural product and a gram‐scale synthesis.

title: Electrochemical PVC Recycling Unlocks Efficient Ring‐Closure Toward Amine‐Bearing Ketene Acetals as Novel Monomers for Poly(Amino Ester) Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT A paired electrochemical synthetic strategy for the upcycling of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) is reported, enabling simultaneous cathodic dechlorination of the polymer backbone and anodic formation of cyclic halo acetals (CHAs) as monomer precursors. The process channels liberated chloride into cyclic acetal structures, which are converted into cyclic ketene acetals and subsequently polymerized via radical ring‐opening polymerization (rROP) to access degradable polyester and poly(amino ester) materials. Electrochemical cyclization unlocks the synthesis of previously unavailable nitrogen‐containing cyclic ketene acetal monomers in remarkably high yields. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal a pronounced heteroatom effect on cyclization efficiency, attributed to conformational preorganization induced by an increasing gauche effect upon ether and amide incorporation. A nitrogen‐containing ketene acetal monomer was polymerized and copolymerized with established ketene acetals, affording new functional, biodegradable polymer materials. Successful copolymerization with methyl acrylate demonstrates the incorporation of hydrolysable moieties into otherwise persistent olefinic materials. Importantly, cathodic PVC dechlorination proceeds independently of the anodic transformation, highlighting the broad applicability of this paired‐electrolysis strategy in an undivided cell. Overall, this work establishes a versatile electrochemical PVC recycling process while simultaneously generating previously inaccessible monomer building blocks for biodegradable polymer synthesis.

title: Hofmeister Engineering Enables High‐Voltage Aqueous All‐Organic Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous all‐organic batteries (AOBs) offer a safe and sustainable alternative for electrochemical energy storage, yet their energy density is constrained by the limited availability of organic redox couples with high‐working voltages. Here we develop a versatile redox couple by pairing a 3,4,9,10‐perylenetetracarboxylic diimide (PTCDI) anode with a quaternary‐ammonium bromine cathode, enabling an initial discharge voltage of up to 2.0 V through reversible two‐electron bromine conversion (Br − /Br 0 /Br + ). This battery chemistry is compatible with diverse charge carriers, including Li + , Na + , K + , NH 4 + , Ca 2+ , and Mg 2+ . We further reveal that electrolyte ions exert distinct effects on electrode reactions: Cations primarily regulate reaction kinetics, whereas anions govern both reversibility and kinetics through the Hofmeister effect. Kosmotropic anions suppress polybromide dissolution and improve reversibility, but retard electrode kinetics, while chaotropic anions facilitate reaction kinetics at the expense of active‐material retention. Guided by this mechanistic insight, a hybrid kosmotropic/chaotropic electrolyte balances these competing effects. The optimized one‐electron configuration retains 83.1% of its capacity after 12 000 cycles, while the two‐electron configuration delivers an energy density of approximately 107 Wh kg −1 based on the combined electrode active‐material mass. High areal capacities exceeding 4 mAh cm −2 further demonstrate its practical potential. This work establishes electrolyte solvation engineering as an effective strategy for high‐energy AOBs.

title: MitoDART: Mitochondria‐Targeted Intracellular DNA Assembly for Selective Mitochondrial Interference and Early Molecular Response Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT Rational modulation of mitochondrial functions to reprogram cellular behavior and fate has emerged as a promising therapeutic paradigm. However, it is still challenging to achieve cell‐selective mitochondrial interference with in situ monitoring of early molecular responses. In this study, we report a mito chondria‐targeted dual‐biomarker‐activated intracellular D NA a ssembly for mitochondrial r egulation and t racking (Mito‐DART), which enables cell‐selective interference of mitochondria and in situ biosensing for early assessment of molecular responses. Based on the AND logic responsive to two tumor biomarkers, apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) and microRNAs, Mito‐DART is specifically activated in tumor cells and undergoes hybridization chain reaction (HCR)‐driven DNA assembly, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis‐associated cellular responses. More importantly, Mito‐DART enables in situ monitoring of cytochrome c (Cyt c) release, an early molecular marker of mitochondria‐mediated apoptosis, within 1 h following mitochondrial disruption, providing an early molecular readout of mitochondria‐mediated apoptotic signaling that complements conventional tissue‐level endpoint assessments. Overall, this design provides a programmable framework for biomarker‐gated mitochondrial intervention that combines selective activation with built‐in assessment of downstream molecular responses.

title: Novel Fluorinated Amino‐Ester Electrolyte With Host–Guest Solvation Enables High‐Voltage and Thermally Safe Lithium–Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–metal batteries (LMBs) face critical bottlenecks to high energy density, long cycle life, and thermal safety, mainly due to insufficient oxidation stability and thermal tolerance of solvation structures in conventional carbonate/ether electrolytes. In this work, we develop a host–guest solvation structure via a molecular fluorination strategy based on a tertiary amine‐ester scaffold functionalized with trifluoroethyl (CF 3 CH 2 ─) and hexafluoroisopropyl ((CF 3 ) 2 CH─) groups, affording two fluorinated solvents: N, N‐dimethylcarbamate trifluoroethyl (TFE) and N,N‐dimethylcarbamate hexafluoroisopropyl (HFS). The distinct polarity contrast between TFE and HFS delivers functional complementarity: TFE, with strong Lewis basicity, promotes lithium‐salt dissociation, while highly fluorinated HFS, with weak solvation ability, accelerates interfacial reduction kinetics through a delocalized charge‐transfer mechanism, forming a LiF/Li 2 O‐rich nanocrystalline solid electrolyte interphase. Consequently, in Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 configurations, the as‐designed electrolyte enables a 10 Ah pouch cell to stably cycle over 260 cycles with 95.2% capacity retention, and a 4.5 V‐charged 22.4 Ah pouch cell delivers an initial energy density of 550 Wh kg −1 . The pouch cell also survives nail penetration and exhibits significantly delayed thermal runaway. This amino‐ester molecular design offers key insights for developing high‐energy, safe LMBs toward practical industrial applications.

title: Hole Mobility Synchronizes Carbon Oxidation and Nitrate Reduction to Switch Photocatalytic Selectivity between Ammonia and Urea
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic conversion of nitrate and renewable carbon feedstocks offers a sustainable route to nitrogen chemicals but remains constrained by mismatched oxidation–reduction kinetics and inefficient C–N coupling. Here, we identify hole mobility as a decisive kinetic regulator that governs nitrate photoreduction selectivity by synchronizing carbon activation and nitrogen reduction pathways. By introducing cadmium vacancies into single‐atom Cu‐anchored CdS, we substantially reduce effective hole mass and accelerate hole transport, enabling oxidative C–C cleavage of biomass‐derived oxalic‐acid to generate reactive *COOH. Concurrently, hole mobility‐induced electron localization at Cu stabilizes nitrate‐derived *NH 2 , promoting selective *NH 2 ‐*COOH coupling while suppressing deep protonation to ammonia. Accordingly, Cu/CdS‐V Cd achieves a record urea yield of 1024 µmol g −1 h −1 with >99% selectivity, approximately fourteen times higher than state‐of‐the‐art nitrate‐based photocatalysts. In contrast, vacancy‐free Cu/CdS with low hole mobility fails to activate carbon feedstock and instead produces ammonia with >99% selectivity. In‐situ spectroscopy and density functional theory reveal that enhanced hole mobility accelerates oxalic‐acid oxidation, strengthens *NH 2 adsorption, and lowers the free‐energy barrier for C–N coupling to enable selective urea formation. These findings establish charge‐carrier mobility, rather than isolated active‐site activity, as a governing principle for artificial photosynthesis, offering a general strategy for selective multi‐reactant photocatalytic transformations.

title: Pulse‐Programmable Electrostatic Memory Using Ultrathin Hexagonal Boron Nitride
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐volatile memory elements that enable multifunctionality and seamless integration with emerging quantum materials are of increasing interest for next‐generation electronic systems. In van der Waals heterostructures, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is widely employed as an inert substrate, encapsulation layer, and gate dielectric. Here we show that ultrathin (∼1.2 nm) hBN can also function as an active, pulse‐programmable electrostatic medium, enabling non‐volatile resistive memory with tunable resistance states in a multi‐terminal device architecture without dedicated gate or floating‐gate elements. Under millisecond current pulses, devices exhibit robust polarity‐dependent hysteresis in both transverse and longitudinal resistance, with programmed states exhibiting long retention times up to room temperature. The switching amplitude is strongly enhanced near the charge‐neutrality regime and vanishes in control devices without hBN, establishing ultrathin hBN as the essential functional element. We attribute this behavior to field‐assisted charge injection and trapping in hBN and near its interfaces, generating metastable electret‐like states that modify the local electrostatic potential landscape and thereby reconfigure electronic transport in the underlying channel. Our results identify few‐layer hBN as an active dielectric platform for non‐volatile memory and reveal a route toward electrostatically programmable transport functionalities in van der Waals systems.

title: Mitochondrial profiling links tumor genotype to metabolic and immune vulnerabilities in liver cancer
abstract: Although oncogenic alterations influence tumor metabolism, how they impose distinct metabolic programs within a shared tissue remains poorly defined. We developed mitochondrial profiling platforms comparing metabolites and proteins in primary liver cancer (PLC) models. Analysis of six PLCs revealed that mitochondrial metabolism is dictated by oncogene identity. Kras-driven tumors required creatine metabolism to buffer energy, whereas c-MYC-driven tumors relied on oxidative phosphorylation. Among c-MYC-driven PLCs, Pten-deficient tumors accumulated mitochondrial phosphoethanolamine, a precursor of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE). Inhibition of PE synthesis selectively impaired Pten-deficient tumor growth and extended survival, partly through CD8+ T cell infiltration and sensitization to tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-mediated cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, PE depletion increased the level of surface TNF receptors, promoting proinflammatory responses. These findings uncover genotype-specific metabolic liabilities and establish PE synthesis as a mechanism of immune evasion in PLC.

title: A new growth curve
An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude ( M w ) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four M w 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

title: A tryptophan cation radical determines radical transfer kinetics and catalytic rate in a ribonucleotide reductase
abstract: Ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) is the sole enzyme responsible for de novo deoxynucleotide synthesis for DNA replication and repair. In the Escherichia coli class Ia RNR, a radical must traverse 32 angstroms along a pathway composed of amino acids spanning β and α subunits to complete each turnover. By incorporating unnatural amino acids to alter reduction potentials of pathway tyrosine residues, we (i) perturb the rates of radical transfer and show that they match the rates of deoxynucleotide production and (ii) directly observe a tryptophan cation radical (W 48 + •) as a kinetically competent pathway intermediate. Together, these results establish that radical transfer through W 48 in α 2 β 2 is the rate-limiting process, which controls the enzymatic activity of E. coli RNR.

title: Science and the arts: Partners in crime
Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

abstract: Small earthquakes [i.e., those of magnitude ( M ) M 2 earthquake within a swarm sequence in California’s Brawley Seismic Zone. Inverting fiber-derived apparent source time functions revealed two distinct rupture episodes separated by 42 milliseconds, reflecting rupture arrest followed by dynamic renucleation. Analysis of a 3-hour sequence showed adjacent, largely nonoverlapping fault patches activated in succession, forming complementary slip partitioning. These fragmented failure patterns within the M 2 rupture and its sequence limited rupture growth, consistent with the absence of a dominant mainshock. Microearthquakes, which are now accessible by fiber-optic sensing, provide direct constraints on fault mechanics across scales bridging laboratory experiments and large earthquakes.

title: Rebuilding science’s social contract with the public
abstract: Much has been written about how the social contract between science and society in the United States is in crisis. According to its terms, research will yield broad economic, health, and security benefits to the very public that funds it. But this relationship depends on public trust in science, its systems, and the scientists themselves, and therein lies the problem. Beyond making discoveries and publishing results, scientists shape their own culture, and that is where some changes may be the key to rebuilding public trust.

Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity
abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)–mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

title: Nutritional interventions’ impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings
abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B vitamins, whereas macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

title: Moving beyond hyperscale ambitions for AI infrastructure in Africa
Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth
abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

title: Covalent–Ionic Bonding Regulation Enables Chemo‐Mechanical Stabilization of High‐Voltage O3‐Type Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Ni–Fe–Mn‐based O3‐type layered oxides are attractive cathode materials for sodium‐ion batteries, but their high‐voltage operation suffers from the coupling between phase transitions and lattice oxygen instability. In this work, guided by hard and soft acids and bases (HSAB) theory, we propose a covalent–ionic dual‐pathway decoupling strategy to stabilize high‐voltage O3‐type layered cathodes. The incorporation of Mg, Ti, and F constructs a rigid architecture in which a covalent Ti─O framework reinforces the transition‐metal octahedral skeleton to suppress detrimental phase transitions, while localized Mg─F ionic coordination stabilizes lattice oxygen through localized electrostatic anchoring to mitigate irreversible oxygen release. Through multiscale structural and spectroscopic analyses, we verify that this bonding regulation suppresses the O3→P3→OP2 multiphase evolution and lattice oxygen escape. The modified cathode maintains 76.32% capacity retention over 400 cycles at 1 C and exhibits robust cyclability across −10°C to 50°C; the assembled full cells achieve a reversible capacity of 166.27 mAh g −1 with an energy density of 330.22 Wh kg −1 at 0.1 C, and an initial capacity of 143.74 mAh g −1 with 72.06% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C. This work demonstrates a bonding‐regulation paradigm that decouples chemo‐mechanical degradation in high‐energy‐density layered oxide cathodes.

title: Synergistic Water‐Deficient Inner Helmholtz Plane and Asymmetric Dual‐Site Nonmetal Catalysts Enable Stable Ah‐Level Aqueous Zn–I2 Batteries at Elevated Temperatures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT At elevated temperatures, intensified water‐induced side reactions and iodine dissolution severely hinder the development of aqueous zinc–iodine batteries. Herein, a marginally hydrophilic and conductive modification layer with a hexagonal layered structure is constructed to stabilize the anode interface. This approach establishes a water‐deficient inner Helmholtz plane and reduces the fraction of weak hydrogen bonds, thereby suppressing spontaneous Zn dissolution and water decomposition. Concurrently, interfacial electronic structure regulation increases the energy barrier for the hydrogen evolution reaction and promotes uniform Zn deposition along the Zn‐(002) crystal plane, effectively inhibiting dendrite growth. These effects are corroborated by theoretical calculations and in situ characterizations. Furthermore, asymmetric dual‐site nonmetal single‐atom–cluster structures are introduced into the cathode host to enhance iodine adsorption and accelerate conversion kinetics, thereby mitigating iodine dissolution. Benefiting from this synergistic design, the assembled coin‐type battery delivers a discharge capacity of 95 mAh g −1 after 60 000 cycles at 8 A g −1 . A sub‐ampere‐hour‐level plastic‐cased battery employing a high‐loading cathode with a theoretical areal‐capacity of 5.6 mAh cm −2 further demonstrates strong practical potential by maintaining excellent cycling stability at 3 C and at 50°C. An Ah‐level pouch battery also exhibits stable operation at 50°C.

title: Interface Engineering to Unlock Multi‐Electron Sn+/S2− Redox Reaction and High Lithium Anode Utilization
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs) offer high theoretical energy density, yet their practical viability is impeded by sluggish cathodic redox kinetics and uncontrolled anodic dendrite growth. Here, we address these challenges by a dual‐interface engineering strategy that exploits halogen anion migration to in situ construct phase‐separated localized electrochemical microreactors (LEMRs) at both electrodes. At the cathode, an in situ‐formed Li 6 PS 5 Cl/LiCl/Li 2 S‐LiI internal LEMR activates the S 2− /S n+ ( n ≥1) multi‐electron redox reaction beyond the conventional S 2− /S 0 redox reaction while maintaining structural integrity. Concurrently, at the Li anode, an interfacial LiCl/C@LiI/LiCl‐LiI anode LEMR confines Li plating/stripping within the LEMR to suppress lithium dendrites. This dual‐LEMR architecture enables the optimized cells to deliver a capacity retention of 86.3% after 450 cycles at 3.6 mAh cm −2 and 80% after 70 cycles at a high areal capacity of 7.5 mAh cm −2 under a low N/P ratio of 0.78, and to achieve an ultra‐high areal capacity of 32.8 mAh cm −2 . This work highlights the potential of anion chemistry as an effective interface engineering strategy to overcome the kinetics and stability limits of all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, and provides a versatile framework for advancing high‐energy ASSLSBs.

title: Antigen‐Presenting Microrobots Program CAR‐T Cell Function
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical forces are emerging as key regulators of T‐cell function, yet how active motion‐ derived mechanical cues from artificial antigen‐presenting cells (aAPCs) influence T‐cell activation and fate remains largely unexplored. Here, we develop self‐propelled antigen‐presenting microrobots (CytoBots)—gas‐driven magnesium microparticles functionalized with anti‐CD3 and anti‐CD28 antibodies—that actively navigate suspension environments and mechanically engage T cells. Unlike immotile aAPCs, CytoBots generate motion‐dependent, force‐bearing stimulation that enhances T‐cell activation. Single‐cell force spectroscopy shows that CytoBots double receptor–ligand binding strength and extend bond lifetime threefold, supporting a role for motion‐enhanced mechanical interactions in T‐cell activation. CytoBot stimulation is associated with enhanced proximal T‐cell signaling, increased phosphorylation of AKT and mTOR, and metabolic changes characterized by elevated mitochondrial respiration and glycolysis‐associated activity. These responses accompany the enrichment of stem‐like and central memory T‐cell populations. In humanized tumor models, CytoBot‐expanded CAR‐T cells exhibit superior cytotoxicity, persistence, and antitumor efficacy. These findings establish microrobotic antigen‐presenting interfaces as a generalizable strategy for programming immune cell function through dynamic mechanotransduction, opening new opportunities for next‐generation cell therapies.

Observability and Parameter Estimation of a Generic Model for Aggregated Distributed Energy Resources
abstract: We propose a novel framework for estimating the parameters of an aggregated distributed energy resources (DER A) model. First, we introduce a rigorous method to determine whether all model parameters are estimable. When they are not, our approach identifies the subset of parameters that can be estimated. The proposed framework offers new insights into the number and specific parameters that can be reliably estimated based on commonly available measurements. It also highlights the limitations of calibrating such models. Second, we introduce a Kalman filtering method to calibrate the DER A model. Since we account for nonlinear effects such as saturation and deadbands, we develop a specific mechanism to handle smoothing functions within the Kalman filter. Specifically, we consider the extended and the unscented Kalman filter. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework on a modified IEEE 34-node distribution feeder with inverter- based resources. Our findings align with the North American Electric Reliability Corporation's parameterization guideline and underscore the importance of model calibration in accurately capturing the collective dynamics of distributed energy resources installed on distribution systems.
